postings.text: Senior MEAL Manager | IRC - International Rescue Committee Skip to main content Senior MEAL Manager IRC - International Rescue Committee Cox's Bazaar International Senior level Speaks English Application deadline: October 31, 2027 (12 months) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Senior MEAL Manager at the International Rescue Committee (IRC) will lead all Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) work for a consortium focused on humanitarian crises. This role involves designing and maintaining the MEAL framework, ensuring data quality, and building the MEAL capacity of partner organizations. The manager will oversee data collection, analysis, and reporting, while also ensuring compliance with donor requirements. The position requires strong leadership and collaboration skills to effectively manage multi-partner programs and promote learning and adaptive management. Candidate Requirements: Minimum 7 years of MEAL experience in humanitarian and development settings At least 3 years in senior or lead roles managing MEAL systems Experience with DFAT or comparable institutional donor requirements Experience in protection, health, WASH, education, GBV, livelihoods Experience leading baselines, surveys, evaluations, and research studies Advanced skills in Excel, Power BI, SPSS, Kobo, and CommCare Strong quantitative and qualitative analysis skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Bangla Master’s degree preferred in relevant field or bachelor’s degree with relevant experience The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Program Brief The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solution driven, passionate changemaker, come join us positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future. Since 2017, IRC has supported Rohingya Refugees and Bangladeshi nationalities communities in Cox's Bazar, Khulna, Barisal, and Chittagong with integrated services. The organization also addresses climate change impacts by building resilience and promoting economic recovery, education, and protection. Purpose of the role: The Senior MEAL Manager leads all MEAL work for the consortium. This is a full-time, hands-on role in the Program Management Unit (PMU), which manages day-to-day delivery of the project. In this role, the post holder will: Set the MEAL framework and standards for the whole consortium. Collect, check and combine indicator data from IRC and all Bangladeshi Partners. Make sure DFAT-funded results are clearly attributed and that each client is counted only once. Build the MEAL skills of partner organizations. Partners differ widely in capacity and resources, so the role works with a good degree of independence day to day. The aim is high-quality results, not just compliance. The post holder is supported by the Assessment and Learning (A&L) Manager, the Management Information System (MIS) Manager and IRC sector MEAL Managers and receives technical oversight from the Head of MEAL & Program Quality. Work Location: IRC Bangladesh, Cox’s Bazar Office Contract Length: 31st October 2027 (with possibility of extension subject to funding, program needs and performance of incumbent) Major Responsibilities: Consortium MEAL framework and strategic ownership: Design, maintain and regularly update the consortium-wide MEAL framework and MEAL Plan, including the Program Logic, log frame, MEL framework, Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS) and Indicator Tracking Table (ITT), in line with DFAT’s Design, Monitoring and Evaluation Standards (February 2026) and Development Evaluation Policy (2026), IRC MEAL policies and IRC’s global strategy, Strategy100. Ensure the framework, MEAL Plan, PIRS and standardized tools are approved and used by all partners. Own the consortium’s MEAL standard and practice. Contextualize existing IRC tools, standards and MEAL systems for the consortium rather than building parallel systems. Lead the standard MEAL methods, tools and reporting system, and strengthen partners’ capacity to use them. Agree with all partners how each indicator is defined and calculated, what data is collected, which tools are used, how often and with what sampling, and who is responsible. Ensure every partner applies the same definitions and protocols and understands the PIRS. Lead the annual Program Logic review and monitoring of key assumptions and risks with partners and contribute monitoring evidence to the consortium risk register. Data collection, consolidation, analysis and reporting: Collect, clean, validate, analyze and compile project data for all indicators across IRC and all Bangladeshi Partners, for both monitoring and reporting. Ensure all partners collect data using CommCare-based tools and upload it daily to one central server and check the data routinely on dashboards. Maintain one common ITT for all partners (used for annual reporting) and analyze CommCare MIS data and the Program Indicator Dashboard (PID) monthly to assess progress and identify priority areas for targeted monitoring. Update the ITT and performance dashboards every month. Ensure data is consistently broken down by sex, age, gender, disability and location on every record (using the Washington Group Short Set on Functioning to identify persons with disabilities), and clear attribution of DFAT-funded results through project-specific codes in the MIS, addressing any attribution gaps through agreed data-sharing protocols and monthly data quality reviews. Apply DFAT’s unique client counting approach across all partners, using the program-specific client identifier in CommCare to count each individual once at service, sector and program level, and report unique reach against the target of 210,841 individuals by sector, sex, age, gender and disability. Ensure program data reported to DFAT is accurate, complete and donor compliant. Set and enforce common data management rules for all partners, covering file naming, storage, version control and data sharing. Ensure sensitive GBV and child protection case data remain within GBVIMS+ and CPIMS+ and agreed information-sharing protocols, with only aggregated, anonymized data used in consortium and DFAT reporting. Run routine consortium-wide analysis to identify programmatic, geographic, thematic and capacity gaps, including gaps in reaching the most at-risk groups (women and girls, children, adolescents and persons with disabilities) in line with JRP Priority 1 criteria, and flag them promptly to the PMU, outside the regular reporting cycle were urgent. Develop and monitor Value for Money (VfM) indicators aligned with DFAT’s 4Es framework (economy, efficiency, effectiveness and equity), including cost per client, cost per output and service utilization rates, working with Finance and sector leads and comparing results across delivery models and against sector benchmarks, and review the results with partners at program performance reviews. Prepare quarterly narrative and monitoring reports in consortium-agreed formats, and the MEAL inputs for DFAT annual performance reporting (led by the Program Coordinator, in the 8+3 format and aligned with DFAT’s whole-of-program indicators), with dashboards developed together with the MIS Manager. Submit reports on time and provide the DFAT inputs on schedule. Routine and process monitoring: Lead a standardized process monitoring approach with tools and checklists for health and nutrition, protection, child protection and GBV, WASH, education, livelihoods, and emergency preparedness and response, covering quality, whether services are delivered as designed, inclusiveness, timeliness and the functioning of cross-sectoral referral pathways, with safeguarding, AAP and GEDSI built in. Monitor service quality, continuity, client access and satisfaction during the phased transition of services to Bangladeshi Partners, in line with the Partner Capacity building and Handover Plan, and report findings and corrective actions to the PMU and DFAT. Select activities for monthly spot checks based on MIS analysis (geographic coverage, program component, data quality performance and risk), and conduct spot checks with partner MEAL staff using digital tools. Plan and lead joint field visits with sector teams and partners, so that teams learn from one another (proposed monthly, and a longer 2–3 day visit each quarter covering all partners’ project areas). Review monitoring findings monthly with sector leads, and present consolidated findings at quarterly Program Performance Review and Reflection meetings, tracking agreed corrective actions to completion. Data quality assurance: Check the quality of partner-reported data by verifying it, applying validation rules, cleaning it with a clear record of changes, and giving partners feedback. Lead annual Data Quality Assessments (DQAs) using IRC’s DQA methodology, adapted to DFAT’s Design, Monitoring and Evaluation Standards, and ensure at least 10% of reported data is verified against source documents each quarter during field visits. Lead on-site data verification and routine spot checks of CommCare records against registers, attendance sheets and case files (verifying sensitive GBV and child protection records only through agreed confidential protocols). Follow up DQA findings with agreed corrective actions and track them to completion and ensure compliance with IRC’s Data Quality Management Framework. Baseline, surveys, evaluations and research: Use the baseline survey (completed in November 2026) as the benchmark for tracking change and refining targets, lead the internally managed outcome surveys (including the Year 2 midline) in line with the PIRS collection frequencies, coordinate the independent external endline survey in Year 3, and provide technical coordination of the Joint Program Review at around Month 18 (including the evaluation questions, validation workshop and joint action-planning workshop). Deliver all survey, review and evaluation activities on schedule. Develop Terms of Reference, methodologies, sampling plans (95% confidence level, 5% margin of error), tools and analysis plans, and oversee enumerators (IRC-enrolled incentive workers) and partner field supervisors, including daily data checks through dashboards, and ensure enumerators are trained in research ethics, safeguarding, PSEA, informed consent and sensitive-topic data collection. Prepare the Scope of Work in consultation with DFAT and share it before the evaluation team is recruited; procure and manage the independent final evaluation to DFAT’s quality and ethical standards and coordinate the management response and action plan and the learning workshop. postings.text: Programme Policy Officer – School Feeding Literacy & Technical Assistance | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content Programme Policy Officer – School Feeding Literacy & Technical Assistance WFP - World Food Programme Phnom Penh National SB-4 (SC8/SC9), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement level Speaks English Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (12 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Food Programme (WFP) is seeking a Programme Policy Officer for School Feeding Literacy & Technical Assistance in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. This role involves supporting the implementation of literacy activities in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport, focusing on improving learning outcomes for primary school children. The officer will coordinate with various stakeholders, provide technical support, and contribute to capacity-building initiatives. The position requires frequent travel and engagement with government institutions to ensure effective program delivery and compliance. Candidate Requirements: At least 3 years of experience in literacy or education programs Experience in designing and implementing literacy interventions Proven experience working with government institutions Strong understanding of government systems and policy development Experience in project management and donor compliance Fluency in English and Khmer DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 24 November 2026-23:59-GMT+07:00 Indochina Time (Phnom Penh) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). This vacancy announcement is open to Cambodian nationals only. POSITION TITLE: Programme Policy Officer – School Feeding Literacy & Technical Assistance TYPE OF CONTRACT: WFP Service Contract GRADE:  SC8 UNIT/DIVISION: School Feeding Programme DUTY STATION:  Phnom Penh, Cambodia DURATION: As soon as possible for 12 months (There is no expectation of contract extension upon completion of the literacy project tasks) REPORTING LINE:  This position reports to the Programme Policy Officer – School Feeding Technical Assistance Lead The incumbent will be based at the WFP Cambodia Country Office in Phnom Penh , with frequent travel to and regular engagement with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport and other government institutions as required. The position will work closely with government counterparts, particularly the Primary Education Department (PED), to support the implementation of USDA McGovern-Dole FY26 literacy activities and broader school feeding technical assistance priorities. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF ASSIGNMENT: Central to its Cambodia programme, WFP has been working with the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) to implement school feeding since 1999 through the provision of hot, nutritious meals in schools and cash/food scholarships to vulnerable primary and pre-primary school children. From 1999 to 2022, this social assistance programme has benefited over two million school children with much work already done to transition school feeding to a nationally managed and funded programme. The programme currently reaches over 300,000 children in Cambodia and has an increasing focus on supporting the scale up of the government’s school feeding programme. The upcoming USDA McGovern-Dole (MGD) FY26 Programme includes a significant literacy component aimed at improving learning outcomes through the development, piloting, and rollout of an upper-grade (4-6) literacy package and task-based package for grade 1-3 in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS), particularly the Primary Education Department (PED). As this intervention represents a new area of support under the programme, with no existing national framework or dedicated external technical partner leading implementation, substantial technical, operational, and coordination support will be required to ensure successful design, rollout, monitoring, and donor compliance. Beyond literacy, the position will also contribute to broader school feeding technical assistance priorities under the National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme (NHGSFP), working closely with the WFP School Feeding Secondment Officer embedded within MoEYS, the School Feeding Technical Assistance team, and relevant government stakeholders. The role will support cross-sectoral coordination and implementation of key milestones under the School Feeding Policy Action Plan (PAP) and USDA McGovern-Dole FY26 program. ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: Support and coordinate with the Primary Education Department (PED) in the development, adaptation, pilot testing, rollout, and institutionalization of upper-grade literacy interventions, including task-based literacy approaches, Om Nan PTOM, PTOM, instructional packages, reading manuals, assessment tools, and learning materials aligned with national priorities and the Global Proficiency Framework. Serve as WFP’s focal point for coordination with MoEYS, PED, NGOs and other relevant stakeholders, providing technical and project management support for literacy-related activities, including work planning, implementation monitoring, risk management, partner coordination, and tracking of programme deliverables to ensure timely implementation and donor compliance. Support the design and delivery of capacity-strengthening initiatives for master trainers, teachers, school leaders, and education officials, including training, mentoring, coaching, and follow-up support to strengthen literacy instruction and effective classroom implementation. Support the monitoring, evaluation, learning, and reporting of literacy interventions, including data collection and analysis, documentation of lessons learned and evidence, quality assurance, and the development, production, and dissemination of teaching and learning materials to inform programme improvement and policy uptake. Conduct research, evidence gathering, analysis, and knowledge management activities to inform literacy programme design, adaptation, scaling, and sustainability. Contribute to the preparation and quality assurance of technical reports, workplans, briefing materials, donor updates, presentations, visibility materials, and other programme documentation related to literacy and technical assistance activities. Serve as a key focal point for inter-ministerial coordination, facilitating collaboration between MoEYS and other relevant government institutions, as well as development partners and technical stakeholders, to strengthen policy coherence, implementation, and problem-solving. Apply in-depth knowledge of government systems and institutional processes to support stakeholder engagement, partnership development, and resource mobilization efforts that contribute to improved education outcomes and human capital development. OTHER SPECIFIC JOB REQUIREMENTS:   Support MoEYS PED in the development, validation, adaptation, piloting, rollout, and institutionalization of upper-grade (4-6) literacy packages, support early grade literacy (1-3), teacher support materials, and related learning interventions under the USDA McGovern-Dole FY26 program. Coordinate closely with relevant MoEYS departments, Provincial Offices of Education, Teacher Training Institutions, and development partners to ensure alignment, ownership, and sustainability of literacy interventions. Coordinate with School Feeding and field office team to share the knowledge of literacy and progress to keep track the progress and achievement workstream as required by donor. Support capacity strengthening activities for government stakeholders, teachers, school personnel, and education actors through training, workshops, coaching, technical exchanges, and learning events related to literacy programming. Facilitate inter-ministerial coordination and follow-up for the implementation of priority activities and broader Technical Assistance milestones under the School Feeding Policy Action Plan (PAP) 2024-2035, working closely with the WFP School Feeding Secondment Officer and School Feeding Technical Assistance Lead to strengthen collaboration across education, nutrition, social protection, agriculture, and other relevant sectors. Contribute to the design, implementation, documentation, and dissemination of technical pilots, innovations, and evidence-generation activities linked to literacy, education, school feeding, and human capital development. Contribute to Cambodia's engagement with regional and global initiatives, technical networks, and communities of practice relevant to literacy, education, school feeding, and human capital development. Provide support to WFP Technical Assistances activities where relevant to support the National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme. Build and maintain effective working relationships with government counterparts, UN agencies, NGOs, academia, research institutions, and development partners to support programme implementation, coordination, learning, and policy dialogue. Ensure gender equality, disability inclusion, protection, environmental considerations, and accountability to affected populations (AAP) are integrated into all aspects of programme design and implementation. Support documentation of lessons learned best practices, implementation experiences, and policy recommendations to inform programme improvements and future scale-up. Perform other duties as required. DESIRED EXPERIENCES FOR ENTRY INTO THE ROLE:   At least 3 years of professional experience in literacy, education, reading improvement, foundational learning, teacher development, or related education programmes. Demonstrated experience supporting the design, implementation, monitoring, and scale-up of literacy interventions, including the development of learning materials, teacher support tools, training programmes, and evidence-based approaches to improve learning outcomes. Proven experience working with government institutions, preferably within or in close partnership with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries

postings.text: Quantitative Researcher, Education & Employment (Remote Eligible) at Mathematica - PurposePhil Career Info Close Jobs search Quantitative Researcher, Education & Employment (Remote Eligible) Mathematica • Full-time • Remote (United States) • $100k - $135k / year • 2d ago Job available in these locations: United States Ann Arbor, MI, United States Cambridge, MA, United States Chicago, IL, United States Princeton, NJ, United States Washington, DC, United States About Mathematica: Mathematica applies expertise at the intersection of data, methods, policy, and practice to improve well-being around the world. We collaborate closely with public- and private-sector partners to translate big questions into deep insights that improve programs, refine strategies, and enhance understanding using data science and analytics. Our work yields actionable information to guide decisions in wide-ranging policy areas, from health, education, early childhood, and family support to nutrition, employment, disability, and international development. Mathematica offers our employees competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, as well as the advantages of being 100 percent employee owned. As an employee stock owner, you will experience financial benefits of ESOP holdings that have increased in tandem with the company’s growth and financial strength. You will also be part of an independent, employee-owned firm that is able to define and further our mission, enhance our quality and accountability, and steadily grow our financial strength. Read more about our benefits here: Benefits at a Glance . Primary Duties and Responsibilities: We are looking for a quantitative researcher to join our division to support rigorous, data-driven, evidence-building activities. Our researchers support ongoing project teams in the planning and execution of projects for clients such as: The U.S. Departments of Education and Labor, National Science Foundation, philanthropic organizations such as the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, and numerous state and local agencies. Mathematica is seeking a researcher with specific expertise in quantitative research methods, causal inference, and social policy research, who will conduct studies and support program improvement and evaluation in the areas of employment and education. The following projects illustrate the type of work we currently have under way. Designing a quasi-experimental analysis to estimate the returns to postsecondary education relative to a high school diploma and examine variation across institution type and programs Applying rigorous analytic methods to assess the implementation and impacts of federal grants for workforce-aligned credentials on labor market outcomes Implementing randomized controlled trials to identify the impacts of return-to-work services for people with injuries and illnesses, and examining the factors that contribute to program effectiveness Conducting a descriptive study of a student loan program to understand how borrowing and repayment distress have responded to policy changes over time, and designing and assessing the feasibility of potential impact studies Examining participation and outcomes in a scholarship program for apprentices with financial need in eligible construction and industrial programs in Wisconsin. Helping states and school districts build capacity to use data and strengthen support for educators and students Conducting systematic reviews and meta-analyses to determine the effectiveness of interventions, programs, policies, and practices across a range of populations and policy areas Depending on projects and interests, duties might include: Participating in evaluation activities such as developing rigorous study designs, analyzing quantitative data from surveys and administrative sources, reviewing and synthesizing existing evidence, applying innovative methods such as machine-learning techniques, contributing to briefs and reports, and developing data visualizations to enhance the accessibility of findings Designing and deploying approaches that use artificial intelligence tools for data collection (such as literature search or web scraping), processing (for example, cleaning and coding) and preliminary analysis (for example, thematic analysis in qualitative data). Helping program administrators and policymakers make decisions by cleaning, organizing, analyzing, and presenting large amounts of data Assessing the strength of study designs and summarizing large and diverse sets of existing research through systematic reviews and meta-analyses Guiding program staff and policymakers in the use of evidence to make decisions about program selection and adaptation Collaborating with state and local organizations through conducting evaluations or refining their programs Presenting findings and disseminating information to policy, practitioner, and researcher audiences. Required Qualifications: Ph.D. in economics, public policy, sociology, education, statistics, data science/data analytics, or a related field. In lieu of a Ph.D., a master's degree with coursework in causal inference and a minimum of 3 years of demonstrated experience applying it to research will be considered equivalent. Strong quantitative analytical skills, including training in causal inference methodologies. Experience working with programming languages such as R, Python, or Stata. Excellent written and oral communication skills, including an ability to translate complex research methods and findings for practitioner and policy audiences. Ability to work well in teams. Of interest: experience working at a human services program or agency, school district, state or federal government, or foundations. A cover letter, CV, and writing sample or job market paper must be submitted at the time of application via our online application system. Please describe your desired start date in the cover letter. Letters of recommendation will be requested for candidates who advance to the final stage of interviews. We will consider applications on a rolling basis. This position offers an anticipated base salary of $100,000 - $135,000 annually. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state, or local protected class. At Mathematica, we understand the importance of building relationships with colleagues. If you’re not located near one of our offices but would like opportunities to meet up with co-workers, we offer coworking spaces where available. Ask your Talent Acquisition partner for more information about this opportunity and whether it’s an option in your area. Any offer of employment will be contingent upon passing a background check. Various federal agencies with whom we contract require that staff successfully undergo security clearance as a condition of working on the project. If you are assigned to such a project, you will be required to obtain the requisite security clearance. Additionally, if you participate in or complete the application process and are denied, Mathematica may choose to terminate your employment. We take pride in our employees and in their commitment to excellence. We encourage staff to collaborate in developing creative solutions to difficult problems and to share the responsibility and enjoyment of carrying out complex projects. This collegial spirit has helped us earn our reputation for innovative and high-quality work. This role involves leading and designing monitoring, learning, and adaptive management approaches aligned with MSD principles. The coordinator will support the team in planning and implementing MSD interventions, monitoring outcomes, and ensuring quality MEL practices. The position requires strong coaching and mentoring skills to enhance the capacity of staff in data collection and analysis. Candidate Requirements: Minimum MA + 5 years of relevant experience Proven experience in M&E in MSD programs, preferably in Somalia's water sector Experience with climate-sensitive monitoring tools and market price monitoring Strong understanding of data use in technology project design Experience in conducting market systems/value chain assessments Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified MEAL Coordinator-Market System Development- W4R About the job The purpose of this assignment is to lead, design and apply monitoring, learning, and adaptive management approaches aligned with MSD principles. The focus is on building practical skills to track adoption, understand partner performance, assess commercial viability, and generate actionable learning to inform MSD intervention implementation, adaptive management and decision-making.  The Meal Coordinator will take an iterative and adaptive approach, flexibly responding to emerging programmatic priorities and team needs and will also transfer skills as part of broader MSD technical capacity strengthening efforts. The primary objective of this role is to lead and support the team’s capacity to plan and implement MSD interventions, monitor and measure outcomes and impact, demonstrate Value for Money (VfM), and learn from and adapt MSD programming. This will be achieved through practical coaching, application of MSD MEL tools and methodologies Your main duties and responsibilities will be: Management and supervision Conduct MSD MEL Capacity Assessment and Develop Capacity Strengthening Plan for all MEAL and Program staff Review of current MEL systems and practices (including institutional MEL and tech platforms) Provide ongoing technical advisory and operational support to apply systems in real time, troubleshoot implementation challenges and strengthen consistency and quality of MEL practice. Provide hands-on support to design, adapt, and operationalize MEL systems and tools, ensuring:  Design and facilitate applied learning session(s) that establishes a foundational understanding MEL for MSD. Introduce and explore core MSD MEL concepts aligned with the DCED Standard, including:  Systemic change and results chains Market actor performance and incentives Adoption, behavior change, and sustainability pathways Adaptive management and evidence-based decision-making Provide coaching and mentoring (individual and small group) tailored to identified gaps Integration with DRC existing institutional MEL systems and technology and applicable across the full program portfolio Support development and refinement of practical deliverables, including:  Results frameworks, results chains and key performance indicators Measurement and management systems for partnerships and systemic change Lead and manage the Monitoring & Evaluation team (including people planning, performance, well-being and development) Provide technical support to field-based Monitoring & Evaluation staff with a view to ensure coherence in data collection and analysis to support program development and quality Coordination and oversight of all aspects of the Monitoring & Evaluation processes Lead all market systems assessment and evaluations Conduct periodic activity monitoring and site visits to the field to monitor data collection/implementation Capacity building through training, feedback, coaching of the Monitoring & Evaluation and programme staff in data collection, monitoring and analysis Enhance Monitoring & Evaluation capacity among staff to ensure accountability, facilitate planning and strengthen service delivery Lead the development of an internal MSD MEL Toolkit that captures tested approaches, tools, and lessons for ongoing and future programming, contextualizing and integrating key aspects Lead the development of Monitoring & Evaluation strategies, tools and ensure coordination of the Monitoring & Evaluation teams input to the country strategy, proposals and reports. Monitoring and evaluation and adaptive Programming Analyze the data gathered and write baseline and impact assessment reports Continuously improve and update data collection tools, so they can be used in the Guide creation of an internal MSD MEL Toolkit, including:  Adapted templates, that enable teams to apply MSD MEL approaches in practice Practical guidance notes that clarify how to measure and interpret system-level and attributable change Conduct Frequent meetings to revisit and refine the theory of change . Adaptive learning coaching for innovation projects Support partners to implement agile and adaptive learning approaches into their work Guide partners and change agents on how to conduct evaluation and learning experiments and collect and analyse data using the right-level-rigour for the stage of the project. Oversee implementation of learning experiments (such as lean testing, rapid experimentation). Support teams to integrate evidence and learning into project decision making. Collect data and deliver quality analysis Design and implement research and adaptive learning projects. postings.text: --> UNESCO - Non-Staff Consultant - AI Readiness Assessment Methodology Non-Staff Consultant - AI Readiness Assessment Methodology Lead the implementation of the Readiness Assessment Methodology for AI in Suriname. This opening expired 8 months ago. Do not try to apply for this job. UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Open positions at UNESCO Consultant Show advice for this position Application deadline 8 months ago : Monday 16 Feb 2026 at 23:59 UTC Open application form Overview Lead the implementation of the Readiness Assessment Methodology for AI in Suriname. You have: Advanced university degree (PhD, or Master’s) in governance of AI or related fields. Minimum 7 years of professional experience in the technology industry and AI governance. Excellent knowledge of English and Dutch; knowledge of Caribbean language is a plus. Proven ability to draft policy-oriented reports clearly and concisely. Understanding of ethical, legal, social issues in AI. Experience conducting policy reviews and assessments related to AI. Tact and diplomacy in stakeholder engagements. Contract This is a Consultancy contract. More about Consultancy contracts . Partner --> AI Application Assistant: Maximize your UN job search. AI Application Assistant Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Social and Human Sciences Sector (SHS) Duty Station: Suriname Job Family: Social and Human Sciences Type of contract : Affiliated personnel Duration of contract : From 1 to 6 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Duty Station Time) : 16-FEB-2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **OVERVIEW OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THE POST** ----------------------------------------- **I. Background and Justification:** In November 2021, the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence was adopted unanimously by Member States. As the first global normative instrument in its field, this global standard aims to harness the positive impact of AI while providing guidelines for Members States to ensure responsible AI development and address its intrinsic risks and societal challenges. This framework emphasizes the protection of human rights and dignity, promoting transparency, fairness, and human oversight in AI systems. It covers essential policy areas such as data governance, environment, gender, education, research, health, and social well-being. UNESCO is building partnerships with Member States in the Caribbean to operationalize the Recommendation on the Ethics of AI into national institutional and regulatory frameworks, namely by deploying the Readiness Assessment Methodology. Following its implementation in over 70 countries worldwide, the RAM has recently been updated to reflect rapid technological advancements and integrate insights gained from its deployment across diverse national contexts, ensuring its continued relevance and effectiveness. UNESCO seeks an expert to oversee the implementation of the Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) in Suriname. The consultant will lead the preparation of a policy- oriented country report, drawing from RAM results and multi-stakeholder consultations. The report aims to inform a comprehensive national AI strategy, and to provide an evidence-based framework on the ethical governance of AI, with medium and long-term priorities identified, aligning with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI. The assessment and resulting report will be structured around the policy action areas of the UNESCO Recommendation. The expert will receive basic training and benefit efrom the technical guidance of the Bioethics and Ethics of Science and Technology Section (SHS/BIO) of the UNESCO Secretariat, as required. Project Scope ------------- **II. Project Scope:** UNESCO’s aim is to enhance national capacities to carry out the values and the principles of the Recommendation. To fulfill this objective, implementation rests on the Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM). The updated tool consists of a survey, structured around the core policy areas of the UNESCO Recommendation (refer to box below for more details) that will assess the resilience of national frameworks, existing laws, policies and institutions to guide AI developments in the country. The project will be conducted in Suriname. The consultant will collaborate with national and regional stakeholders, including government ministries, academia, civil society, the private sector. Tasks include mapping of key stakeholders, organizing work sessions, conducting interviews and consultations and preparing a policy-oriented country report based on the RAM findings. ***Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM)*** A critical initial stage in the implementation of the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI is the deployment of RAM, as mandated by the Recommendation, to assist Member States in identifying their status at specific moments of their readiness trajectory. In recognition of the rapid pace of technological advancements in AI, and to integrate insights from more than 70 countries that have already implemented the tool, the RAM questionnaire has been updated to ensure that it remains relevant, effective, and responsive to evolving national contexts. In its updated version, the RAM is structured around the policy action areas of the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, supporting Member States in translating ethical principles into concrete and actionable policies. The RAM is a macro level instrument that will help countries understand where they stand on the scale of preparedness to implement AI ethically and responsibly for all their citizens, highlighting what institutional and regulatory changes will be needed. Furthermore, the output of the RAM will also help UNESCO tailor the policy reform and institutional capacity building efforts to the needs of different countries. This will ensure that the country has in place human capacity, policies, and regulations to address the challenges brought by AI, such as reinforced traditional biases, and ensure that people and their interest are always at the centre of AI development. Duties and Responsibilities --------------------------- **III. Duties and Responsibilities** The aim of this consultancy is to lead the development of research and analytical outputs towards the production of a country policy-oriented report. The report will be based on the evidence gained through the deployment of UNESCO’s AI Readiness Assessment Methodology and the key outcomes of national consultations. The consultant shall be responsible for the piloting of the RAM in Suriname as follows: 1. Provide a RAM implementation timeline in coordination with UNESCO. 2. Carry out a mapping of key stakeholders to be engaged for data collection purposes in the RAM implementation. 3. Facilitate work and liaise with a multidisciplinary National Steering Committee that will oversee the deployment of the RAM from the government’s side, notably led by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation (EZOTI). The National Steering Committee will be consulted through the project’s implementation. 4. Conduct the RAM questionnaire to gain in-depth understanding of the potential for AI development, the state of the art in the country in terms of institutional and regulatory readiness, as well as the regulatory and institutional gaps to be filled to transform the potential into action. 5. Coordinate broad-based multistakeholder national consultations and/or focus groups to present the results of the readiness assessment and to facilitate discussions leading to the identification of needs, concerns, and policy priorities for government, civil society, academia and the private sector. III. Duties and Responsibilities cont. -------------------------------------- 6\. Prepare a diagnostic report based on the outcomes of the RAM exercise. To this end, lead in data collection, data curation and analysis, ensuring a high level of quality. Where relevant and necessary, articulate regional and/or comparative perspectives and analysis for the purposes of cross-learning and exchange of good practices. 7\. Organize a mid-term update call with the UNESCO Office and Government counterpart, between 6 to 8 weeks after the project launch. This should take stock of the process and research carried out thus far, discuss challenges if any, and proposals for solutions to address them. The mid-term update should be followed by a recapitulative email of the meeting, particularly if significant points need to be addressed. 8\. Organize a validation workshop, together with the UNESCO Office and Government counterpart, to present the draft country report based on the RAM implementation. This will also be an opportunity to receive feedback from a broader set of stakeholders and possibly provide advice or recommendations at the sub-regional level for national frameworks in keeping with developments in AI. At this stage, additional follow-up with experts may be necessary to support the process and access further data to inform a national report. 9\. Draft the final policy-oriented country report presenting the findings of the updated RAM questionnaire. Depending on the country context, this report may be complementary to the existing national AI strategy or serve as the blueprint for establishing such a strategy/roadmap where one does not exist or updating it. The report will feature recommendations concerning the regulatory and other policy reforms, institutional design, and capacity-development programmes needed for effective and responsible governance of AI in the country, based on the short- and long-term priorities identified, and using the Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence as an overall framework. The report should follow the format which will be provided by UNESCO, and should include qualitative and quantitative information, relevant data visualizations, examples of good practices, highlights, etc. A contact list of the main stakeholders having participated in the exercise should feature at the end of the final report, to facilitate follow-up. 10\. Support UNESCO and the government counterpart in the organization of the launch of the report with national representatives and main stakeholders. The consultant will present the results of the report. This will also be the opportunity to share that the process is intended to be renewed regularly to track progress over time. 11\. Participation in high-level national, regional, or global events organized by UNESCO may be required, to showcase the outcome of the project. 12\. Ensure overall coordination with the UNESCO Office for the Caribbean, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation (EZOTI), national stakeholders, and other relevant stakeholders involved throughout the RAM process. Deliverables ------------- **IV. Deliverables:** The aim of this consultancy is to lead the development of research and analytical outputs to produce an **AI policy and action-oriented country report**. The report will be based on the evidence brought to light and knowledge gained through the deployment of UNESCO’s AI Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) and the key outcomes of the broad national consultations. The consultant is responsible for the following deliverables: 1. **Diagnostic Report**, in English, on the country’s readiness and identified challenges following UNESCO’s AI Readiness Assessment Methodology. The report should also include as annexes: the implementation timeline and a provisional mapping of key stakeholders to consult throughout the process. 2. **Synthesis Report**, in English, on the key outcomes from the multistakeholder national consultations and/or focus groups, stemming from the diagnostic report, and progress achieved based on the results obtained in

postings.text: National Consultant to Conduct the End of Project Evaluation for the MUSHO Project | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content National Consultant to Conduct the End of Project Evaluation for the MUSHO Project UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | Adjumani, Yumbe, Kyegegwa, Isingiro National Senior level Speaks English Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant to conduct the end of project evaluation for the MUSHO Project, which focuses on enhancing women's agency and resilience in refugee settlements and host communities in Uganda. The evaluation will assess the project's effectiveness, relevance, and sustainability, while ensuring a gender-responsive approach. The consultant will engage with various stakeholders, including government ministries and community organizations, to gather data and provide actionable recommendations. This consultancy is expected to contribute to improved decision-making and accountability in advancing gender equality and women's empowerment. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in Gender/Women's studies, Peace and Conflict Studies, or related field At least 5 years of experience in planning, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of development projects Experience in designing and leading gender-responsive evaluations Strong knowledge of Women, Peace, and Security programming Fluency in English Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. This consultancy will support the final evaluation of “The Project for the Implementation of Women, Peace and Security Agenda in Refugee Settlements and Host Communities (MUSHO)” implemented from September 2024 – February 2027. The project aimed to reach 11,000 direct and 43,100 indirect beneficiaries across 5 refugee hosting districts, Adjumani, Yumbe, Madi Okollo, Kyegegwa and Isingiro, in Uganda.   The evaluation will assess the achievement of the project’s goal which was ‘Enhancing women's agency and resilience through comprehensive approaches to women, peace, and security in the humanitarian context in Uganda. The project Outcomes include:  Refugee and host community women, girls, men, and boys have increased capacity to actively participate and contribute meaningfully to peacebuilding and conflict mitigation processes;  Refugee women and youth including women peacebuilders and women human rights defenders’ access timely and quality social and protection services through strengthened protection, referral, and access to justice mechanisms;  Women and youth have increased participation and benefit from gender responsive climate change mitigation and DRR systems and programs to overcome conflict and climate shocks; Income and economic opportunities for refugee and host community women and girls are scaled up to address economically induced conflicts in the humanitarian context, including violent extremism & radicalisation. The project design was informed by the following Theory of Change. 1) IF refugee and host community women, men, and youth have increased capacity to actively participate and contribute meaningfully to peacebuilding and conflict mitigation process, 2) IF refugee women and youth including women peacebuilders and women human rights defenders, access timely and quality social and protection services through strengthened protection, referral and access to justice mechanism, 3) IF women and youth have increased participation and benefit in gender-responsive climate change mitigation and DRR systems and programs to overcome conflict and climate shocks, and 4) IF income and economic opportunities for refugee and host community women and girls are scaled up to address economically induced conflicts in the humanitarian context, including violent extremism and radicalization, THEN 5) women’s agency and resilience in peace, security and humanitarian contexts will be enhanced 6) BECAUSE women are key drivers of peace and security and including them in peace process leads to more lasting peace and stable societies.  The MUSHO project has been implemented through Responsible Parties: Women International Peace Centre (WIPC), Alight, Peace Winds Japan (PWJ) alongside other sub-partners such as Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), National Agricultural Research Institute (NaCRRI), Abi Zonal Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Abi ZARDI), National Association of Professional Environmentalists (NAPE), CFAO Mobility Uganda (Toyota Uganda) and RICCI Every day.  Purpose of the evaluation: The UN Women Evaluation Policy  is the main guiding document that sets forth the principles and organizational framework for evaluation planning, conduct and follow-up in UN Women. These principles are aligned with the United Nations Evaluation Group (UNEG) Norms and Standards for Evaluation in the UN System . The key principles for gender-responsive evaluation at UN Women are: 1) National ownership and leadership; 2) UN system coordination and coherence with regard to gender equality and the empowerment of women; 3) Innovation; 4) Fair power relations and empowerment; 5) Participation and inclusion; 6) Independence and impartiality; 7) Transparency; 8) Quality and credibility; 9) Intentionality and use of evaluation; and 10) Ethics.  It is a priority for UN Women that this endline project evaluation will be gender-responsive and will actively support the achievement of gender equality and women’s empowerment, with emphasis on UN Women’s key areas central to increasing women’s participation in advancing the women peace and security agenda, women’s protection and safety, climate resilience and economic wellbeing in humanitarian action.    The primary intended users of this evaluation are: Staff in target Government Ministries, Departments and Agencies, District Local Government and CSOs;  Target beneficiary communities/groups including grassroot women rights organizations; Staff of responsible partners;  Sectoral leads in the participating UN-agencies and refugee response coordination;  UN Agencies technical working groups;  Development partners.  The primary intended uses of this evaluation are:  Learning and improved decision-making to support the advancement of the NAP III WPS, Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment (GEWE) and gender-responsive disaster risk reduction practices; Provide accountability for the development effectiveness of the project to the donor and other stakeholders; Inform capacity development and mobilization of national stakeholders to advance the WPS agenda, protection services, gender-responsiveness and empowerment of women, girls and youth in humanitarian action; Provide lessons learned and recommendations to inform future resource mobilization and project design. Evaluation objectives, criteria and key questions: The objectives of the evaluation are to:  Assess the relevance of the project and its approach in line with local, national, and international priorities on WPS and its intervention in addressing the needs of refugee and host community women in alignment with GEWE; Assess the effectiveness and efficiency of the UN Women’s approach for achievement of results, as defined in the logical framework, including the Program Theory of Change;  Analyze how the human rights approach and gender equality principles were integrated in the design and implementation of the project; Identify and validate lessons learned and good practices that support gender equality and human rights in relation to UN Women’s mandate; Assess the inter-connectedness and sustainability of UN Women’s initiatives on increasing leadership, protection and economic opportunities for refugee women and analyse possible weakness to improve next steps for scale-up programming; Provide actionable recommendations with respect to the HDP nexus. The evaluation will seek to answer the following key evaluation questions aligned to the UN Evaluation Group (UNEG) evaluation criteria as well as standards based on Human Rights and Gender Equality.  Criterion Questions Relevance and coherence Was the project design, including the choice of interventions and selection of implementing partners appropriate to address the identified needs of beneficiaries, especially refugee women, girls and youth and marginalized groups? Did the design and partner selection align to UN Women’s comparative advantage?   To what extent was the intervention aligned with country priorities for gender equality and the promotion of the active participation of women in peace, security, and recovery in Uganda?   What was the level of engagement between the Partners and key Stakeholders at all levels and the ability to leverage the partnership process to inform the advocacy strategy?   How well did the project design consider learning from previous evaluations / reviews of WPS and LEAP projects? Effectiveness and sustainability To what extent did the project achieve planned outputs and contribute to expected outcomes?    To what extent has the project contributed to sustained changes in women's agency, leadership, economic resilience and influence over peacebuilding and community decision-making, beyond immediate project outputs?   What unexpected outcomes (positive and negative) have been achieved? Did the interventions contribute to the expected outcomes?   What were the main enabling and hindering factors to achieving planned outcomes and what actions need to be taken to overcome any barriers that limit required progress?   Did the partners responsible for implementation have access to the necessary skills, knowledge and capacities needed to deliver the project and ensure sustainability of efforts and benefits?   What local accountability and oversight systems have been established to support the continuation of activities?    Which interventions have the greatest potential for institutional ownership, sustainability and scale-up and what would be required to achieve this? Efficiency How effectively did UN Women’s management structure, including financial and risk management, support efficient project implementation and delivery of required results and address delays through corrective actions?   To what extent were planned output results delivered on time and within budget?   Were the results appropriate to the resources used? Human Rights and Gender Equality How did the project integrate gender equality, human rights and development effectiveness principles: Participation/empowerment; Inclusion/non-discrimination; National accountability / transparency in its design and implementation?   To which extent the project reached the most vulnerable groups considering the current context in the country (ex. People with disability, women affected by conflict and among others).  Evaluation Design:  The evaluation is expected to be non-experimental and summative. It will employ mixed methods including desk-based review of relevant documents backed by consultation with key project stakeholders and field-based primary data collection from direct project beneficiaries. The evaluation will follow a collaborative and participatory approach, ensuring close engagement with programme beneficiaries, implementing partners, ministries, departments, agencies and local governments and other key stakeholders. The analysis of the application of human rights and gender equality principles will be an integral part of the evaluation. Integration of human rights and gender equality issues into the evaluation requires adherence to three main principles – inclusion, participation, and fair power relations.  Management and Repo

postings.text: Roster of Consultants - Primary Health Care, Papua New Guinea – Various Provincial Locations (Duty Station to Be Assigned) | WHO - World Health Organization Skip to main content Roster of Consultants - Primary Health Care, Papua New Guinea – Various Provincial Locations (Duty Station to Be Assigned) WHO - World Health Organization Port Moresby International Band level B level Speaks English Application deadline: November 23, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The consultancy aims to enhance primary health care (PHC) in Papua New Guinea by implementing the WHO PNG’s ACE approach. The consultant will work with the Provincial Health Authority to analyze health system bottlenecks, advise on strategic priorities, and engage communities for improved health outcomes. Key responsibilities include leadership coordination, operational intelligence, quality standards, addressing barriers to care, community engagement, and performance assessment. The role requires a strong background in public health and experience in maternal and child health, immunization, and health system improvement. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in public health or related field At least seven years of relevant professional experience Strong knowledge of WHO–UNICEF PHC framework Experience in maternal, newborn and child health Strong analytical and facilitation skills Expert knowledge of English | Job Description - Roster of Consultants - Primary Health Care, Papua New Guinea – Various Provincial Locations (Duty Station to Be Assigned) (2604737) Roster of Consultants - Primary Health Care, Papua New Guinea – Various Provincial Locations (Duty Station to Be Assigned)-(2604737) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):11 months Job Posting: Nov 9, 2026, 5:33:03 AM Closing Date: Nov 23, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Papua New Guinea-Port Moresby Organization: WP_PNG Papua New Guinea Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. Purpose of the Consultancy To strengthen primary health care (PHC) in an assigned province or provinces of Papua New Guinea by translating WHO PNG’s ACE approach—advocate, convene and enable—into practical, time-bound improvements in key PHC outcomes, including maternal, newborn and child health, immunization, communicable diseases and noncommunicable diseases. Working through the Provincial Health Authority (PHA), the consultant will apply a systems approach to analyse bottlenecks, advise on strategic priorities, convene communities and other sectors, provide operational support, field-test practical tools, and document results and lessons for adaptation and scale-up. Background WHO and UNICEF define PHC as a whole-of-society approach that addresses people’s health needs across the continuum of care, as close as possible to where they live. PHC has three components: (i) integrated health services, with an emphasis on primary care and essential public health functions; (ii) multisectoral policy and action; and (iii) empowered people and communities. The renewed focus on PHC is a globally shared strategic direction, and partners are aligning their investments accordingly. In Papua New Guinea, the Mid-term Review of the National Health Plan 2021–2030 identified PHC-oriented health-system reform as the most immediate priority. Further, the Joint External Evaluation of the International Health Regulations (August 2026) recommended investment in essential health service delivery and WASH to support resilient primary care at levels 1–3 and in communities. WHO is reinforcing this direction through the mid-term review of the WHO Papua New Guinea Country Cooperation Strategy 2024–2028 and by strengthening provincial technical cooperation. This support will help the National Department of Health (NDoH) and PHAs deliver essential health services through a PHC approach. Deliverables The consultant will carry out six functions: 1. Leadership and multisectoral coordination. Facilitate PHA agreement on a few costed, time-bound integrated PHC priorities. Map and align contributions of districts, programmes, churches, partners and other sectors (including but not limited to local-level governments, Ward Development Committees, education, agriculture, water and sanitation, transport, security services such as the PNG Defence Force, correctional services and police, and the private sector). 2. Operational intelligence. Triangulate routine data on maternal and child care, immunization, vaccine-preventable disease (VPD) surveillance, and priority diseases—including TB, HIV, malaria, hypertension and diabetes—with information from reports, registers and consultations with frontline health workers and communities; verify signals generated from event-based surveillance, investigate discrepancies, and map zero-dose children and underserved catchments. 3. Standards and quality. Coach PHA and district teams through one integrated supervision approach covering maternal and child care, vaccination, microplanning, cold chain, AEFI and VPD reporting, and screening, diagnosis, treatment and referral for the priority conditions, including communicable and noncommunicable diseases; agree time-bound corrective actions with clear responsibilities and verify their implementation. 4. Addressing barriers to care. Identify why people miss or drop out of care, including social and gender barriers. Investigate financing (release and use of operational funds, out-of-pocket costs), medicines and last-mile delivery, workforce, transport and referral; present feasible, affordable options to PHA leadership. 5. Implementation, community engagement and capacity. Adapt and operationalize integrated PHC interventions based on the provincial context, including integrated outreach services providing immunization to zero-dose and missed children, a defaulter follow-up tool, an integrated supervisory checklist (L1–4), and referral and medicine-stock tracking. Facilitate community planning with WDCs, village health assistants and the “triad of trust” (health worker, teacher, church leader); set up community feedback; coach PHA counterparts. Document necessary adaptations and lessons for national review and possible scale-up. 6. Performance, learning and communications. Assess agreed indicators using graphs from healthcare facilities and the PHC Dashboard; support learning between districts through learning notes and facilitated exchanges; prepare human-interest stories, photo stories, short web and social-media content and briefings for the PHA, NDoH, WHO and partners, including Gavi, subject to consent and WHO clearance. Cross-cutting: Health emergencies (when requested). Prepare materials to support outbreak detection, community alerts, responses to diseases such as measles and polio, and continuity of essential PHC services during emergencies, in coordination with PHA, NDoH and WHO emergency leads. Output 1 (by end of week 6): Provincial PHC baseline and 90-day action plan agreed with the PHA. Deliverable 1.1: Baseline report (maximum 15 pages) covering the three PHC components and tracer areas: verified bottlenecks, underserved catchments including zero-dose children, operational fund flows, a stakeholder map and up to 10 indicators with baselines. Deliverable 1.2: Costed 90-day integrated action matrix, including community and multisectoral actions, with 2–3 priority demonstration catchments identified based on need, equity, service gaps and implementation feasibility. Output 2 (by end of month 3): Integrated improvement package in use. Deliverable 2.1: Integrated tool set with coaching aids (outreach microplan, follow-up, referral and medicine-stock tools). Deliverable 2.2: Community engagement and multisectoral action plans for the priority catchments, developed with WDCs, village health assistants, the triad of trust and relevant sectors. Deliverable 2.3: Record of orientation and on-site coaching delivered to PHA counterparts, with a functioning PHA-led PHC coordination mechanism for reviewing implementation progress, resolving bottlenecks and tracking agreed actions. Output 3 (by end of month 6): Field-tested improvements and sustainability options. Deliverable 3.1: Field-test report demonstrating implementation of the integrated PHC improvement package in priority catchments, including integrated outreach, supportive supervision, referral and follow-up mechanisms, with verified results by tracer area against baseline, including changes in service coverage and the number of zero-dose children. Deliverable 3.2: Options brief (maximum 4 pages) on financing and sustaining integrated PHC outreach, covering budgeting and release of operational funds and alignment of partner funds. Deliverable 3.3: One learning note and one communication product. Output 4 (by end of month 9): Performance review. Deliverable 4.1: Performance review against the baseline and a second costed 90-day action matrix. Deliverable 4.2: Note on options, costs and prerequisites for extending tested approaches to other districts. Output 5 (final two weeks): Results, communication and handover. Deliverable 5.1: Results and handover note: evidence of change, unresolved issues, tools and capacity transfer. Deliverable 5.2: Dissemination package: human-interest stories and a briefing presentation for the PHA, NDoH, WHO and partners. Qualifications, experience, skills and languages Educational Qualifications: Essential: Advanced university degree (master’s level or above) in public health, medicine, nursing, midwifery, epidemiology, health systems, health policy, health services management or a related field. Desirable: Postgraduate training in primary health care, immunization, maternal and child health, quality improvement, health financing, supply chain management, community engagement or monitoring and evaluation. Experience Essential: At least seven years of relevant professional experience in primary health care, public health or health-system improvement, including work at the subnational or decentralized level and practical work in maternal, newborn and child health, immunization or other priority PHC programmes at national and international levels. Experience producing analytical reports, implementation tools or decision briefs for government or public-health programmes. Desirable: Experience in immunization microplanning, zero-dose approaches, community engagement or multisectoral coordination. Excellent communication skills in English and the ability to present research findings and policy options on complex topics including AI, culture and education related policy questions. Proficiency in quantitative and qualitative research methodologies with the capacity to design mixed methods studies and translate evidence into policy guidance.
