Partner --> Fast-track your UN career: Let the AI Application Assistant tailor your applications to catch recruiters' attention. AI Application Assistant Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Culture Sector (CLT) Duty Station: Paris Job Family: Culture Type of contract : Non Staff Duration of contract : From 7 to 11 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Duty Station Time) : 09-JAN-2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **Background** UNESCO has a mandate to guide cultural policies that safeguard cultural rights and protect cultural diversity in the face of the structural impact of the digital transformation on societies and the cultural sector in particular. In the MONDIACULT 2022 Declaration, Member States called upon UNESCO to support them in harnessing digital transformation, drawing upon the 2017 Operational Guidelines on the Implementation of the Convention in the Digital Environment and the culture-related provisions of the 2021 UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. Building on this mandate, the UNESCO World Conference on Cultural Policies and Sustainable Development – MONDIACULT 2025 established AI and Culture as a central focus area, reflecting the growing influence of digital technologies and artificial intelligence on culture. Preparatory work included the Report of the Independent Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence and Culture (CULTAI Report), convened by UNESCO and a global survey on the implementation of the MONDIACULT Declaration, which examined progress on various topics, including digital transformation and AI. The conference featured ministerial debates and side events that examined the opportunities of AI for cultural access, heritage protection and increased visibility of diverse cultural expressions, together with the risks linked to cultural homogenization, erosion of linguistic diversity, the marginalization of minority voices, the lack of fair recognition for creators and unbalanced cultural data governance. These discussions confirmed the need for coherent cultural policies that address the evolving dynamics of AI-driven environments and that empower local communities and cultural professionals. As part of the CLT/EO, the Special Projects and Partnerships (SPP) unit supports transversal initiatives and special projects in the field of culture by coordinating and monitoring their implementation. This includes cross-sectoral initiatives, such as the UNESCO Framework for Culture and Arts Education (2024) and its Implementation guidance (2025), among others. In this context, CLT/EO/SPP supports an integrated approach to MONDIACULT 2025 thematic areas, particularly AI and culture, by strengthening analytical capacities, generating evidence for policy reflection and advancing cooperation across institutions. It further contributes specialised research functions to support UNESCO’s mandate on strategic challenges, especially AI and culture, including the development of analytical tools, policy-relevant evidence and cross-sector coordination mechanisms. **Overview of the Functions of the Post** Under the overall authority of the Assistant Director-General for Culture (ADG/CLT) and the direct supervision of the Programme Coordinator for Special Projects and Partnerships (CLT/EO/SPP), the Consultant will provide senior-level support on MONDIACULT thematic areas, particularly on AI policy and management for the Culture Sector. The role requires advanced research expertise, strong analytical judgement, experience in designing and elaborating knowledge products in collaboration with academic, civil society, private sector and other stakeholders, and the ability to coordinate complex processes across UNESCO entities and external partners. The Consultant will support the technical follow-up of MONDIACULT 2025 and contribute to the preparatory work towards MONDIACULT 2029. This includes examining how rapid socio-technical change affects cultural rights and governance, analysing institutional and community-level needs and producing forward-looking insights that inform policy development. This work requires consolidating diverse sources of evidence, producing structured analytical outputs and translating research findings into actionable policy contributions. Long Description ---------------- The Consultant will design an internal AI strategy for the Culture Sector and contribute to the preparation of policy guidance for Member States. The work involves reviewing existing evidence, comparing policy approaches across sectors and organisations, analysing Member State priorities and identifying governance gaps related to cultural data, algorithmic distribution systems, institutional accountability, transparency requirements, linguistic diversity, cultural rights and the conditions that shape equitable participation in AI-intensive environments. It also requires the capacity to integrate research, strategic planning and policy analysis in a coherent framework aligned with the MONDIACULT process. The Consultant will also design and support an AI and Culture community engagement initiative to strengthen cooperation among creators, artists, cultural professionals, civil society, technologists and institutional partners. This requires knowledge of community engagement models, network formation, participatory methodologies and mechanisms to translate community insights into policy-relevant outputs. The role further demands experience in designing multi-stakeholder processes and supporting their translation into evidence-based cultural policy. **Deliverables and Timeframe** **Deliverable 1 (03/2026) – Technical contribution to MONDIACULT 2025 follow-up and preparation for MONDIACULT 2029** Research-based analytical contribution supporting the technical follow-up of MONDIACULT 2025, integrating evidence from the ministerial sessions, side events, the digital library and other preparatory work. The deliverable will synthesise these inputs with emerging data from cultural ecosystems, identify priority domains for deeper inquiry and propose a structured approach for monitoring and advancing AI-related cultural policy commitments in preparation for the MONDIACULT 2029 action plan. **Deliverable 2 (05/2026) – Internal Artificial Intelligence strategy for the UNESCO Culture Sector** A practical internal AI strategy for the Culture Sector aligned with the MONDIACULT process and the preparation of the MONDIACULT 2029 action plan. The strategy will build on existing UNESCO documents, policy outcomes and operational initiatives and will incorporate evidence from consultations across Culture Sector entities and other relevant sectors. It will propose culturally rights-based priorities, coordination mechanisms, analytical functions and implementation pathways that guide how the Sector should engage with AI in its programmes, partnerships and support to Member States. **Deliverable 3 (07/2026) – Evidence-based framework and methodological plan for Artificial Intelligence policy guidance** A mixed methods research plan that defines analytical approaches, data collection instruments, literature review and baseline analysis required to produce rigorous policy guidance on AI and culture. It will summarise the key policy areas that require examination, such as the implications of AI for culture and arts education, the conditions that support human creativity and authorship, the impact on heritage protection, cultural rights, linguistic diversity, cultural data practices, algorithmic distribution systems, institutional accountability and the evolving forms of mediation between creators, institutions and audiences, with particular attention to the needs of the Global South. **Deliverable 4 (09/2026) – Analytical and pilot design framework on Artificial Intelligence, culture and arts education** A structured analytical framework and pilot design focused on the role of AI in culture and arts education across formal, non-formal and lifelong learning contexts. The deliverable will define key policy questions, conceptual foundations and design parameters for innovative approaches to culture and arts education in AI shaped environments. It will address issues such as cultural rights in education, human creativity and authorship, skills development, ethical and critical AI literacy, inclusion and access, pedagogical innovation and institutional readiness. The framework will outline a pilot initiative in culture and arts education, including objectives, target groups, learning modalities, implementation steps, resource requirements and indicators for assessing educational quality, relevance and policy uptake. The deliverable will also identify pathways for integrating lessons into national education and cultural policies. **Deliverable 5 (10/2026) – Draft Artificial Intelligence policy guidance document for the cultural and creative ecosystem** A research driven draft guidance document that synthesises evidence generated through the mixed methods research plan and advances preliminary policy orientations for Member States. postings.text: Research Specialist Scientific Donor Relationships Coordinator | UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Skip to main content Research Specialist Scientific Donor Relationships Coordinator UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Lusaka BG08 level Speaks English, Italian, Spanish Application deadline: November 18, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Research Specialist-Scientific & Donor Relationships Coordinator will lead scientific and technical efforts in land-use monitoring and biodiversity conservation in Zambia. This role involves ensuring the quality and credibility of monitoring frameworks and assessments, while also managing donor relationships and compliance with funding guidelines. The position requires collaboration with various stakeholders, including government and community partners, to promote sustainable development and restore degraded ecosystems. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in environmental management and a strong background in donor-funded projects. Candidate Requirements: Master's or Ph.D. in relevant field 5+ years of experience in environmental management or related projects Experience in ecosystem monitoring and field team coordination Engagement with international development agencies Field experience in Sub-Saharan Africa Knowledge of land degradation and biodiversity conservation Proficiency in Remote Sensing and GIS applications Fluency in English and Italian Job Description The Organization The Alliance of Bioversity International and the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) deliver research-based solutions that harness agricultural biodiversity and sustainably transform food systems to improve people’s lives. Alliance solutions address the global crises of malnutrition, climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation. With novel partnerships, the Alliance generates evidence and mainstreams innovations to transform food systems and landscapes so that they sustain the planet, drive prosperity, and nourish people. The Alliance is part of CGIAR, a global research partnership for a food-secure future. About the position The Research Specialist-Scientific & Donor Relationships Coordinator will provide overall scientific and technical leadership to the Land-Use Monitoring component, ensuring the quality, credibility, and timeliness of monitoring frameworks, technical assessments, and deliverables. Given the central role of Italian institutional and donor engagement in the project, the position will also serve as the project's Donor Relationships Coordinator, ensuring effective communication, compliance, and reporting vis-à-vis AICS and the Italian Cooperation system, and supporting the broader institutional relations function across government, community, and private sector stakeholders. The Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, in partnership with the Botanic Garden – Museum Network of Sapienza University of Rome, is implementing the project “Restoring the Biodiversity of Degraded Ecosystems and Reducing Deforestation in the Northwestern and Copperbelt Regions along the Lobito Corridor, while Promoting Sustainable Development”, funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) under the Partnership Arrangement for AID 013387/01/0. The 36-month initiative (September 2026 – September 2029) works in Zambia's Northwestern and Copperbelt Provinces to restore degraded Miombo woodland landscapes, strengthen institutional and community capacity for land and forest monitoring, and promote sustainable, gender-equitable livelihoods, in close collaboration with the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MoGEE), the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), and other national and provincial partners. Component 1 focuses on strengthening monitoring and reporting capacities for sustainable land and forest management, including institutional and community-based monitoring systems, a geo-platform integrating satellite and community-sourced data, and capacity building for government, community, and forest ranger stakeholders. Component 1 is technically led by the Botanic Garden – Museum Network, Sapienza University of Rome, working in close coordination with the project's Alliance-hosted Project Management Unit (PMU). The position will be based in Lusaka, Zambia, with regular travel to project sites in the Northwestern and Copperbelt Provinces and missions to Rome, Italy Key Responsibilities Scientific Coordination Component 1 Lead the overall scientific strategy and technical design of forest restoration, land monitoring, and biodiversity conservation activities. Establish scientific methodologies and monitoring frameworks to assess landscape health, biodiversity recovery, and deforestation rates. Supervise technical assessments on soil quality, vegetation cover, and ecosystem health in mining-affected zones. Draft, review, and ensure the quality of scientific reports, technical briefs, and project deliverables submitted to donor agencies and partners. Lead the design and technical development of the project's geo-platform, monitoring indicators, and data-quality protocols under Component 1, in coordination with the MRV and Land-Use-Change Experts. Ensure that Component 1 monitoring tools and outputs are designed as decision-support instruments that feed into district and national planning processes and Components 2–4. Donor Relationships & Financial/Technical Narrative Reporting Serve as the project's liaison officer for contacts with AICS and the Italian Embassy in Lusaka and Rome on matters relating to overall project scientific quality, in close coordination with the Principal Investigator and Project Manager. Ensure project implementation and reporting comply with the provisions of the Partnership Arrangement for AID 013387/01/0 and applicable AICS guidelines and procedures. Preparation and consolidation of quarterly and annual technical and financial reports to AICS, in line with agreed templates, formats, and deadlines, and in coordination with the PI, project coordinator, Alliance’s finance team and Support instalment requests, budget realignments, and no-cost extension processes with AICS, as required. Ensure donor visibility requirements are respected across project communications, publications, and events. Support the organization of, and reporting to, the Project Steering Committee (PSC), including preparation of technical materials for AICS and Embassy representatives. Institutional Relations & Stakeholder Engagement Maintain strategic alignment and ongoing communication with the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) and relevant Italian diplomatic missions. Facilitate inter-institutional working groups and multi-stakeholder dialogues to ensure policy integration, local ownership, and long-term sustainability. Support the development of fund-raising efforts in Africa, including the development of project proposals. Programmatic & Operational Support Provide scientific guidance for field team activities on component 1 across the Northwestern and Copperbelt provinces. Implement technical and filed work activities as agreed with supervisor. Oversee the technical integration of community-led land management plans with national policy frameworks. Help organize technical workshops, capacity-building seminars, and stakeholder consultation meetings. Contribute to the preparation of Annual Operating Plans and budget estimates, in coordination with the PMU and the M&E Focal Point. Participate actively in PMU coordination meetings, prepare meetings minutes and contribute to overall project risk management and adaptive management processes. Requirements Qualifications and requirements Master's or Ph.D. degree in Forestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Conservation Biology, or a related discipline. Minimum of 5 years of professional experience managing technical, scientific, or research-driven projects in environmental management, biodiversity conservation, forestry, or land restoration. Proven experience in field-based ecosystem monitoring and hands-on coordination of scientific field teams. Proven track record of high-level engagement with international development agencies. Direct experience working on donor-funded international development programs (experience with AICS procedures and guidelines is highly advantageous). Field experience in Sub-Saharan Africa, specifically in Southern Africa, is required. Prior experience liaising with or reporting to institutional donors on financial and narrative reporting matters is an asset. In-depth understanding of land degradation assessment, sustainable forest management, and biodiversity conservation. Knowledge of African context and in particular of Zambian environmental legislation, forestry policies, and local governance structures is advantageous. Practical knowledge and applied experience in Remote Sensing, GIS applications, and Earth Observation tools for environmental monitoring and landscape health assessment. Proven track record of technical and scientific production, including a demonstrated ability to author, review, and publish scientific articles, research papers and technical reports. Familiarity with donor compliance frameworks and financial/narrative reporting cycles for institutional development cooperation programs is an asset. Digital CBT and Financial Inclusion Support onboarding and delivery through approved digital channels. Monitor connectivity, access, agent coverage, liquidity and FSP capacity. Beneficiary Accountability and Protection Communicate entitlements, payment details and feedback channels to beneficiaries. Follow up CBT complaints and issues and refer protection concerns appropriately. Identify barriers to safe, equitable CBT access for vulnerable groups. G. Emergency Preparedness and Anticipatory Action Support CBT preparedness for shocks, including delivery, onboarding, FSP readiness and contingency arrangements. Support rapid CBT activation and scale-up following approved triggers. Document lessons from major CBT activations to strengthen preparedness. H. Coordination, Monitoring and Learning Coordinate with WFP functions, partners, FSPs, Government and other CBT stakeholders. Maintain accurate CBT data and submit timely monthly and quarterly reports. Analyze implementation, payment exceptions, FSP performance, beneficiary concerns and risks. Document Karamoja lessons and good practices to improve CBT guidance, tools and procedures. Provide CBT operational or surge support across WFP Uganda as required. 5. Experience in CBT, digital payments, financial inclusion, payment operations or social protection is highly desirable. Experience in beneficiary onboarding, payments, reconciliation, assurance, monitoring or data management is desirable. Experience with FSPs, mobile operators, banks or other digital payment providers is an advantage. Experience working with Government, partners and communities. Experience in Karamoja or a similar remote, shock-prone environment is an advantage. Languages Fluency in spoken and written English. postings.text: Programme Policy Officer (Poverty Graduation Technical Specialist / Team Leader), SC9 based at the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content Programme Policy Officer (Poverty Graduation Technical Specialist / Team Leader), SC9 based at the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment WFP - World Food Programme Vientiane National SB-4 (SC8/SC9), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement level Speaks English, Lao Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Programme Policy Officer (Poverty Graduation Technical Specialist / Team Leader) will lead WFP-supported activities aimed at enhancing the resilience of rural women in Laos through a climate-resilient and gender-responsive poverty graduation program. This role involves providing strategic and technical advisory support to the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, overseeing program implementation, and ensuring compliance with climate and disaster risk considerations. The officer will also coordinate capacity-building activities and develop key knowledge products to disseminate pilot experiences. The position requires collaboration with various stakeholders to empower women and improve their livelihoods. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in relevant field At least 5 years of experience in community development and poverty reduction 3 years in a management role Experience in designing and monitoring livelihood activities Strong analytical and leadership skills Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills Fluency in Lao and English DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 25 November 2026-23:59-GMT+07:00 Indochina Time (Vientiane) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). Background The Building Resilience and Reducing Rural Poverty Project (BRRRP) is an initiative by the Government of Lao PDR, particularly the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE), in collaboration with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), aimed at addressing food insecurity, rural poverty, and reduce vulnerabilities exacerbated by climate change. It aims to improve the health, resilience, and socioeconomic profile of poor households, particularly women, through a combination of adaptive and shock-responsive social protection measures. The project targets districts in four provinces: Khammouan, Louangphabang, Savannahkhet, and Xaiyabuly, which are characterized by high poverty rates, malnutrition, and climate risks. It combines nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfers (CCT) with an innovative poverty graduation program, aimed to support the most vulnerable populations, particularly poor pregnant women and mothers of young children. Key components of the project include: Output 1: Coverage of shock-responsive and nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfer program expanded. Output 2: Gender-responsive and climate-resilient poverty graduation program piloted. Output 3: Social protection delivery systems and CCT implementation enhanced. Output 4: Institutional capacity for gender-smart and climate-responsive monitoring and evaluation strengthened. Under Output 2 WFP will provide technical support to MAE in the design, implementation, and evaluation of the climate-resilient and gender-responsive poverty graduation program specifically for rural women. The pilot will benefit at least 4,500 rural women as beneficiaries of conditional cash transfer, across four districts in four provinces.  Recognizing the multidimensional nature of poverty and climate vulnerability, the program will offer a holistic set of sequenced, climate-smart, and time-bound interventions tailored for poor women, combining targeted cash transfers with: (i) livelihood grants to pursue climate-resilient and sustainable livelihoods, (ii) technical skills training, (iii) support for financial inclusion, and (iv) social empowerment through psychosocial support, including dedicated coaching and life skills training to promote social inclusion and positive behavior change. The pilot graduation program under Output 2 consists of activities across five poverty graduation pillars (social protection, livelihoods promotion, financial inclusion, social empowerment, coaching & mentorship), in a strategic sequence within 24 months to empower poor women with skills, knowledge, tools, access to resources, livelihoods, and self-confidence to build long-term resilience, particularly to climate shocks. The pilot combines support for immediate needs (with conditional cash transfer) with longer-term investments in training and income generation to build long-term resilience. The position of Poverty Graduation Technical Specialist (national position) is based at the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment and will be required to periodically report and collaborate with WFP on the progress of implementation. 1. Responsibilities Act as Team Leader of the WFP supported activities under Output 2, support the strengthening of institutional and technical capacities of government counterparts by providing overall strategic and technical advisory support to DRD-PR and MAE related to poverty graduation by strengthening the resilience of women to climate change; Program preparation, implementation oversight and management, support in training, and input on monitoring, documentation and knowledge management for the pilot; Oversee administrative aspects and support day-to-day management of activities within Output 2; Apply climate and disaster risk considerations throughout the pilot activities such as livelihood selection, technical training, life skills training and others; Provide technical guidance to ensure that the design and implementation of the graduation pilot comply with the required climate and disaster risk screening and assessment of the project, incorporates climate and disaster risk considerations throughout the programme cycle and is aligned with the climate and district-level Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessments (CRVA) recommendations; Ensure that livelihood choices are informed by appropriate climate and disaster-risk screening and that climate risks and resilience considerations are systematically integrated across pilot design and implementation; Ensure that assessments of potential risks associated with climate variability are considered for the recommended livelihood options; Provide oversight and guidance of the development of key knowledge products and disseminate pilot experiences to the government of Lao PDR, ADB, civil society organizations, development partners, and external audiences; Support and provide guidance to the DRD-PR on designing and monitoring partner-level agreements, and monitoring their implementation through the establishment of constructive relationships with those partners; Work closely with the Gender and Social Development Specialist to ensure that training, monitoring, coaching, livelihoods support, and other graduation activities are designed and implemented in ways that respond to the specific vulnerabilities and constraints faced by rural women in the target districts, and ultimately support their longer-term well-being, resilience, agency, livelihoods, and economic empowerment; Take overall responsibility for preparing reports and overseeing the team’s development of technical documents such as operations manual, work plan, training modules, and monitoring tools and systems; Coordinate capacity building activities including training, and development of training materials for DRD-PR and pilot implementation staff; Any other duties, as required. 2. Qualifications and Required Experience Advanced university degree in international or community development, anthropology, sociology, gender studies, public policy, natural resources management, economics, political science, business management, disaster risk management, or another related field. Degree or professional qualifications in management desired. At least 5 years of professional experience in community development and poverty reduction programmes, including climate change, disaster risk management, natural resource management, and rural development, of which at least three years were in a management role. Candidates should also have a minimum of three years of experience designing, implementing, and monitoring livelihood activities and economic inclusion interventions, including cash-plus and/or poverty graduation approaches, with a strong focus on household-based approaches, women’s empowerment, and climate resilience. Solid understanding of the government structure after the restructuring, national and agriculture sector plans and priorities. Excellent analytical, strategic thinking, problem-solving, decision-making and leadership skills. Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, particularly with government institutions and development partners. Experience working on climate resilience in Lao PDR is highly desirable. Experience working with international organizations (e.g., UN agencies, IFIs such as IFAD, ADB, and World Bank) is highly desirable.  Fluency in Lao and excellent writing, speaking and understanding of English required. The consultant will focus on strategic activities related to health emergency preparedness, misinformation management, and behaviorally informed communication. Responsibilities include developing capacity-building plans, conducting social listening, and providing technical support for health communication initiatives. The role requires collaboration with various stakeholders to strengthen health communication frameworks and community engagement efforts. Candidate Requirements: University degree in communications, public health, or related field Minimum five years of experience in risk communication or health communication Experience in developing RCCE training or capacity-building activities Proficiency in MS Office applications Fluency in English and Khmer | Job Description - National Consultant - Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Cambodia (2604657) National Consultant - Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Cambodia-(2604657) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):6 months Job Posting: Nov 10, 2026, 4:53:01 AM Closing Date: Nov 24, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Cambodia-Phnom Penh Organization: WP_KHM Cambodia Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. Purpose of the Consultancy The consultancy will provide technical support to WHO Cambodia and the Ministry of Health to strengthen risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) systems, capacity, coordination and implementation. The consultant will support strategic RCCE activities related to health emergency preparedness and response, social listening, misinformation and disinformation management, and behaviourally informed communication, aligned with APHSAF, the National Action Plan for Health Security 2025–2029, the draft Multi-hazard RCCE Framework, and Communication for Health (C4H) approaches. Background Effective communication and community engagement are essential to resilient health systems. Communication for Health (C4H) and risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) use evidence-informed communication, behavioural and social science, and community insights to promote healthy behaviours, strengthen trust, address misinformation and support preparedness and response to public health emergencies. In Cambodia, strengthening C4H and RCCE capacities can advance national health priorities and health security by improving coordination, health literacy, community engagement and access to timely, inclusive and responsive health information and services. These efforts support the Asia Pacific Health Security Action Framework (APHSAF), building on APSED, as well as Cambodia’s implementation of the International Health Regulations (2005) and the National Action Plan for Health Security 2025–2029. They emphasize stronger communication systems, meaningful community participation, social listening and feedback, management of misinformation and disinformation, and the use of community insights to inform health programmes and emergency response. To support these priorities, WHO Cambodia seeks a national RCCE consultant to provide technical and operational support for C4H and RCCE planning, implementation, coordination, monitoring and evaluation. The consultant will help strengthen national and subnational capacities, coordination with the Ministry of Health and partners, and the use of evidence-informed and context-appropriate communication approaches across health programmes and emergency preparedness and response. Deliverables Under the supervision of the WHO Cambodia Senior Advisor, and in collaboration with colleagues in the Western Pacific Regional Office, particularly the Risk Communication Officer in the Health Emergencies Programme (CPI/WHE), the consultant will work on-site at the WHO Cambodia Office in Phnom Penh, with the following outputs and deliverables. Output 1: Strengthened RCCE and Communication for Health systems and capacities across priority health programmes and public health emergencies Deliverable 1.1: A rapid review of existing RCCE, Communication for Health, social and behaviour change, social listening, infodemic management and related capacity-building materials in Cambodia, including identified gaps, opportunities and recommendations for an integrated capacity-building approach. Deliverable 1.2: A prioritized RCCE and Communication for Health capacity-building plan, developed in consultation with the Ministry of Health and relevant partners, aligned with APHSAF, the National Action Plan for Health Security 2025–2029, the draft Multi-hazard RCCE Framework, relevant national health strategies and WHO C4H approaches. Deliverable 1.3: Adapted training materials and documentation of technical support provided for selected RCCE and C4H training or capacity-building activities targeting national and subnational health authorities, priority disease programmes and relevant partners, including participant feedback and recommendations for follow-up. Output 2: Strengthened use of behavioural and community insights to inform health communication and community engagement interventions Deliverable 2.1: Monthly social listening and community feedback reports covering agreed priority communicable diseases, noncommunicable diseases and emerging health threats, highlighting community concerns, information needs, behavioural barriers, misinformation trends and actionable recommendations for relevant programmes. Deliverable 2.2: Technical inputs and documented coordination support for the planning and implementation of priority RCCE and Communication for Health activities with the Ministry of Health, WHO technical programmes, regional counterparts and partners, including routine health promotion, seasonal health risks and public health emergency preparedness and response. Deliverable 2.3: Provide technical support to the Department of Communicable Disease Control and the National Centre for Health Promotion of the Ministry of Health for the ongoing social and behaviour change communication activities, including but not limited to the handwashing campaign in traditional markets, H5N1 behavioural insights generation and the development of infodemic management standard operating procedures (SOPs). Deliverable 2.4: H5N1: WCO sees BRIDGE as an opportunity to access WRPO’s funding and make RCCE interventions in Cambodia more evidence-informed, starting with H5N1. WPRO’s goal is to validate the BRIDGE tools at the country level. In this context, provide support and ensure WHO protocols and quality control are maintained in the field research study using the BRIDGE tool for H5N1 among communities in two provinces, in close collaboration with CDC, MoH, and a third-party contractor who will conduct the research among communities. Deliverable 2.5: National Infodemic Management SOP: A draft version has been revised following feedback from a prior review workshop and shared with CDC and WPRO focal points in January. postings.text: Consultant International pour l’enquête de couverture post-campagne rougeole à Madagascar | WHO - World Health Organization Skip to main content Consultant International pour l’enquête de couverture post-campagne rougeole à Madagascar WHO - World Health Organization Antananarivo International B – P3 level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 14, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Consultant will provide an independent and timely estimation of measles vaccination coverage achieved during the follow-up campaign in Madagascar, adhering to WHO methodological standards. This role involves designing the survey methodology, training field teams, ensuring quality assurance, analyzing data, and drafting reports. The consultant will work closely with a national consultant to coordinate operational aspects with the Ministry of Public Health and other partners. The position requires extensive experience in field epidemiology and vaccination program evaluation. Candidate Requirements: Doctorate or master's degree in epidemiology, biostatistics, public health, or related field At least 7 years of field epidemiology or vaccination program evaluation experience Experience designing or analyzing at least 3 cluster vaccination coverage surveys per WHO methodology Experience in sub-Saharan Africa or resource-limited island contexts, preferably Madagascar Expert knowledge of WHO cluster survey manual and VCQI tool Proficiency in electronic data collection software (ODK/KoBo) and statistical analysis software (R or Stata) Ability to train field teams and communicate findings to decision-makers Fluent in French and intermediate in English | Job Description - Consultant International pour l’enquête de couverture post-campagne rougeole à Madagascar (2604764) Consultant International pour l’enquête de couverture post-campagne rougeole à Madagascar-(2604764) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):03 months Job Posting: Nov 9, 2026, 10:30:14 AM Closing Date: Nov 14, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Madagascar-Antananarivo Organization: AF_MDG Madagascar Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. 1. Area of expertise : Consultant International pour l’enquête de couverture post-campagne rougeole à Madagascar 2. Purpose of consultancy Le consultant international sera chargé de fournir une estimation indépendante, robuste et disponible en temps utile de la couverture vaccinale contre la rougeole atteinte par la campagne de suivi d'octobre 2026, selon les normes méthodologiques de l'OMS, afin d'éclairer les décisions programmatiques du Ministère de la Santé Publique, de la DPEV et des partenaires. 3. Background Madagascar a organisé, du 5 au 9 octobre 2026, une campagne nationale de vaccination supplémentaire (SIA) contre la rougeole, couvrant l'ensemble des districts du pays, avec l'appui de Gavi, l'Alliance du Vaccin, et de ses partenaires (OMS, UNICEF). Cette campagne était intégrée à la campagne round 2 contre la polio et la supplémentation en vitamine A. Pour toute campagne de vaccination contre la rougeole qu'il finance, Gavi recommande qu'une enquête de couverture post-campagne (ECPC) indépendante, soit conduite selon les normes de l'OMS et recommandée par le Measles & Rubella Partnership dans les trois mois suivant la fin de la campagne. Cette enquête ne se substitue pas au suivi administratif et à la surveillance en cours de campagne ; elle en est le complément indépendant, seul à même de mesurer la couverture réellement atteinte, y compris chez les enfants n'ayant jamais reçu de dose de vaccin antirougeoleux (« zéro dose »). Dans le contexte de faiblesse des couvertures vaccinales, notamment avec MCV2 à 37% et MCV1 à 67% en juillet 2026, corroborée par les épidémies de rougeole en cours à Madagascar, avec un total de 62 districts en 2026. Une mesure indépendante et rigoureuse de la couverture atteinte par la campagne est nécessaire pour orienter les décisions programmatiques ultérieures, y compris d'éventuelles activités de rattrapage ciblées. Les revues internationales des ECPC menées ces dernières années montrent que cet exercice est souvent retardé, insuffisamment standardisé, et parfois réduit à un exercice de redevabilité plutôt qu'à un outil d'aide à la décision : sur les campagnes nationales rougeole conduites dans le monde depuis 2020, moins d'un quart ont été suivies d'un rapport d'ECPC disponible. Les présents termes de référence proposent un dispositif rigoureux, documenté et utilisable à temps pour Madagascar. Articulation avec un consultant national qui sera recruté séparément (termes de référence distincts) pour assurer l'interface opérationnelle avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique (MSANP), la DPEV, les DRSP et SDSP concernés, ainsi que la coordination logistique du travail de terrain. Le présent consultant international assure la direction technique de l'enquête : conception méthodologique, formation, assurance qualité, analyse et rédaction du rapport, en binôme étroit avec le consultant national. 4. Deliverables Objectifs spécifiques • Estimer la couverture vaccinale de la dose administrée pendant la campagne de suivi, avec intervalle de confiance à 95 %, au niveau national et par strate ou région prioritaire ; • Estimer la couverture parmi les enfants antérieurement « zéro dose » en vaccination de routine, afin d'évaluer la capacité de la SIA à atteindre les enfants les plus vulnérables ; • Identifier les raisons de non-vaccination et les obstacles d'accès (connaissance de la campagne, distance, disponibilité des équipes, facteurs socioculturels) ; • Évaluer la qualité de mise en œuvre de la campagne (couverture par carte vs déclaration, respect du calendrier, qualité de l'enregistrement) ; • Produire des recommandations opérationnelles pour les activités de rattrapage éventuelles, la préparation des futures campagnes et le renforcement de la vaccination de routine. Étendue des travaux par phase : Cadrage et protocole : Revue documentaire (plan de la SIA, microplans, données administratives, rapports de surveillance) ; élaboration du protocole d'enquête conforme au manuel OMS (échantillonnage, questionnaire, plan d'analyse) ; calcul de la taille d'échantillon et du plan de sondage ; soumission pour approbation éthique et validation technique (comité national, DVSSER, DPEV, OMS, Gavi, UCP) Outils et formation : Adaptation du questionnaire standard OMS au contexte malgache (bilingue français/malgache) ; programmation de la collecte électronique (ODK/KoBo) ; élaboration des manuels de terrain ; formation des superviseurs et enquêteurs nationaux, avec le consultant national Collecte : Supervision technique de la collecte (présentielle et/ou à distance selon les zones) ; contrôle qualité en temps réel des données ; appui à la résolution des difficultés de terrain, en particulier dans les zones enclavées Analyse : Nettoyage et analyse des données avec l'outil VCQI (*Vaccination Coverage Quality Indicators*) ou équivalent validé par l'OMS ; production des indicateurs standards (couverture par dose, atteinte des zéro-dose, raisons de non-vaccination) Restitution : Rédaction du rapport préliminaire puis du rapport final ; présentation des résultats aux autorités nationales et aux partenaires (Ministère, DPEV, DVSSER, OMS, UNICEF, Gavi) ; appui à l'intégration des résultats dans la planification 2027 Méthodologie attendue par parametre : L'enquête suit le manuel de référence de l'OMS sur les enquêtes de couverture vaccinale en grappes (*Vaccination Coverage Cluster Surveys: Reference Manual*, WHO/IVB/18.09, révisé en 2021), avec un échantillonnage probabiliste rigoureux. Le consultant est responsable de finaliser les choix méthodologiques ci-dessous, sur la base des standards suivants : Plan de sondage : Sondage probabiliste en grappes à deux degrés (sélection aléatoire des grappes, puis échantillonnage aléatoire simple ou segmentaire des ménages) ; la méthode des « premières maisons » n'est pas acceptée Taille d'échantillon : Calculée par strate pour une précision définie (par exemple ± 5 points), avec ajustement pour l'effet de grappe (*design effect*), à l'aide du calculateur OMS de taille d'échantillon Stratification : Au minimum une stratification permettant une estimation distincte pour les zones à risque documenté et pour le reste du pays Population cible : Enfants éligibles à la campagne, avec sous-analyse des enfants antérieurement zéro-dose en vaccination de routine Délai de mise en œuvre : Idéalement 4 à 8 semaines après la fin de la SIA (limiter le biais de rappel), et au plus tard dans les 3 mois, conformément à la recommandation du Measles & Rubella Partnership Outils de collecte : Questionnaire électronique standardisé (ODK/KoBo), incluant les indicateurs OMS de couverture, de qualité et de raisons de non-vaccination Analyse : VCQI ou équivalent validé par l'OMS ; indicateurs présentés avec intervalles de confiance à 95 % et effets de plan Assurance qualité : Supervision indépendante de la collecte, contrôle des données en temps réel, plan d'analyse pré-spécifié avant le début de la collecte Livrables et calendrier indicative : 3 semaines après le démarrage : Protocole d'enquête finalisé (plan de sondage, questionnaire, plan d'analyse) et dossier d'approbation éthique 5 semaines après le démarrage : Outils de collecte électroniques testés et manuels de terrain 6 semaines après le démarrage : Formation des superviseurs et enquêteurs réalisée 10 semaines après le démarrage : Rapport de supervision de la collecte, avec contrôle qualité des données 12 semaines après le démarrage : Base de données nettoyée et analysée (VCQI) 13 semaines après le démarrage : Rapport préliminaire (résultats clés, format synthétique pour décision rapide) 16 semaines après le démarrage : Rapport final complet, avec recommandations opérationnelles 17 semaines après le démarrage : Présentation des résultats aux autorités nationales et aux partenaires 5. Qualifications, experience, skills and languages Educational Qualifications: Diplôme de niveau doctorat OU master en épidémiologie, biostatistique, santé publique OU discipline apparentée. Experiences : • Au moins 7 ans d'expérience professionnelle en épidémiologie de terrain ou en suivi-évaluation des programmes de vaccination. • Avoir conçu, supervisé ou analysé au moins 3 enquêtes de couverture vaccinale en grappes selon la méthodologie OMS, idéalement incluant des EPC rougeole ou RR. • Expérience de travail en Afrique subsaharienne ou dans des contextes insulaires à ressources limitées ; une expérience à Madagascar ou dans la région de l'océan Indien est souhaitée et constituera un atout majeur. Skills/Knowledge : • Maîtrise du manuel OMS de référence des enquêtes en grappes (WHO/IVB/18.09) et de l'outil VCQI ou équivalent ; maîtrise d'un logiciel de collecte électronique (ODK/KoBo) et d'un logiciel d'analyse statistique (R ou Stata). • Capacité de formation d'équipes de terrain, rigueur méthodologique, capacité rédactionnelle et de restitution à des publics décisionnels Languages and level required (Basic/Intermediate/Expert) : Expert knowledge of french Intermediate knowledge of english 6. Location : Antananarivo, avec déplacements sur le terrain pour la formation et la supervision 7. Remuneration and budget (travel costs are excluded) : a. Remuneration: Payband level B – P3 b. Living expenses : related to country Perdiem rate 8. Please add the name of the following : a. Hiring Manager: Dr CISSOKO Bobossam b. Partner --> Boost Your Career Prospects - Try Pro Membership Now UN Talent Pro Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Education Sector (ED) Duty Station: UIL Hamburg Classification of duty station: Standard Duration of Assignment: Job Family: Education Type of contract : Non Staff Duration of contract : From 7 to 11 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Paris Time) : 16-JAN-2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **OVERVIEW OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THE POST** ----------------------------------------- **Background and Context** The UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning (UIL) is located in Hamburg, Germany, and is one of UNESCO’s eight education Institutes. UIL supports Member States in the field of lifelong learning with a focus on learning ecosystems, skills for life and work, and inclusive learning. It pays special attention to UNESCO’s Global Priorities Africa and Gender Equality. Within UNESCO’s broad educational mandate, the mission of the Institute is to promote the recognition of and create the conditions for the exercise of the right to education and learning. The Institute undertakes research, capacity-building, networking and publication on lifelong learning. UIL responds to the concerns of all UNESCO Member States, giving priority to least developed countries. Despite global efforts, 739 million youth and adults lack basic literacy skills—two-thirds of whom are women. While Southern Asia and sub-Saharan Africa house the largest shares of this population, significant challenges persist across all regions, requiring urgent policy and financial investment to reach the most disadvantaged. To address these gaps, UNESCO launched the Global Alliance for Literacy (GAL) in 2016 coalition of 31 countries and diverse stakeholders dedicated to advocating for and accelerating literacy improvements in the nations with the greatest need, and UIL is the Secretariat of this Alliance. Published every three to four years, the Global Reports on Adult Learning and Education (GRALEs) take stock of adult learning and education (ALE) progress on national, regional and global level, identifies challenges and provides actionable recommendations for policymakers, practitioners and researchers and other relevant ALE stakeholders. The sixth Global Report on Adult Learning and Education (GRALE 6) will monitor the progress in implementing the Marrakech Framework for Action (MFA, 2022)—the outcome document of CONFINTEA VII—as well as the Recommendation on Adult Learning and Education (RALE, 2015). On behalf of UNESCO, UIL is mandated to serve as the Secretariat to prepare and publish GRALE 6 in 2027. In a context of rapid urban growth and increasing challenges related to social inclusion, sustainability, and economic development, UIL established the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities (GNLC) to support local governments in harnessing lifelong learning as a strategic tool for inclusive and sustainable urban development. The GNLC, coordinated by UIL, is an international, policy-oriented network that provides inspiration, know-how, and examples of best practice. Its mission is to support and accelerate the practice of lifelong learning in cities worldwide by promoting policy dialogue and peer learning among member cities, forging links and fostering partnerships, building capacities for lifelong learning, and developing tools to encourage and recognize progress in building learning cities. The GNLC opened for membership in 2015. Since then, the network has grown to more than 400 member cities across all five UNESCO regions. Long Description ---------------- **Purpose of the consultancy** In the framework of the GAL Secretariat, GRALE 6 Cluster, and GNLC Coordination workplans, UIL is seeking a consultant to 1) contribute to the GRALE 6 survey data collection among Member States; 2) contribute to the development and implementation of the core activities, regular communication and follow up with the GAL and GNLC members; 3) contribute to the organisation and implementation of capacity building workshops, and webinar series; 4) support Team Leaders when required. **Main duties and responsibilities** Under the overall authority of the Director of the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning (UIL, and under the direct supervision of the Team leader of Quality Learning Ecosystems programme (until the end of March 2026) and Team Leader of the Skills Throughout Life Programme and GNLC Coordinator (from April 2026 onwards), the individual consultant will undertake the following main responsibilities: **A. Participate in and prepare detailed minutes of weekly meetings of GRALE 6 Cluster **B. Contribute to the GAL workplan implementation (January - November 2026)** B.1. Prepare monthly reports on the course participation and completion; identify and implement strategies for wider promotion and dissemination of the course B.3. Support the implementation of three learning courses within the GNLC Academy throughout the year C.2.1. Workshop in Dubai - June C.2.2. Workshop in Morocco - September C.2.3. Workshop in Shanghai - October C.3. Coordinate communication with all members of the GNLC **D. Support the organisation the GNLC 2026 Webinar Series (April - December 2026)** Support on the Organisation of six webinars throughout 2026, overseeing all aspects from planning and speaker coordination to technical execution, interpretation, and follow-up communication. D.1. Organise the second webinar in April 2026 D.2. Organise the third webinar in June 2026 D.3. Organise the fourth webinar in August 2026 D.4. Organise the special webinar in September 2026 D.5. Organise the fifth webinar in October 2026 D.6. Organise the sixth webinar in December 2026 **E. Coordinate Progress Reports on learning city development (April – December 2026)** E.1. Support on the design, set up and launch of the online survey to collect progress reports, including communication with all cities involved. E.2. Collect progress reports from all learning cities involved in the process and systematically organize the data for analysis. E.3. Support the development of an analysis document based on the progress reports. **F. Contribute to the preparations of the Seventh International Conference on Learning Cities (ICLC7)** F.1. Prepare application documents and launch the call for applications for host city. F.2. Organize the selection process, including communication with all key stakeholders F.3. Organise the Learning City Award preparations for launching the call for applications **G. Contribute to the administrative work of the programme (April – December 2026)** G.1. Contribute to the preparation, review and ongoing monitoring of project-related documents, including quarterly/annual project reviews. G.2. Assist the programme in preparing and revising budgets in liaison with ADM to ensure approval in timely manner. G.3. Support drafting standard correspondence and presentations for projects/programmes. Long Description ---------------- **List of deliverables** **Deliverables to be submitted by 30 January 2026** - - A.1. postings.text: E T Consultant | World Bank Group Skip to main content E T Consultant World Bank Group Tegucigalpa Both national and international EC3 - Extended Term Consultant Appointment level Speaks English, Spanish Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Bank Group is seeking an Extended Term Consultant to provide environmental and social risk management support for its Honduras program, primarily focusing on the transport sector. The consultant will work under the guidance of a Senior Social Development Specialist and an Environmental Specialist, engaging in tasks such as risk assessment, compliance monitoring, and capacity building for project stakeholders. This role requires strong communication skills in both English and Spanish, as well as a solid understanding of environmental and social standards. The consultant will play a crucial role in ensuring effective project implementation and stakeholder engagement. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in relevant field At least five years of experience in environmental and social risk management Experience with environmental and social assessments Knowledge of World Bank ESF or similar standards Operational experience in Latin America and the Caribbean Excellent communication skills in English and Spanish Strong client orientation and problem-solving skills Willingness to travel within the region E T Consultant Job #: req39338 Organization: World Bank Sector: Social Development Grade: EC3 Term Duration:  0 years 7 months Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment Location: Tegucigalpa,Honduras Required Language(s): English Preferred Language(s): Spanish Closing Date: 11/25/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC Description At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG) , you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector , development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd . The World Bank Group serves 30 client countries in Latin America and the Caribbean Region (LCR). Clients range from large, rapidly growing middle-income clients to IDA countries to small Caribbean states to one fragile state. Despite immense resources, dynamic societies, and an average annual per capita income of about $4,000, deep inequalities persist in most LCR countries, with nearly a quarter of the Region's people living in poverty. The Bank's strategy in LCR is focused on five pillars: (a) stimulating growth and improving competitiveness; (b) reducing poverty and inequality; (c) making governments and institutions work for people; (d) providing a platform for addressing global issues (climate change, gender, trade, disease, migration); and (e) reducing risk, whether from extreme weather events, climate change, crime and violence or other events. Country and Project Context Honduras is Central America’s second-largest country by area and population, home to approximately 11 million people. Its economy is relatively small and open, with agriculture and light manufacturing, especially textiles, serving as important sources of employment and exports. The country’s development continues to be shaped by institutional capacity constraints, implementation challenges, and limited economic diversification, which can influence investment, service delivery, and job creation, and foster emigration. Strengthening public sector effectiveness and improving implementation capacity remain important priorities to accelerate development results. Despite recent progress, Honduras remains one of the poorest countries in Latin America and the Caribbean, with persistent rural deprivation and high levels of inequality. To expand opportunities for the Honduran population, especially the most vulnerable, it is essential to drive stronger economic growth, boost productivity and competitiveness, and foster inclusion by improving access to quality basic services and jobs. Simultaneously, advancing institutional reforms in critical areas such as energy and water sustainability, governance, and the business climate remains vital to ensure long-term resilience and equitable development. The World Bank Group (WBG) supports Honduras in reducing poverty through loans, grants, technical assistance, advisory services, and knowledge sharing. Its strategy aims to build a green, inclusive, and resilient economy by improving human development, promoting job creation, and strengthening resilience to natural hazards. Duties and Accountabilities The World Bank Group is seeking an Extended Term Consultant to provide in-country environmental and social risk management technical support to the Honduras program.  The consultant will be expected to dedicate a majority of their time to projects in the transport sector.  Key responsibilities are listed below.  The Consultant will work under the direction of a Senior Social Development Specialist and an Environmental Specialist. · Identify, assess and monitor environmental and social risks and impacts; advise task teams and clients on proportionate mitigation measures. Provide technical advice to the client for instrument preparation, including environmental and social assessments, management frameworks and plans, stakeholder engagement plans, labor management procedures, resettlement and Indigenous Peoples instruments, grievance mechanisms, occupational and community health and safety plans, among others. · Undertake implementation support, including field missions and site visits as needed; review monitoring reports; identify compliance gaps and emerging risks; agree practical corrective actions with clients and task teams; and follow up on implementation of agreed measures. · Support the design and delivery of capacity building for project implementation units, government counterparts, contractors, supervision consultants, and other stakeholders on environmental and social risk management requirements and practices. ·   Support client communication.  Including communication of Bank requirements to the client, helping to ensure that both the client and the Bank remain on track with agreed-upon commitments and action plans. ·   Assess client implementation readiness and providing support as needed.  This will include reviewing the client's implementation of E&S measures through site visits and provide recommendations on actions to Bank staff. ·   Carry out periodic risk assessments, recommend actions, and carry out follow-on steps as requested by Bank staff.  ·   Perform any other tasks as requested. · Selection Criteria · Advanced degree (Master’s or equivalent) in environmental sciences, engineering, natural resource management, social sciences, anthropology, sociology, development studies, public policy, law, or another field relevant to environmental and social risk management. · At least five years of directly relevant professional experience in environmental and social risk management for development projects. Experience covering both environmental and social dimensions is strongly preferred. · Demonstrated experience preparing, reviewing, or supervising environmental and social assessments and management instruments, and addressing issues such as occupational and community health and safety, biodiversity, pollution prevention, land acquisition and resettlement, Indigenous Peoples, labor, stakeholder engagement, and grievance management. · Sound knowledge and practical experience of the World Bank ESF and/or legacy safeguard policies. Comparable experience with environmental and social standards of another international financial institution is desirable. · Relevant operational experience in Latin America and the Caribbean. · Excellent written and oral communication skills in English and Spanish, including the ability to prepare high-quality technical reports and communicate complex environmental and social issues clearly and effectively. · Strong client orientation, sound judgment, diplomacy, practical problem-solving skills, ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines, and willingness to travel within the region, including to remote areas. · Environmental and Social Risk Management: Demonstrates sound knowledge of environmental and social standards and applies a proportionate risk-based approach across sectors to identifying, assessing, managing, and monitoring E&S risks and impacts across sectors and project stage. · Operational Delivery: Provides timely, practical, and technically sound environmental and social   advice to Task Teams and Management, supporting project preparation, implementation, supervision, and resolution of emerging issues. Client Engagement and Policy Dialogue: Engages effectively with government counterparts, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders, providing clear technical guidance and facilitating constructive dialogue on E&S risk management. · Collaboration and Integration: Works effectively across environmental and social disciplines, sectors, countries, and institutional boundaries. · Knowledge and Capacity Building: Shares knowledge, develops practical guidance, and strengthens client and team capacity through coaching and training. WBG Culture Attributes: 1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders. 2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact. 3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results. Former and current ET staff who have completed or are in the process of completing their third-year ET appointment are not eligible for future ET appointments. This role aims to support aspiring entrepreneurs and youth-led enterprises in the livestock value chains, fostering sustainable income and employment opportunities. The Specialist will guide business development services, strengthen financial capabilities, and develop partnerships with financial service providers. The position requires a strong understanding of enterprise viability and experience in market systems and financing for youth. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree or PhD in relevant field 10 years experience with Master's or 5 years with PhD Experience in enterprise development and incubation Proven experience in financial partnerships and financing for enterprises Strong understanding of cash flow and financing needs Experience adapting support for young women and disadvantaged youth Excellent written and spoken English Experience with large-scale youth entrepreneurship programs POSITION ANNOUNCEMENT – INTERNAL/EXTERNAL Youth Enterprise Development and Inclusive Finance Specialist REF: YEDIF/REAP/025/2026               The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI) seeks to recruit a Youth Enterprise Development and Inclusive Finance Specialist who leads three inter-connected areas of REAP Ethiopia: youth entrepreneurship incubation, market system development , and access to appropriate finance. The role will help aspiring entrepreneurs and existing youth-led and youth-employing enterprises establish, stabilise and grow viable businesses in feed and related livestock value chains, generating sustained income and dignified and fulfilling work. ILRI is a member of the CGIAR, a global research alliance that works to transform food, land and water systems in a climate crisis and is the only CGIAR centre dedicated to addressing multiple development challenges through sustainable livestock solutions. REAP is a five-year multi-country initiative intended to advance education and relieve poverty by enabling 1,000,000 financially disadvantaged young women and men, aged 18 to 35 years, to access new work opportunities in sustainable feed and livestock value chains across the seven countries. The Program will equip young people with technical, entrepreneurial, financial; digital and workplace capabilities linked to real economic opportunities and enable financially disadvantaged young people to access work, finance, productive assets, markets and income-generating opportunities that improve household resilience and wellbeing. Among its participants, the Program shall target 70% young women and at least 5% youth with disabilities and 20,000 refugees and displaced young people. The programme will support youth-led and youth-inclusive enterprises to enter, stabilise and grow in feed and livestock markets; strengthen market systems, services, and commercial relationships; and improve policy, finance, innovation, extension, and other enabling systems required for youth-led enterprises to succeed and generate additional employment opportunities. Across these areas, it applies gender-transformative and inclusive approaches to address restrictive gender and social norms, reduce barriers to young women’s participation, and strengthen their agency, voice, leadership and access to resources and opportunities. Safeguarding measures are embedded throughout the programme to protect young people from harm and support their safe participation. Led by ILRI, the consortium includes ICARDA, IITA, the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, and icipe, working with downstream delivery partners, enterprise-support organisations, financial institutions, government and private sector actors. The Director draws on partners’ expertise in feed and livestock systems, enterprise development, market systems, inclusive finance, digital innovation, policy, and gender and social inclusion to guide country delivery and achieve measurable youth work outcomes, adapting implementation in response to evidence. Working through downstream partners and across the consortium, the postholder will guide incubation and business development services, strengthen financial capability and investment readiness, and develop partnerships with financial service providers to facilitate suitable financing for youth enterprises, in line with REAP’s overall access-to-finance approach. The Specialist will focus on enterprise capability, market opportunity identification, commercial linkages, suitable financing and partner performance, ensuring that youth enterprises respond to demonstrated demand and participate sustainably in feed and livestock market systems. Key Responsibilities: Strategy and country delivery Lead costed country plans for entrepreneurship, incubation and inclusive finance, aligning partner responsibilities and support packages with programme guidance and youth work outcomes. Use market and technical evidence to prioritise viable enterprise models and differentiated support pathways; coordinate consortium inputs and advise the Country Lead on delivery bottlenecks and adaptations. Identify market-system constraints and opportunities affecting youth participation, and translate them into enterprise-development plans that strengthen market access, services, partnerships and financing. Youth entrepreneurship and incubation Guide enterprise profiling and pathway matching based on skills, assets, maturity, constraints and growth potential, aligned with approved financing windows. Ensure support builds practical business capability in costing, pricing, cash flow, records, governance, operations and formalisation, and assess whether enterprises are progressing towards viability beyond programme support. Facilitate sustainable commercial linkages between youth enterprises, buyers, suppliers, processors and other market actors. Develop and validate commercially viable business models and use market evidence to guide their adaptation, scaling or discontinuation. Financial Capability, Investment Readiness and Access to Finance Strengthen enterprises’ financial capability and investment readiness, assess financing needs, and maintain a pipeline of finance-ready enterprises matched to suitable financial products. Identify and engage suitable financial service providers and partners, and develop appropriate financing options, including working capital, leasing, asset finance, value-chain finance and risk-sharing mechanisms. Address financing barriers for young women and underserved youth, and coordinate financing roll-out, referrals and monitoring of uptake, repayment and performance with relevant partners. Inclusive enterprise, market systems and financing pathways Work with gender and inclusion colleagues to address barriers involving collateral, documentation, assets, mobility, care responsibilities, disability and control over income; avoid selection that favours only better-capitalised participants. Embed safeguarding, safe work and participant feedback in enterprise, market systems and finance support, preventing unsuitable debt and excessive risk transfer while promoting agency and sustainable income. Partner leadership and performance Assess incubation, business-development, market systems development and financing partners; define results and quality standards, strengthen capacity, review delivery and recommend corrective action to the Country Lead. Coordinate with feed systems, digital and inclusion teams so enterprise and financing support responds to demonstrated market opportunities and technical requirements. Use enterprise, market system and financing evidence to improve support packages, assess product effectiveness, recommend scaling or discontinuation, and share practical lessons with the country team and programme leads Academic and professional qualifications: Education: Master’s degree or PhD in finance, marketing, agribusiness, business administration, entrepreneurship, economics, agricultural economics, development studies or a related field. postings.text: Programme Policy Officer (Livelihood and Technical Training Specialist)_SC8 based at the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content Programme Policy Officer (Livelihood and Technical Training Specialist)_SC8 based at the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment WFP - World Food Programme Vientiane National SB-4 (SC8/SC9), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement level Speaks English, Lao Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Food Programme is seeking a Programme Policy Officer specializing in Livelihood and Technical Training to support the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment in Laos. The officer will develop training modules, tools, and strategies to empower rural women through livelihood grants and technical skills training. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in livelihoods, sustainable development, or related fields Strong understanding of Laos-specific government structure and agriculture sector Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills At least 3 years of experience in livelihood programs and poverty reduction Experience in developing and managing training modules Experience in climate-resilient livelihoods development Prior experience with international donor-supported projects Fluency in Lao and excellent English skills DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 25 November 2026-23:59-GMT+07:00 Indochina Time (Vientiane) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity.
