ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). Background The Building Resilience and Reducing Rural Poverty Project (BRRRP) is an initiative by the Government of Lao PDR, particularly the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE), in collaboration with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), aimed at addressing food insecurity, rural poverty, and reduce vulnerabilities exacerbated by climate change. It aims to improve the health, resilience, and socioeconomic profile of poor households, particularly women, through a combination of adaptive and shock-responsive social protection measures. The project targets districts in four provinces: Khammouan, Louangphabang, Savannahkhet, and Xaiyabuly, which are characterized by high poverty rates, malnutrition, and climate risks. It combines nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfers (CCT) with an innovative poverty graduation program, aimed to support the most vulnerable populations, particularly poor pregnant women and mothers of young children. Key components of the project include: Output 1: Coverage of shock-responsive and nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfer program expanded. Output 2: Gender-responsive and climate-resilient poverty graduation program piloted. Output 3: Social protection delivery systems and CCT implementation enhanced. Output 4: Institutional capacity for gender-smart and climate-responsive monitoring and evaluation strengthened. Under Output 2 WFP will provide technical support to MAE in the design, implementation, and evaluation of the climate-resilient and gender-responsive poverty graduation program specifically for rural women. The pilot will benefit at least 4,500 rural women as beneficiaries of conditional cash transfer, across four districts in four provinces.  Recognizing the multidimensional nature of poverty and climate vulnerability, the program will offer a holistic set of sequenced, climate-smart, and time-bound interventions tailored for poor women, combining targeted cash transfers with: (i) livelihood grants to pursue climate-resilient and sustainable livelihoods, (ii) technical skills training, (iii) support for financial inclusion, and (iv) social empowerment through psychosocial support, including dedicated coaching and life skills training to promote social inclusion and positive behavior change. The pilot graduation program under Output 2 consists of activities across five poverty graduation pillars (social protection, livelihoods promotion, financial inclusion, social empowerment, coaching & mentorship), in a strategic sequence within 24 months to empower poor women with skills, knowledge, tools, access to resources, livelihoods, and self-confidence to build long-term resilience, particularly to climate shocks. The pilot combines support for immediate needs (with conditional cash transfer) with longer-term investments in training and income generation to build long-term resilience. The position of Livelihood and Technical Training Specialist (national position) is based at the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE) and will be required to periodically report and collaborate with WFP on the progress of implementation. 1. Responsibilities Support the strengthening of institutional and technical capacity of government counterparts by providing specific strategic and technical advisory support to the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment including in the area of nutrition-sensitive and climate-smart agriculture, livelihood approaches, resilience building, and food systems transformation. Thoroughly review the climate resilience and vulnerability assessment and market assessment findings and recommendations, particularly the menu of climate-resilient and sustainable livelihood options recommended for each district and strategies to adapt them to climate change and disaster risks specific to the locations; Support the development of tools related to livelihoods development with specific considerations for poor women with small children and provide training to district level coordinators, coaches, PMU and DRD-PR staff on: 1. Livelihood matching tools to help participants select suitable livelihoods considering the minimum requirements to engage in the livelihood activity, including skills, resources, level of literacy, etc. and considerations to their situation (care responsibilities, customs, etc.) 2. Livelihood plan template that clearly indicates i) selected income-generating activity; ii) rationale for its selection; iii) a detailed list of assets, raw materials, equipment, tools or inputs needed to start or enhance an existing livelihood, and iv) potential diversification strategies. 3. Livelihood grant utilization monitoring as indicated and approved in the livelihood plan within three months of receiving the grant. Support the development or upgrade of training modules and materials related to livelihoods development and ensure that climate resilience and adaptation strategies, and gender considerations (based on the Gender Assessment and Gender Action Plan (GAAP)) are incorporated. Provide inputs and recommendations on relevant indicators, procedures, and tools to ensure regular monitoring of the livelihoods supported and provide support in the analysis of monthly livelihoods monitoring data, including its impacts on climate resilience. Organize Training of Trainers (ToT) for district coordinators and coaches to equip them to deliver training to pilot participants. Identify and recommend partnerships to deliver necessary technical training to pilot participants and leverage existing services. Develop highly contextualized strategies and provide guidance to the district level coordinators, coaches, and DRD-PR staff through in-person training and/or developing Guidance Note(s) to communicate clear and consistent guidance on the following: 1. support pilot participants in purchasing good quality assets, raw materials, equipment, tools or inputs; 2. use of mobile money to access digital financial services wherever possible 3. utilization of second tranche of livelihood grant; 4. strategies to grow and diversify income sources. Support the development of the intensive support initiative in collaboration with the Gender and Social Development Specialist. Support development of tools, training materials, and on-the-job mentoring & training. Oversee documentation and dissemination of best practices, lessons learned, and knowledge products to inform scaling and policy development. Any other duties, as required 2. Qualifications and Experience required Advanced degree in livelihoods, value chains, sustainable development, economics, public policy, or related fields. Strong understanding of Laos-specific context, in terms of the government structure after the restructuring, national and agriculture sector plans and priorities. Excellent analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills. Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, particularly with government institutions and development partners.      At least 3 years of professional experience in livelihood programs, including small and medium-sized enterprises in the context of poverty reduction, social protection, economic inclusion, rural development, and women’s empowerment.      Experience in developing, managing and organizing training modules       Experience in climate-resilient livelihoods development is required.       Must have prior experience working on international donor-supported projects or programs (e.g., UN agencies, IFIs such as IFAD, ADB, World Bank).       Fluency in Lao and excellent writing, speaking and understanding of English required. postings.text: Consultant National pour la Conception et animation de la Master Class Médias « Comprendre et valoriser les données pour mieux informer : une approche sensible au genre » – En marge du Forum Data-Territoires 2026 (Home Based) | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content Consultant National pour la Conception et animation de la Master Class Médias « Comprendre et valoriser les données pour mieux informer : une approche sensible au genre » – En marge du Forum Data-Territoires 2026 (Home Based) UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | Home Based - May require travel National Senior level Application deadline: November 19, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool ONU Femmes Maroc is seeking a national consultant to design and facilitate a Master Class for media professionals focused on understanding and valuing statistical data, particularly gender-sensitive data. The Master Class aims to enhance the participants' ability to interpret, contextualize, and present statistical information accurately. The consultant will work closely with the HCP and will be responsible for creating educational content, interactive exercises, and evaluation tools. This role requires a strong background in journalism, communication, and training, with a focus on gender issues. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in journalism, communication, or related field At least 7 years of experience in journalism, communication, or media training Proven experience in designing and facilitating participatory training Strong analytical skills and ability to simplify statistical information Excellent communication and facilitation skills Fluency in French and Arabic; English is a plus Knowledge of Moroccan media landscape and public statistics Understanding of gender equality issues Background: La production, l'analyse, la diffusion large et l'utilisation de données statistiques détaillées et ventilées, notamment par sexe, sont des conditions essentielles à l'élaboration de politiques publiques ciblées, inclusives et fondées sur des données probantes. Leur appropriation par les acteurs qui les relaient auprès du grand public, en particulier les professionnels des médias, conditionne la qualité du débat public. Dans le cadre de son partenariat avec le Haut-Commissariat au Plan, ONU Femmes Maroc contribue au renforcement de l'intégration de la dimension genre dans la production, l'analyse et la valorisation des statistiques, ainsi qu'au développement d'une culture de la donnée auprès des utilisateurs de la statistique publique. Les médias jouent à cet égard un rôle essentiel dans la diffusion, la compréhension et la mise en perspective de la statistique publique. Or, une donnée statistiquement exacte peut conduire à une information imprécise ou trompeuse lorsqu'elle est mal interprétée, sortie de son contexte conceptuel, comparée à un indicateur mesurant une réalité différente ou présentée sans les précautions méthodologiques nécessaires. Dans ce cadre, le HCP organise, en partenariat avec ONU Femmes Maroc, une Master Class dédiée aux professionnels des médias, en marge du Forum Data-Territoires 2026. Le Forum se veut un espace stratégique de réflexion, d’échange et de collaboration autour des enjeux de la donnée à l’échelle territoriale L’événement l réunira autorités statistiques, producteurs de données, institutions territoriales, décideurs publics, chercheurs et acteurs de l’innovation.  Complémentaire aux panels institutionnels et scientifiques du Forum, la Master Class placée sous le thème « Comprendre et valoriser les données pour mieux informer : une approche sensible au genre  » vise à renforcer les capacités des professionnels des médias à comprendre, interpréter et valoriser les données statistiques, notamment les données ventilées par sexe et territorialisées, tout en préservant la rigueur scientifique de l’information diffusée. À cette fin, ONU Femmes Maroc recrute un.e consultant.e national.e chargé.e de concevoir les contenus et outils pédagogiques et d’animer la Master Class. Le/la consultant.e travaillera sous la supervision du/de l’analyste de projet d'ONU Femmes Maroc, en coordination étroite avec le HCP, et sera appuyé.e par le/la point focal.e Ressources humaines, interlocuteur/trice pour les questions contractuelles et de paiement. Les livrables seront soumis à la validation d'ONU Femmes Maroc. Objectif de la consultation La consultation a pour objectif de concevoir et d'animer une Master Class permettant aux professionnels des médias de renforcer leurs capacités à interpréter, contextualiser et restituer de manière rigoureuse les données statistiques produites par le HCP, notamment les données sensibles au genre et territorialisées. Plus spécifiquement, la Master Class devra permettre aux participant.e.s de : interpréter correctement les principaux indicateurs statistiques et identifier les limites de ce qu’ils permettent d’affirmer ; identifier et éviter les erreurs fréquentes d’interprétation, de comparaison et de présentation des données statistiques ; transformer les données statistiques en contenus journalistiques clairs, rigoureux et accessibles, adaptés aux différents formats médiatiques ; mieux intégrer les données ventilées par sexe et les disparités territoriales dans le traitement médiatique afin de rendre visibles les inégalités entre les femmes et les hommes et d’éviter la reproduction de stéréotypes de genre; renforcer le dialogue entre producteurs de statistiques publiques et professionnels des médias. La formation ciblera notamment les : Journalistes de la presse écrite, audiovisuelle et numérique arabophones et francophones ; Responsables éditoriaux et journalistes spécialisés ; Une équipe identifiée de cadres du HCP appelé à s’approprier l’approche et les outils pédagogiques de la formation en vue de leur duplication dans le cadre de formations ultérieures. Tâches du/de la consultant.e Le/la consultant.e sera responsable de : Concevoir le scénario pédagogique et le programme détaillé de la journée, en séquences de 15 à 30 minutes alternant quiz interactifs, simulations, études de cas, jeux de rôles, travaux de groupe et débriefs ; les notions statistiques seront introduites à partir des choix, erreurs et questionnements observés pendant les exercices ; Élaborer les cas pratiques, exercices et supports d'animation, construits prioritairement à partir de publications, tableaux et indicateurs récents du HCP sur les thématiques à convenir avec l'expert.e métier du HCP et avec l'appui d'ONU Femmes Maroc pour la dimension genre. Les exercices devront mobiliser une diversité de formats et de supports de communication (notamment article web, dépêche, reportage, interview, radio, télévision, réseaux sociaux et infographie/data visualisation), afin de mettre en pratique l’adaptation de l’analyse et de la présentation des statistiques aux spécificités de chaque format et de chaque public ; Animer la Master Class : constitution d'équipes de 4 à 6 participant.e.s en « mini-rédactions », dynamique de challenge entre équipes, utilisation d'outils de vote interactif, coaching des groupes et débriefs systématiques associant regard éditorial, expertise statistique du HCP et, pour les cas concernés, lecture orientée genre; Concevoir et administrer les outils d'évaluation de la journée (tests de positionnement en début et en fin de journée, questionnaire de satisfaction ; Produire une fiche de bonnes pratiques à l'intention des journalistes et le rapport final de la mission; Produire un guide de formation complet et animer une demi-journée de formation à l’attention des cadres du HCP, afin d’assurer le transfert de compétences et de leur permettre de reproduire la formation de manière autonome dans d’autres régions. Le/la consultant.e devra concevoir et animer une journée de formation participative, pensée comme une expérience pratique plutôt que comme une succession de présentations théoriques : les participant.e.s seront placé.e.s face à des situations proches de leur pratique professionnelle (interpréter un chiffre, choisir un angle, proposer un titre, détecter une mauvaise comparaison, corriger un extrait d'article, réviser une lecture à la lumière de nouvelles données). Des études de cas seront développées en concertation avec le HCP, en fonction des données disponibles et adaptées aux objectifs de la formation. Les thématiques qui seront utilisées comme cas d’usage avec une perspective genre seront convenues entre le HCP, ONU-Femmes et le consultant lors du développement du contenu du cours. Le contenu définitif et le séquençage de la Master Class seront proposés par le/la consultant.e et finalisés en concertation avec ONU Femmes Maroc et le HCP.  À titre indicatif, la journée pourra s’articuler autour des deux sessions (ou axes) suivants : Session 1 - Comprendre les statistiques officielles : notions de base et bonnes pratiques d'interprétation et lecture sensible au genre Objectifs : Comprendre les principes fondamentaux de la statistique officielle ; Savoir interpréter correctement les principaux indicateurs produits par le HCP ; Identifier les erreurs d'interprétation les plus fréquentes dans le traitement médiatique des données. Session 2 -  Des chiffres au récit : utiliser les données sensibles au genre pour éclairer les politiques territoriales Objectifs : Comprendre ce que les données sensibles au genre disent d’un territoire pour mieux rendre compte des politiques publiques locales. Savoir repérer, dans les rapports et les tableaux de bord, les indicateurs utiles pour éclairer les écarts entre les femmes et les hommes dans un territoire. Développer une lecture critique des résultats présentés dans les rapports et tableaux de bord. Contenu : Du chiffre à la décision publique : comment les données éclairent les politiques territoriales ; Indicateurs de suivi et d'évaluation des politiques de développement intégrant la dimension de genre ; Mesure des disparités territoriales et des écarts entre femmes et hommes ;  Principes d'une couverture médiatique sensible au genre : langage, représentation, choix des sources et des visuels; Études de cas fondées sur des publications et tableaux de bord du HCP et sur des productions d'ONU Femmes. Livrables Livrable Charge de travail estimée (en jours) Livrable 1 Note de cadrage, scénario pédagogique et programme détaillé de la Master Class (séquences, durées, méthodes, répartition des rôles entre consultant.e, expert.e du HCP et ONU Femmes Maroc) 2 Livrable 2 Kit pédagogique et d'animation : cas pratiques fondés sur les données du HCP, quiz interactifs, simulations et jeux de rôles, supports de présentation et guide d'animation 5 Livrable 3 Animation de la Master Class le 14 décembre 2026 à Tanger (de 09h30 à 16h30), y compris la préparation sur site 1 Livrable 4 Outils d'évaluation : tests de positionnement en début et en fin de journée et questionnaire de satisfaction 1 Livrable 5 Rapport final incluant la synthèse de la journée, les résultats des évaluations et leur analyse, les enseignements tirés et des recommandations pour de futures éditions, accompagné de la fiche de bonnes pratiques à l'intention des journalistes 2 Livrable 6  Production d’un guide de formation complet afin d’assurer le transfert de compétences aux cadres internes du HCP, de sorte qu’ils puissent reproduire la formation de manière autonome dans d’autres régions et animation d’une demi-journée de formation à destination des cadres du HCP  2 Calendrier La mission couvrira un maximum de 13 jours de travail, répartis entre début novembre et fin décembre 2026.  Lieu de travail et déplacements La consultance s'effectue à distance (home-based). Plusieurs réunions de cadrage et de travail visant à préparer le contenu de la formation seront prévues en présentiel (au siège du HCP) après concertation avec les parties prenantes. Une mission en présentiel d'une jour

postings.text: E T Consultant | World Bank Group Skip to main content E T Consultant World Bank Group San Salvador, Santo Domingo Both national and international EC3 - Extended Term Consultant Appointment level Speaks English, Spanish Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Bank is seeking an Extended Term Consultant (ETC) to serve as an Environmental and Social Specialist in Central America and the Dominican Republic. The role involves providing technical and operational support for environmental and social risk management throughout project preparation and implementation. The ETC will work closely with task teams and clients to ensure compliance with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework and associated policies. This position aims to enhance portfolio delivery and promote sustainable practices in investment operations. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in relevant field At least five years of experience in environmental and social risk management Experience with environmental and social assessments Knowledge of World Bank ESF and safeguard policies Operational experience in Latin America and the Caribbean Excellent communication skills in English and Spanish Strong client orientation and problem-solving skills Ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines E T Consultant Job #: req39335 Organization: World Bank Sector: Environment Grade: EC3 Term Duration:  0 years 7 months Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment Location: San Salvador,El Salvador Required Language(s): English Preferred Language(s): Spanish Closing Date: 11/25/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC Description At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG) , you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector , development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd . The World Bank's Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) Region supports a diverse portfolio of investment operations across multiple sectors, requiring effective management of environmental and social (E&S) risks and impacts throughout project preparation and implementation. This work is guided by the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable safeguard policies, the World Bank Group Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, and relevant Good International Industry Practice (GIIP). To support the operational demand of its portfolio, the World Bank is seeking an Extended Term Consultant (ETC) to serve as an Environmental and Social Specialist, primarily supporting the LC2 Country Management Unit (CMU), which covers Central America and the Dominican Republic, with potential assignments in LC3 depending on operational needs. The ETC will provide technical and operational support operations in preparation and implementation across sectors, including E&S due diligence, risk management, supervision, and capacity building for implementing agencies. The assignment is intended to strengthen portfolio delivery through integrated environmental and social due diligence, implementation support, client capacity building, and timely advice to task teams and management through the end of FY27. Duties and Accountabilities: ·  Serve as the assigned or supporting Environmental and Social Specialist for selected operations in Central America, and potentially in the Caribbean (including IPFs and P4Rs), applying the ESF, legacy safeguards where relevant, and associated World Bank requirements throughout project preparation and implementation. · Identify, assess and monitor environmental and social risks and impacts; advise task teams and clients on proportionate mitigation measures. Review instruments such as environmental and social assessments, management frameworks and plans, stakeholder engagement plans, labor management procedures, resettlement and Indigenous Peoples instruments, grievance mechanisms, occupational and community health and safety plans, among others. · Prepare and provide timely inputs to Bank operational documents and systems both during preparation and implementation, including Environmental and Social Review Summaries, Environmental and Social Commitment Plans, Project Appraisal Documents or Project Papers, Aide Memoires, Implementation Status and Results Reports, and relevant environmental and social risk management databases. · Undertake implementation support, including field missions and site visits as needed; review monitoring reports; identify compliance gaps and emerging risks; agree practical corrective actions with clients and task teams; and follow up on implementation of agreed measures. · Identify opportunities to integrate sound environmental and/or social management practices in investment operations to promote environmental and social sustainability, climate-smartness and positive environmental and social impacts (benefits) and enhance local capacities for implementing sound environmental and social management practices · Advise clients on incorporating environmental and social requirements into bidding and contract documents and on establishing effective contractor, supervision, monitoring, incident-reporting, and grievance-management arrangements. · Design and deliver hands-on capacity building for project implementation units, government counterparts, contractors, supervision consultants, and other stakeholders on environmental and social risk management requirements and practices. · Support the Environmental and Social (E&S) CMU focal points for Central America and, as requested, for the Caribbean in conducting  portfolio reviews, quality enhancement, strategic briefings, cross-country knowledge exchange, and other priority tasks responding to evolving work-program needs. · In the case of PforRs, develop the corresponding Environmental and Social Systems Assessments (ESSASs), and thereafter supervise the E&S aspects of such PforRs. ·Carry out other assigned tasks related to the broad objectives of the unit, as needed. Note: This vacancy announcement is for one position posted across two possible duty stations that includes El Salvador and Dominican Republic . The selected candidate's duty station will be determined based on organizational requirements and business needs.  Selection Criteria · Advanced degree (Master’s or equivalent) in environmental sciences, engineering, natural resource management, social sciences, anthropology, sociology, development studies, public policy, law, or another field relevant to environmental and social risk management. · At least five years of directly relevant professional experience in environmental and social risk management for development projects. Experience covering both environmental and social dimensions is strongly preferred. · Demonstrated experience preparing, reviewing, or supervising environmental and social assessments and management instruments, and addressing issues such as occupational and community health and safety, biodiversity, pollution prevention, land acquisition and resettlement, Indigenous Peoples, labor, stakeholder engagement, and grievance management. · Sound knowledge and practical experience of the World Bank ESF and/or legacy safeguard policies. Comparable experience with environmental and social standards of another international financial institution is desirable. · Relevant operational experience in Latin America and the Caribbean, preferably in Central America, the Dominican Republic, and/or the Caribbean 3 countries, including familiarity with country environmental and social institutions and regulatory frameworks. · Excellent written and oral communication skills in English and Spanish, including the ability to prepare high-quality technical reports and communicate complex environmental and social issues clearly and effectively. ·Strong client orientation, sound judgment, diplomacy, practical problem-solving skills, ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines, and willingness to travel within the region, including to remote areas. · Environmental and Social Risk Management: Demonstrates sound knowledge of environmental and social standards and applies a proportionate risk based approach across sectors to identifying, assessing, managing, and monitoring E&S risks and impacts across sectors and project stage. · Operational Delivery: Provides timely, practical, and technically sound environmental and social   advice to Task Teams and Management, supporting project preparation, implementation, supervision, and resolution of emerging issues. Client Engagement and Policy Dialogue: Engages effectively with government counterparts, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders, providing clear technical guidance and facilitating constructive dialogue on E&S risk management.. · Collaboration and Integration: Works effectively across environmental and social disciplines, sectors, countries, and institutional boundaries. · Knowledge and Capacity Building: Shares knowledge, develops practical guidance, and strengthens client and team capacity through coaching and training. WBG Culture Attributes: 1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders. 2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact. 3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results. postings.text: Working Group and Research Coordinator | UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Skip to main content Working Group and Research Coordinator UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Khartoum Middle level Speaks Arabic, English Application deadline: November 18, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Working Group and Research Coordinator will support the effective functioning and sustainability of the Local Education Group's Technical Working Groups (TWGs) in Sudan. This role involves managing day-to-day operations, facilitating coordination among stakeholders, and ensuring contributions to the Transitional Education Plan (TEP) implementation and monitoring. The consultant will also coordinate research activities and maintain documentation to inform sector dialogue and decision-making. The position requires strong project management skills and a deep understanding of the education sector. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in Education or related field 5+ years in education sector coordination Experience with Local Education Groups Strong project management skills Fluency in Arabic and English Working Group and Research Coordinator JOB DETAILS Type of contract : Consultancy   Level : Middle Hiring Unit : Education Duty Station : Khartoum Work location : On site Duration of contract : 11 months Hiring open to : Internal and External candidates. Application deadline (Midnight UTC+2 Time) : 18.11.2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism BACKGROUND/OVERVIEW Sudan’s education sector continues to operate in a complex and rapidly evolving context, requiring sustained coordination among national authorities, development partners, UN agencies, civil society organizations and other education stakeholders. Within this environment, maintaining a common framework for sector priorities, coordinated planning and policy dialogue is essential to ensure that available resources and technical support contribute coherently to national education objectives. The Sudan Transitional Education Plan (TEP) 2025–2027 provides this overarching framework, establishing agreed priorities for the education sector and guiding collective efforts towards maintaining access to education, improving teaching and learning, and strengthening the capacity and resilience of the education system. It also provides an important basis for aligning partner interventions, monitoring sector progress and identifying areas requiring further technical and policy attention. The Local Education Group (LEG) serves as the principal sector coordination and dialogue platform supporting this process. It brings together key education stakeholders to promote alignment around national priorities, facilitate information sharing and consultation, review progress and challenges, and strengthen coordination between government and education partners. Through its technical structures and engagement with sector partners, the LEG supports collective oversight of TEP implementation and provides a platform through which technical evidence and sector priorities can inform strategic dialogue and decision-making. PROJECT BACKGROUND UNESCO OFFICE The UNESCO Sudan Office supports national efforts to advance education, science, culture, communication and information in line with UNESCO’s mandate and national development priorities. Working closely with government institutions, UN agencies, development partners and civil society, the Office provides technical assistance, supports capacity development, promotes policy dialogue and facilitates coordination in UNESCO’s areas of competence. In the education sector, UNESCO works closely with the national education authorities and sector partners to support education planning, policy development, system strengthening and institutional capacity development. Particular attention is given to strengthening sector coordination, education data and planning, teacher development, inclusive and equitable education, alternative learning pathways, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and evidence-informed decision-making. In the current context, UNESCO also plays an important role in supporting coordinated implementation and monitoring of national education priorities through the TEP and the LEG. CONSULTANCY RATIONALE/SCOPE OF THE CONSULATNCY PROJECT BACKGROUND  The Sudan Transitional  Education Programme (TEP) 2025–2027 serves as the primary strategic framework for advancing national education priorities, strengthening sector policy dialogue, and supporting system-level reforms. It provides an overarching framework for coordinating and monitoring priority interventions and for promoting greater alignment among government, development partners and other education stakeholders. The System Capacity Grant (SCG) complements the TEP by providing targeted support to strengthen institutional capacities, technical mechanisms and coordination structures required for effective implementation of sector priorities. Within this framework, the Local Education Group (LEG) Technical Working Groups (TWGs) provide important technical platforms for translating sector priorities into coordinated technical action. The TWGs contribute to the implementation and monitoring of the TEP, facilitate technical dialogue and collaboration among relevant stakeholders, and support research and evidence generation to inform policy and sector decision-making. They also provide an important link between specialized technical work and the broader strategic dialogue and coordination undertaken through the LEG. The consultancy will provide dedicated coordination, research and technical support to strengthen the effective functioning and sustainability of the TWGs. This will include facilitating coordination within and across the Working Groups, strengthening their linkages with the LEG, supporting their contributions to TEP implementation and monitoring, and coordinating relevant research and evidence-generation activities. The consultancy will also support relevant SCG-funded activities and help ensure that TWG technical outputs, evidence and recommendations are systematically documented, followed up and used to inform sector dialogue and decision-making. CONSULTANCY RATIONALE/SCOPE OF THE CONSULTANCY This consultancy will support the effective functioning, coordination, and sustainability of the LEG Technical Working Groups (TWGs), ensuring that they serve as effective technical mechanisms for advancing TEP implementation, research and evidence generation, implementation of relevant SCG activities, and sector policy dialogue. The consultancy will strengthen linkages between the TWGs and the LEG, promote collaboration across Working Groups, and ensure that their work and outputs contribute effectively to TEP implementation, monitoring, research, policy development, and sector-level decision-making. Long Description CONSULTANCY OBJECTIVES Under the overall authority of the Head of UNESCO Office in Sudan and the direct supervision of the Head of Education Programme, and in close coordination with LEG Coordinator, the consultant should support the effective functioning, coordination, and sustainability of the LEG Technical Working Groups and strengthen their contribution to TEP implementation, monitoring, research and evidence generation, SCG activities, and sector policy dialogue. The specific tasks of Consultancy would include: T1: Manage day-to-day TWG operations, including workplans, meeting schedules, agendas, facilitation, documentation, visibility and continuous follow-up with focal points and members. T2: Strengthen cross-TWG coordination and linkages with the LEG; streamline TWG outputs and recommendations for LEG consideration and follow up on relevant LEG decisions. T3: Coordinate TWG contributions to TEP implementation, monitoring and review, including follow-up on activities and indicators, technical inputs, review processes, and sector consultations. T4: Coordinate research and evidence generation, establish and operationalize the National Research Group, support relevant SCG activities, facilitate technical follow-up on priority areas, and maintain documentation, trackers, knowledge products, and periodic reporting. Deliverable: A Monthly Technical Working Groups Coordination and Progress Report. The monthly report will cover the status of TWG meetings, workplans and action points; progress against TWG priorities and activities; and TWG contributions to TEP implementation and monitoring, and any recommendations for improvements. It will also cover research and evidence-generation activities, the National Research Group and researcher collaborations; relevant SCG-supported activities; cross-TWG coordination and inputs to the LEG; and technical products completed during the month. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration   Project Context and Scope IOM in the Republic of Moldova is implementing the “Reducing community-level vulnerabilities to TIP in Moldova” project, which supports national efforts to strengthen the protection of and assistance to victims of crime, including victims of trafficking in human beings. MLSP has a central role in the development and coordination of the NRMV. Effective implementation requires a clear legal and institutional framework, practical referral and case-management arrangements, and coordinated action by central and local authorities, multidisciplinary teams, service providers and civil society organisations. In this context, the consultancy will provide targeted support to MLSP to review selected aspects of NRMV implementation and identify feasible measures for improvement. The review will consider, as relevant, the functioning of the multidisciplinary approach, referral and case management for victims of trafficking and other victims of crime, the roles of specialists at local level, coordination between central and local actors, access to specialised services, and consistency with applicable EU, regional and international standards. You have: Advanced university degree (master’s or higher) in education policy, economics, public administration, social sciences, or related fields. Proven experience in developing costed implementation plans, strategies, or action frameworks for education systems or public sector reforms. Partner --> AI Application Assistant: Maximize your UN job search. AI Application Assistant Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Education Sector (ED) Duty Station: Multiple Job Family: Education Type of contract : Non Staff Duration of contract : From 1 to 6 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Duty Station Time) : 11-JAN-2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **OVERVIEW OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THE POST** ----------------------------------------- **Background** In recent years, teacher shortages in Ireland’s public education system have worsened. Various factors may be contributing to the shortages. Despite efforts to address the issue, teacher shortages persist, and there is still no clear consensus among Irish educational stakeholders regarding their causes or the most effective solutions. The project **‘Strategic Workforce Planning for Teachers in Ireland’** aims to fill in this gap. It began in August 2024 and will be implemented for two years until August 2026. It is implemented by UNESCO, in cooperation with the Department of Education and Youth and the European Commission and it is funded by the European Union via the Technical Support Instrument. It aims to achieve the following outcomes: a) Enhanced consensus among relevant stakeholders regarding challenges to the teaching profession and measures to improve the teacher workforce planning in Ireland; b) The results of the project will be used by the Department of Education and Youth to develop a strategy on the improvement of teacher workforce planning. In the long-term and in combination with other related efforts, the project intends to contribute to even further enhancing the status and attractiveness of the teaching profession and reducing teacher shortages in Ireland. As part of the ongoing project activities, a **diagnostic review** was conducted to examine the main factors contributing to teacher shortages in Ireland. It explored multiple interrelated causes and provided an in-depth analysis across different school types. Building on this analysis, the project undertook a **review of EU and international best practices** to identify effective policy responses to teacher shortages. This phase presented case studies of countries facing similar challenges, analysing the measures they introduced, and the outcomes achieved. Following this, a **peer learning workshop** was carried out, during which Irish stakeholders - including government departments, teacher education institutions, school management bodies, and teacher unions - examined the international examples and discussed their relevance to the Irish context. These steps have culminated in a set of evidence-based policy **recommendations** to improve the recruitment, deployment, retention, and professional development of teachers in Ireland. Building on the previous phases, the next stage of the project focuses on translating the agreed recommendations into a feasible, clear, and actionable **costed implementation roadmap**. The roadmap will serve as a practical tool for the Department of Education and Youth to move from analysis to implementation by setting out clear actions, responsibilities, timelines, indicative costs, and monitoring mechanisms. It will also identify potential funding sources and outline governance mechanisms. Long Description ---------------- **Objectives** The purpose of this consultancy is to develop a costed implementation roadmap that operationalises the project’s recommendations into a coherent, feasible, and well-resourced plan for action. This roadmap (15–30 pages) will be based on desk research, stakeholder consultations, and validation meetings with the project’s Working Group (WG) and Advisory Group (AG). Long Description ---------------- **Specific tasks** Under the supervision of UNESCO and in close collaboration with the Department of Education and Youth, the European Commission (SG REFORM), and the project Working and Advisory Groups, the consultant will undertake the following tasks: **Task 1. Review and synthesis** - Review key project outputs, including the diagnostic analysis, the best practice review, and recommendations. - Analyse relevant Irish policy frameworks, teacher workforce data, and financial mechanisms to ensure that roadmap is feasible, cost-effective, and aligned with national priorities. - Map potential synergies with ongoing national or EU-funded initiatives related to education workforce planning and teacher development. **Task 2. Draft costed implementation roadmap** - Prepare a structured draft roadmap (15–30 pages) presenting: (i) concrete measures to enhance teacher workforce planning; (ii) a timeline for their implementation; (iii) a list of stakeholders involved in their implementation together with specific roles; (iv) governance proposals; (v) indicators and a monitoring system; (vi) estimations of human and financial resources and proposals for financing sources. - Ensure that the roadmap reflects the Irish education context, aligns with national policy priorities, and integrates inputs from the project’s prior stages. - Present findings in a clear, results-oriented, and actionable format suitable for policy use. **Task 3. Validation and finalisation** - Present the draft roadmap to the Advisory Group and Working Group in an online consultation meeting. - Consolidate and analyse feedback from UNESCO, the Department of Education and Youth, the European Commission (SG REFORM), and both Groups. - Submit the final version of the costed implementation roadmap. **Deliverables and timeline** **Deliverable** **Description** **Indicative deadline** Inception note 2–3-page note outlining understanding, methodology, and workplan. February 16th, 2026 Draft costed implementation roadmap 15-20 pages, including proposed measures, governance, costing, resources, timeline, and indicators. March 23rd, 2026 Final costed implementation roadmap Revised and approved final version. PowerPoint presentation of the roadmap for the Advisory Group and Working Group online consultation meeting. April 20th, 2026 **COMPETENCIES (Core / Managerial)** ------------------------------------ Professionalism (C) **-** ----- For detailed information, please consult the [UNESCO Competency Framework](https://en.unesco.org/sites/default/files/competency_framework_e.pdf). **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** --------------------------- **Education** - Advanced university degree (master’s or higher) in **education policy, economics, public administration, social sciences, or related fields****.** **Professional experience** - At least **5-7 years of professional experience** in **education sector planning, workforce planning, or policy development****.** - Proven experience in **developing costed implementation plans, strategies, or action frameworks** for education systems or public sector reforms. - Demonstrated ability to conduct **financial estimation, costing, and resource analysis**. - Experience in engaging with **government ministries, education authorities, and international organisations****.** - Familiarity with **EU-funded projects** and **education system governance** is an asset. - Knowledge of the **Irish education system** or comparable European contexts is desirable. **Skills and competencies** - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. - Excellent drafting and synthesis skills in **English****.** - Ability to synthesise complex technical information into clear, actionable policy recommendations. - Strong interpersonal skills. - Capacity to deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines. Long Description ---------------- **SELECTION AND RECRUITMENT PROCESS** ------------------------------------- ***APPLICATION PROCESS*** ***Procedure*** *Interested candidates will need to submit one consolidated PDF document in the place of “Employment History Form”which includes the following information:* - *A short description, two to three pages only, explaining the approach proposed for completing the expected scope of work.* - *A financial proposal, one page only, for delivering the activities described in the call;* - *A short CV, focusing on previous relevant working experience, consultancy assignments and deliverables and relevant expertise to the scope of work.* *The full proposal should not exceed 7 pages. Proposals missing any of the above will not be considered.* *The complete application shall be submitted on or before **23:59 CET, 11 January 2026**. Please note that only pre-selected candidates will be contacted.* Please note that all candidates must complete an on-line application and provide complete and accurate information. To apply, please visit the [UNESCO careers website.](https://careers.unesco.org/careersection/2/joblist.ftl) No modifications can be made to the application submitted. This consultancy is for an International Expert who can provide dual leadership: • For CMDA: Support technical and project coordination, hydrogeological assessments and conceptual model development for Output 1.1 (Assessment of groundwater resources, recharge and extraction dynamics). • For AF GRG: Support technical and project coordination, hydrogeological conceptual modelling, and reporting tasks to ensure timely delivery of climate resilience outputs. The expert will conduct a review of relevant legislation and procedures, analyze anonymized trafficking cases, and engage with stakeholders to identify gaps and propose recommendations. This consultancy involves collaboration with a Supporting Legal Expert and requires strong legal expertise in trafficking and victims' rights. The position is based in Chisinau and is expected to last up to 10 working days. Candidate Requirements: University degree in law At least seven years of relevant legal experience Experience with trafficking in human beings and victims' rights Proven legal analysis and drafting skills Fluency in Romanian and English Experience working with public authorities and civil society Strong communication and coordination skills Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration   Project Context and Scope IOM in the Republic of Moldova is implementing the “Reducing community-level vulnerabilities to TIP in Moldova” project, which supports national efforts to strengthen the protection of and assistance to victims of crime, including victims of trafficking in human beings. Access to identity, civil-status, travel, residence and other relevant documents can be essential for victims of trafficking to exercise their rights and access protection, assistance, justice and longer-term recovery support. In practice, documentation may involve several institutions and may be complicated by missing or expired documents, uncertainty regarding identity or residence status, procedural requirements, unclear institutional responsibilities or the specific protection circumstances of a victim. MLSP, as the main beneficiary of this assignment and a key institution in the protection and referral system, requires a concise evidence base on the main documentation bottlenecks and possible avenues for resolving them. The assignment will combine a targeted legal and procedural review with analysis of selected anonymised cases and interviews with relevant stakeholders. It will document priority gaps and propose realistic next steps and a practical roadmap for MLSP-led dialogue and advocacy with the Public Services Agency, the Ministry of Justice and other competent institutions. Two separate but complementary consultancy positions will be issued: one Lead Legal Expert and one Supporting Legal Expert. Both experts will work as a team, while remaining individually contracted for up to 10 working days each. The scope and division of work will be agreed with MLSP and IOM at inception and may be adapted within the available working days.   Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing   Protection Unit of IOM in the Republic of Moldova; “Reducing community-level vulnerabilities to TIP in Moldova” Project. Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract The overall objective is to support MLSP in identifying and addressing priority legal and practical barriers related to the documentation of victims of trafficking in persons. Under the overall supervision of the IOM Program Coordinator and in close coordination with the other expert, MLSP, the expert will undertake the following: • Agree on the priority documentation issues, methodology, institutions to be consulted, selected cases or scenarios and division of responsibilities. • Conduct a targeted review of relevant legislation, regulations, administrative procedures, guidance and available materials concerning identity, civil status, residence, migration, travel and other documentation relevant to victims of trafficking.  • Analyse a limited selection of anonymised trafficking cases or case scenarios to identify recurring legal and procedural barriers and their consequences for victims. • Conduct targeted interviews or consultations with relevant stakeholders, which may include MLSP, the Public Services Agency, the Ministry of Justice, migration and law-enforcement authorities, prosecutors, courts, civil-status bodies, consular actors, legal aid providers, specialised services and civil society organisations. • Document priority legal, administrative, coordination and implementation gaps, including issues affecting Moldovan nationals, foreign victims and persons unable to obtain documents through ordinary procedures. • Help distinguish issues that may be addressed through coordination, administrative practice or guidance from those that may require regulatory or legislative action. • Contribute to concise, prioritised recommendations and a practical roadmap for MLSP, indicating suggested follow-up actions, institutions to be engaged and an indicative sequence for inter-institutional dialogue and advocacy. • Present and discuss preliminary findings with MLSP, IOM and selected stakeholders through a focused validation meeting or workshop and incorporate relevant feedback. • Lead the overall analysis and coordinate the work of the Supporting Legal Expert, including allocation of tasks, consolidation of inputs and resolution of substantive gaps or inconsistencies. • Take primary responsibility for drafting, quality assurance, finalisation and timely submission of the joint inception note, preliminary gap analysis, validation materials, final report and MLSP roadmap. MLSP and IOM may adjust the focus and level of detail during inception, within the available 10 working days and without changing the overall objective of the assignment. The deliverables will be prepared jointly or in a coordinated manner with the Supporting Legal Expert. Purpose of consultancy To support the Country Support and Project Management Group (CSP) in following up on and documenting progress on the recommendations of the Fifth Regional Forum of WHO Collaborating Centres in the Western Pacific, including refining the action plan, tracking progress and achievements, improving monitoring and reporting, strengthening the visibility of WHOCC contributions, and supporting preparations for the next Regional Forum. Background The Fifth Regional Forum of WHO Collaborating Centres in the Western Pacific, held in November 2025, identified key recommendations to strengthen collaboration, coordination, visibility, technical cooperation, and alignment of WHOCC activities with regional and country priorities. Following the Forum, a draft action plan was developed, and several follow-up activities have been initiated. As the Region moves towards the next Regional Forum in 2027, there is a need to review progress against the action plan, document achievements and lessons learned, and identify remaining gaps and priorities. WHO therefore seeks consultancy support to refine the action plan, improve how progress is monitored and reported, and strengthen the visibility and communication of WHOCC contributions and progress made in following up on the Forum recommendations. Deliverables The selected consultant will support CSP in following up on the recommendations of the Fifth Regional Forum of WHO Collaborating Centres in the Western Pacific. The consultant will review progress against the draft action plan, consult with relevant WPRO divisions, country offices and selected WHOCCs, and refine the action plan by clarifying actions, timelines, responsibilities, milestones and indicators. The consultant will develop practical tools for monitoring, reporting and tracking progress; document achievements, challenges and lessons learned; gather feedback from relevant stakeholders; and recommend ways to improve the visibility and communication of WHOCC contributions. The consultant will also prepare a final package of the refined action plan and related monitoring and reporting tools to support continued follow-up and preparations for the next Regional Forum. Method(s) to carry out the activity The work will be carried out under the direct supervision of the Executive Officer and the Coordinator, CSP, and in collaboration with relevant WPRO divisions, country offices and WHOCCs. The consultant will review relevant documents, consult with relevant stakeholders, and participate in meetings and discussions. Draft outputs will be revised based on feedback received. The consultant will prepare a technical reference manual and a learning guide, focusing on macroeconomic effects of various shocks. Responsibilities include model specification, documentation, and collaboration with UN ESCWA staff. The role requires advanced proficiency in Python and extensive experience in macroeconomic analysis and modeling. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in economics or related field 15 years of professional experience in macroeconomic analysis Experience in developing and calibrating Quarterly Projection Models Proficiency in Python for macroeconomic modeling Experience in documenting macroeconomic models Publication in reputed journals Result of Service Develop a QPM calibrated to Jordan as the common application and its replication to Morocco. The applications will include macroeconomic effects of the shocks such as food prices, oil prices, exchange rates, interest rates, remittances and fiscal shocks as relevant. The assignment will deliver two complementary resources: a technical reference manual for maintaining and extending the model, and an example-based learning guide for using it with economic judgment. Work Location Remote Expected duration 2 months Duties and Responsibilities Background: Sound and timely forecasting and policy analysis have become more important than ever for governments and central banks in the Arab region, which are frequently exposed to external shocks such as swings in food and oil prices, changes in global financial conditions and fluctuations in remittance flows. Assessing how such shocks are transmitted to growth, inflation, the exchange rate and interest rates, and designing appropriate policy responses, requires analytical frameworks that are internally consistent and transparent, and economists able to apply them with sound judgment. The challenge is more pressing for countries with limited policy space and high debt service burdens, where policy errors are costly. Against this background, ESCWA is strengthening capacity to use model-based frameworks for short- and medium-term forecasting and policy simulations. A Quarterly Projection Model (QPM) complements this annual macro-fiscal framework. As a semi-structural, quarterly gap model of the type widely used in central bank forecasting and policy analysis systems, the QPM focuses on near-term dynamics, including the output gap, inflation, the exchange rate and interest rates, and on the transmission of external shocks and policy decisions. It also provides a consistent framework for bringing short-term indicators, nowcasts and expert judgment into the forecast. Duties and Responsibilities: The consultant will work in close cooperation with the delegated staff member under the overall supervision of the Cluster Leader of the Shared Economic Prosperity. The consultant will undertake the following tasks: • Prepare an inception note confirming the model specification, data feasibility, deliverable sequence and timetable before implementation. • Prepare a QPM calibrated to Jordan and a reproducible baseline forecast, and document the model structure, equations, data, calibration and solution in close cooperation with UN ESCWA staff. All code shall be written in Python and shall rely exclusively on free-of-charge, open-source packages distributed under licences that permit use, modification and redistribution. • Document how the framework is used in practice, covering the forecasting cycle, the recording of judgment, policy simulations, model maintenance and extensions as evidence and policy needs evolve, in close collaboration with UN ESCWA staff. • Develop a practical learning guide built on numerous worked examples, following the approach set out below, including the four required shock applications. • Prepare a data inventory and a replication package in Python that allows all reported outputs to be recreated. • Address ESCWA’s consolidated technical comments on each draft deliverable and carry out the final replication checks. Working arrangements: The consultant will prepare the model for Jordan first, the applications and the guides, and respond to consolidated technical comments. ESCWA will nominate a focal point, confirm the intended audience and priority applications, and coordinate the review. The proposed sequence of work is: (i) inception and data review; (ii) model and baseline preparation; (iii) worked examples and draft guides; and (iv) technical review and final replication checks. ESCWA shall provide one consolidated set of written technical comments on each draft deliverable. ESCWA team will replicate the application for Morocco using the technical manual and share it with the consultant for validation including the comments. The consultant shall address the comments within the agreed scope and finalise the models for Jordan and Morocco and the technical guides. Qualifications/special skills A Master’s degree in economics, econometrics or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. A minimum of 15 years of professional work experience in macroeconomic analysis, modelling and forecasting is required, including hands-on experience in developing, calibrating and operating Quarterly Projection Models or similar semi-structural models for forecasting and policy analysis at a central bank, ministry of finance or international financial institution. Experience in documenting macroeconomic models and preparing technical manuals, training or learning materials for economists is required. Publication in reputed journals in this field is required. Advanced proficiency in Python for macroeconomic modelling, including writing documented and reproducible code, is required. Experience with model-solution and forecasting toolkits (for example, Dynare or Python-based equivalents) and with version control is desirable. Knowledge of economic development issues of Arab countries, particularly Jordan, is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariate; and Arabic is a working language of UNESCWA. For this position, fluency in English is required. Note: "Fluency" equals a rating of 'fluent' in all four area ( speak, read, write, and understand). Additional Information Not available. postings.text: --> UNESCO - Call for individual consultants - Promoting sustainable development Call for individual consultants - Promoting sustainable development Support UIL in transforming lifelong learning policies and practices. This opening expired 10 months ago. Do not try to apply for this job. UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Open positions at UNESCO Hamburg ( Germany ) Consultant Show advice for this position Application deadline 10 months ago : Wednesday 7 Jan 2026 at 23:59 UTC Open application form Overview Support UIL in transforming lifelong learning policies and practices. You have: Advanced university degree (masters) in education, social sciences, development studies, global area/ regional studies or any other related fields. At least 3 years of relevant work experience in the field of education/LLL policy and capacity-building. Previous work experience in designing online and in-person training for policymakers working in the field of lifelong learning. Familiarity with ESD and RVA in different countries. At least 3 years of relevant experience working with an international city network. Proven experience in collaborating on international projects in the field of education. Fluency in English (both written and spoken). Fluency in Spanish (both written and spoken). Excellent drafting and communication skills. Excellent facilitation and instructional design skills. Excellent independent working skills. Excellent analytical skills. Contract This is a Consultancy contract. More about Consultancy contracts . Partner --> Strong networks lead to stronger careers. Colleagues.org Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Education Sector (ED) Duty Station: remote Classification of duty station: Standard Duration of Assignment: Job Family: Education Type of contract : Non Staff Duration of contract : From 7 to 11 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Paris Time) : 07-JAN-2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **OVERVIEW OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THE POST** ----------------------------------------- BACKGROUND Promoting sustainable development through flexible and inclusive lifelong learning systems The UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning (UIL) works to support lifelong learning systems and policy development at the national and local level through policy support, research, partnerships and networking, and tailored capacity-building activities. Recognition, Validation and Accreditation (RVA) of non-formal and informal learning is one of the pillars of inclusive lifelong learning policy. Consequently, many countries have developed a national system for RVA. UIL considers it of the utmost importance to use RVA for the integration of outcomes of non-formal and informal learning into national, regional and global qualifications frameworks. Within the context of the new UIL–SOU GNLC Academy Hub, UIL will implement a capacity-building programme on “Strengthening Lifelong Learning Systems through Multi-Level and Multi-Sectoral Engagement”, which is designed to support countries at different levels of system development, providing them with structured technical inputs, opportunities for international exchange and tailored support for advancing or updating national lifelong learning policies, strategies and practices. The programme will involve a component on flexible pathways and RVA and how they connect different sectors and sub-sectors. This line of work will also include follow-up activities with countries previously involved in UIL’s capacity-building workshops. At the local level, UIL is working with UNESCO Learning Cities to support the development, enhancement and implementation of local lifelong learning policies and strategies. A particular focus of this work is in the area of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) and lifelong learning for climate action, including the recent launch of the Greening Communities Guidance (GCG). In 2026, UIL will promote the practical use of the GCG in learning cities and will develop materials and offer targeted trainings to support cities in implementing the guidance. PURPOSE OF THE CONSULTANCY This consultancy will support UIL in advancing its work on lifelong learning policies and practices at both national and local levels. Through targeted capacity-building and follow-up activities, a consultant is sought to contribute to the above described programmatic areas. The consultant will play a key role in developing knowledge and training resources, facilitating national and regional engagement, providing technical feedback on country outputs, and supporting the further development and dissemination of key resources related to the Greening Communities Guide. Further responsibilities include coordinating the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities (GNLC) ESD Working Group. Overall, this consultancy will contribute to UIL’s strategic objectives of fostering inclusive and sustainable lifelong learning systems worldwide. MAIN DUTIES AND RSPONSIBILITIES Under the overall authority of the Director of the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning (UIL) and the team leader of the Skills Throughout Life Team, the individual consultant will undertake the following main responsibilities: **Thematic area: ESD and greening communities** **Revise the ESD Online Course and support coordination of the GNLC ESD working group** - Revise the structure and content to reflect the Greening Communities Guidance (English and Spanish edition) - Develop a hybrid workshop format for implementing the course - Assist in coordinating the GNLC’s ESD Working Group activities and meetings. Long Description ---------------- **Contribute to the implementation of the Greening Communities Guide** - Support the organization of capacity building webinars to support the implementation of the Greening Communities Guidance - Contribute to the development of a support package with materials to enhance practical usability of the guidance - Draft elements for a social media campaign on greening communities within the UNESCO GNLC - Coordinate the translation of the guidance document into Spanish - Engage in a regular exchange with the Secretariat of the Greening Education Partnership to support the guide’s promotion and implementation **Flexible LLL systems:** **Develop and implement targeted RVA training packages for selected countries** - Develop bilateral training packages for two countries, including content development (based on UIL/UNESCO resources) and design of targeted workshop formats - Organize and implement bilateral training workshops for the selected countries - Evaluate the outcomes of the trainings and provide a short report on the results to UIL **Develop a capacity-building training on the UNESCO Qualifications Passport and RVA** - Collaborate with partners at UNESCO HQ to co-create an online capacity-building training to support UNESCO Qualifications Passport evaluators in selected countries in the RVA of non-formal and informal learning outcomes possessed by refugees and internally displaced persons. **Contribute to the new edition of the** **Global Inventory** **of National and Regional Qualifications Frameworks** - Co-develop and support the enhancement of a cross-country analysis report to be featured in the sixth edition of the Global Inventory of National and Regional Qualifications Frameworks. - Develop a thematic chapter on private sector involvement in RVA together with Cedefop and ETF colleagues for this edition of the Inventory. - Provide further inputs to support the ongoing development and finalization of the Inventory during regular engagement and exchange with partners at Cedefop, ETF and UNESCO HQ. **Promoting learning city development** **Contribute to the development of the GNLC Academy Offer and regional networks** **Contribute to the implementation of the GNLC webinar series** - Support the coordination of the GNLC with a particular focus on Latin America and the Caribbean - Contribute to the expansion of the GNLC Academy offer - Contribute to implementing a GNLC webinar series The consultancy is expected to last 11 months, commencing on 15 January 2026 and concluding on 15 December 2026. The consultant is required to work remotely and must submit editable versions of all deliverables in English (and, in some cases, Spanish) within the contract period. The specified dates for the deliverables indicated below are subject to revision. List of deliverables - **Deliverables to be submitted by 31 January 2026** - Support package with materials to enhance practical usability of the Greening Communities Guidance developed - **Deliverables to be submitted by 28 February 2026** - Elements for a social media campaign on greening communities within the UNESCO GNLC developed, implementation supported - Capacity building webinar to support the implementation of the Greening Communities Guidance organized - ESD working group meetings coordinated - **Deliverables to be submitted by 31 March 2026** - Thematic chapter on private sector involvement developed for the Global NQF Inventory - ESD working group meetings coordinated - GNLC webinar series supported - **Deliverables to be submitted by 30 April 2026** - Content and structure of the ESD online course revised (English) - Hybrid workshop format for implementing the course developed - Capacity building webinar to support the implementation of the Greening Communities Guidance organized - ESD working group meetings coordinated - **Deliverables to be submitted by 31 May 2026** - Content and structure of the ESD online course revised (Spanish) - Hybrid workshop format for implementing the course developed (Spanish) - Capacity building webinar to support the implementation of the Greening Communities Guidance organized - Spanish version of the Greening Communities guidance - ESD working group meetings coordinated - GNLC webinar series supported Long Description ---------------- - **Deliverables to be submitted by 30 June 2026** - Capacity building webinar to support the implementation of the Greening Communities Guidance organized - Cross-country analysis for the Global Inventory of NQFs developed - Inputs to support the finalization of the Inventory during regular engagement and exchange with partners provided; UIL contributions coordinated - ESD working group meetings coordinated - **Deliverables to be submitted by 31 July 2026** - Capacity-building online training on the UNESCO Qualifications Passport for refugees and internally displaces persons developed - Greening Communities Guidance in selected GNLC member cities piloted - ESD working group meetings coordinated - GNLC webinar series supported - **Deliverables to be submitted by 13 August 2026** - Bilateral RVA training packages for two countries developed, including content development (based on UIL/UNESCO resources) and design of targeted workshop formats - ESD working group meetings coordinated - **Deliverables to be submitted by 30 September 2026** - Needs-based assessment of applicability of the Greening Communities Guidance in GNLC member cities with recommendations on revision and development of additional materials - Learning cities network activities supported with a particular focus on Latin America and the Caribbean and strategic development of the GNLC Academy offer supported - ESD working group meetings coordinated - GNLC webinar series supported - **Deliverables to be submitted by 31 October 2026** - Bilateral training workshops for two countries implemented - Capacity-building online training on the UNESCO Qualifications Passport for refugees and internally displaces persons implemented - ESD working group meetings coordinated - **Deliverables to be submitted by 30 November 2026** - New edition of the ESD course implemented - Materials to support the implementation of the Greening Communities
