postings.text: Senior Economist - Research | ECB - European Central Bank Skip to main content Senior Economist - Research ECB - European Central Bank Frankfurt Both national and international F/G (bracket 2 - step 1) level Speaks English Application deadline: December 02, 2026 (20 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Senior Economist position at the ECB involves conducting high-quality research for publication in top finance and economics journals, providing research-based policy advice, and developing analytical frameworks to support policy analysis. The role requires collaboration with internal and external counterparts and participation in research conferences. Candidates will have opportunities for professional development and access to extensive research resources. The position is based in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, and offers a fixed-term contract with the possibility of conversion to a permanent role. Candidate Requirements: PhD or equivalent in economics, finance, or relevant field Research papers suitable for high-quality academic journals Extensive knowledge of empirical and/or quantitative methods Excellent writing and presentation skills Advanced English (C1) and intermediate knowledge of another EU language General Information Type of contract Fixed-term contract which may be converted into a permanent contract after three years subject to individual performance and organisational needs Who can apply? EU nationals Salary F/G (bracket 2 - step 1) full time monthly net salary: €6,517 plus benefits, for further information see what we offer. Working time Full time Place of work Frankfurt am Main, Germany Closing date 02.12.2026 Your team You will be part of the Directorate General Research. Our Directorate General has around 60 staff, split across two divisions: Financial Research and Monetary Policy Research. Our people conduct research on monetary policy transmission and implementation, financial institutions and markets, financial stability, regulation and supervision, monetary economics, international finance and economics, macroeconomics, labour economics, macro-econometrics and the economics of climate change. In your role as a Senior Economist, you will conduct state-of-the-art research aimed at publication in top finance and economics journals, provide research-based policy advice to senior management in the Directorate General, other ECB business areas and senior policymakers, share your latest research findings in internal and external research seminars, conferences and policy fora, and publish your work in academic journals.  The ECB is an inclusive employer and we strive to reflect the diversity of the population we serve. We encourage you to apply irrespective of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religious beliefs, sexual orientation or other characteristics.  Your role As a Senior Economist you will: conduct high-quality research and publish in top finance and economics journals; provide research-based policy advice and analysis on key central bank policy issues; contribute to the development of analytical frameworks and tools to support policy analysis; establish and maintain productive working relationships with internal and external counterparts (e.g. through active participation in international research conferences and research networks). For this role we are seeking candidates who demonstrate the potential for growth, and we will support the selected candidate in their development of the required skills. We actively support professional development for our staff. Besides learning opportunities such as training and mentoring, we encourage horizontal mobility after some years in the same position. The position offers you excellent opportunities to develop your research agenda in a unique, international setting that combines research excellence with policy impact. You will have the chance to work in a stimulating environment where you can apply your research to analysis supporting policy decisions. We provide access to research assistance, excellent computing facilities and a rich set of confidential and proprietary datasets, as well as the opportunity to interact with academic consultants. You will be able to attend external conferences and seminars in your area of expertise. You will be part of a multicultural team that strives for continuous innovation to make a positive impact on the lives of European citizens. Qualifications, experience and skills Essential:  a PhD or equivalent in economics, finance or another relevant field, or close to completing a PhD in one of these fields (see How you can join us for details on degree equivalences); research papers suitable for publication in high-quality, peer-reviewed academic journals in the areas of financial or monetary policy research (if you received your PhD several years ago, a publication record in line with your seniority, comprising papers published in high-quality, peer-reviewed academic journals); extensive knowledge of state-of-the-art empirical and/or quantitative methods; excellent writing and presentation skills; an advanced (C1) command of English and an intermediate (B1) command of at least one other official language of the EU, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. You engage collaboratively with others. You pursue team goals and learn willingly from other people’s diverse perspectives. You signal any need for change by explaining it and proposing alternative solutions. You analyse complex information effectively and can evaluate different views to arrive at solutions. You know and anticipate stakeholder needs. You are motivated to contribute to the ECB’s mission, to serve the citizens of the EU as a member of a public institution and to work with colleagues from all over Europe. You are motivated to be part of our team and to develop and use your skills and competencies to achieve the aims of this position. Working modalities We offer internationally competitive salaries and allowances. Taxes on salaries, allowances and benefits are paid to the European Union instead of the national tax authorities. postings.text: Consultant (Extreme Heat Risk Governance) | UNDRR - United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction Skip to main content Consultant (Extreme Heat Risk Governance) UNDRR - United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction Geneva, Dakar CON level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 19, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is seeking a Consultant for Extreme Heat Risk Governance in Dakar, Senegal. The role involves engaging with the Senegalese government to implement the Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework and Toolkit, identifying governance gaps, and developing a roadmap for heat risk reduction. The consultant will coordinate with various stakeholders, support data collection, and facilitate workshops. This position requires a strong background in disaster risk reduction and governance, along with fluency in English and French. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor's degree in relevant field Minimum 5 years of experience in governance or disaster risk reduction Experience with national and sub-national stakeholders in Senegal Experience in drafting strategic documents and stakeholder consultations Fluency in English and French Result of Service The Government of Senegal received support in applying the Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework and Toolkit to identify governance gaps, strengthen inter-agency coordination, assess heat-risk governance maturity, and develop a prioritized roadmap and financing strategy for advancing extreme heat risk reduction and resilience measures at national and sub-national levels. Work Location Dakar, Senegal Expected duration 13 months Duties and Responsibilities Established in December 1999, the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the designated focal point in the United Nations system for the coordination of efforts to reduce disasters and to ensure synergies among disaster reduction activities of the United Nations and regional organizations and activities in both developed and less developed countries. Led by the United Nations Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Disaster Risk Reduction (SRSG), UNDRR has over 160 staff located in its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and in regional offices. Specifically, UNDRR guides, monitors, analyses and reports on progress in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030, supports regional and national implementation of the Framework, and catalyzes action and increases global awareness to reduce disaster risk, working with UN Member States and a broad range of partners and stakeholders, including civil society, the private sector, parliamentarians and the science and technology community. Extreme heat has emerged as a defining challenge of the 21st century. It is now more frequent, intense and prolonged, driving rising mortality, productivity losses, infrastructure disruption, ecosystem decline and deepening inequalities. Recognizing the scale of the challenge, the UN Secretary-General has named extreme heat a "top-tier climate risk", calling for urgent and coordinated action to strengthen prevention, preparedness, resilience and governance. In response to the UN Secretary-General's Call to Action on Extreme Heat, UNDRR, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the Global Heat Health Information Network (GHHIN) coordinated the development of the Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework and Toolkit, with experts from national and subnational governments, international financial institutions, UN and other international organizations, and additional partners. Launched at COP30 in Belém, Brazil, to help decision-makers measure, understand, strengthen and sustain heat-risk governance and investment across sectors and scales, this consultancy supports the implementation of a programme of pilot projects to apply and test the Framework and Toolkit in Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and Small Island Developing States (SIDS). With support from the Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems (CREWS) Initiative and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), Senegal will test the Framework and Toolkit through coordinated technical assistance provided by UNDRR. The project aims to identify governance gaps, priority actions, institutional responsibilities and financing opportunities to protect vulnerable populations, systems and domains. Duties and Responsibilities The consultant will be based in Dakar, Senegal. The consultant will work under the overall supervision of the Programme Management Officer, UNDRR Regional Office for Africa, and the Global Lead, Extreme Heat Risk Reduction at UNDRR Headquarters. The consultant will work closely with the Government of Senegal and technical experts from UNDRR Headquarters, WMO and GHHIN, as well as relevant partners in the country. The consultant will undertake or oversee the following: 1. Government Engagement and Coordination Maintain regular engagement with the Government of Senegal to identify champion entities, agree on the project approach and expected results, and support the establishment and functioning of cross-sectoral inter-agency relationships in support of integrated extreme heat risk governance, including stakeholder onboarding, relationship management and follow-up. 2. Stakeholder Mapping and Engagement Map relevant government institutions, partners, donors and investors, together with the knowledge partner providing technical assistance to the project, as well as in-country knowledge partners and technical experts. Support documentation of roles, mandates and coordination linkages for extreme heat risk governance and investments. Develop and implement a stakeholder and partner engagement strategy. 3. Socialization of the Framework and Toolkit Support sensitization and outreach activities on the Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework and Toolkit with key stakeholders in Dakar and at sub-national level, as relevant. 4. Assessment and Data Collection Support key informant interviews, surveys and questionnaires to collect in-country information, including climate-services use in decision-making and heat-governance maturity assessments, in coordination with UNDRR, WMO and GHHIN technical experts. 5. Support Multi-Stakeholder Workshops and Tabletop Simulations Support the Government of Senegal in planning, designing, preparing and delivering multi-stakeholder workshops together with UNDRR, WMO and GHHIN staff and technical experts, including scenario-based tabletop simulation exercises and consolidation of workshop outputs. 6. Input to the Phase 2 Roadmap and Financing Strategy Support internalization and processing of the outcomes of the first inter-agency coordination meeting among Senegalese government institutions to consolidate and validate priority actions and indicative financing strategies for subsequent phases identified by the Government of Senegal and key stakeholders through workshops and meetings, in coordination with UNDRR, WMO, GHHIN and government counterparts. Qualifications/special skills Bachelor's degree in disaster risk reduction, public administration and/or governance, political affairs, emergency management, engineering, public policy, urban planning, social science, or a related field is required. Minimum 5 years of experience in public administration and/or governance, political affairs, disaster risk reduction, risk management, engineering, urban planning or a related field in Senegal is required. Work experience with national and sub-national stakeholders in Senegal is required. Experience drafting strategic planning documents, reports and conducting stakeholder consultations is required. Experience supporting inter-agency and cross-sectoral coordination processes is desirable. Experience and familiarity with extreme heat risk prevention, mitigation and management measures is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in English and French is required for this consultancy. Knowledge of an additional United Nations official language is desirable. Additional Information Due to the high volume of applications received, only successful candidates will be contacted. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). Para la preparación de esta propuesta, abajo se detallan los elementos a considerar: 1. Completar la aplicación en línea. 2. Enviar por correo electrónico: 1. Gracias por su interés en esta oportunidad de consultoría de la UNESCO; y esperamos recibir su propuesta. **Antecedentes** ---------------- Las tendencias regionales —marcadas por la inestabilidad, el bajo crecimiento económico, el aumento de las desigualdades, la crisis ambiental y la limitada inversión social— continúan amenazando el derecho a una educación de calidad en América Latina y el Caribe. En este contexto, el mandato de la UNESCO en el marco del ODS 4, y en particular de la meta 4.7, adquiere relevancia estratégica para promover sistemas educativos más inclusivos, seguros y orientados al bienestar integral. La UNESCO cuenta con una trayectoria consolidada en la articulación entre la educación, la salud, el bienestar y los derechos humanos. Desde su rol fundador en ONUSIDA en 1996 hasta las lecciones aprendidas durante la pandemia de COVID-19, la Organización ha evidenciado la necesidad de enfoques intersectoriales que fortalezcan el papel de la educación en la prevención de riesgos, la reducción de desigualdades y la protección de niñas, niños y jóvenes. En este marco, la Estrategia de la UNESCO en educación para la salud y el bienestar busca mejorar los resultados educativos y de bienestar mediante el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de los sistemas educativos y de los actores clave, contribuyendo a los ODS de educación, salud e igualdad de género. De manera complementaria, la agenda de Educación para el Desarrollo Sostenible y Educación para la Ciudadanía Mundial impulsa el desarrollo de conocimientos, habilidades, valores y actitudes para la convivencia democrática, la paz y la sostenibilidad. La Hoja de Ruta EDS 2030 y el trabajo de las redes regionales EDS 2030 y ECM LAC han fortalecido la producción de evidencia, el intercambio de buenas prácticas y el acompañamiento técnico a los países. Estos enfoques quedaron reflejados en la actualización de la Recomendación de 1974, adoptada en 2023, que integra la visión humanista de la UNESCO ante los desafíos globales contemporáneos. En continuidad con esta agenda, y a partir de las prioridades expresadas por los ministros y ministras de Educación de la región, la UNESCO impulsó en 2024 un proceso regional para la prevención y el abordaje de la violencia en el sector educativo. Este proceso incluyó una consulta regional en 27 países, con más de 5.800 respuestas, así como espacios subregionales y nacionales, y culminó en la Reunión Regional de Alto Nivel celebrada en Bogotá, Colombia. Como resultado, los Estados Miembros mandataban a la UNESCO que diseñara un Plan de Acción Regional para responder de manera articulada, preventiva y multisectorial a las distintas formas de violencia que afectan las trayectorias educativas. El Plan de Acción Regional para la Prevención y el Abordaje de la Violencia en el Sector Educativo en América Latina y el Caribe fue elaborado de manera participativa durante 2025, incorporando aportes de ministerios de Educación, especialistas de la UNESCO y del Sistema de Naciones Unidas, academia y organizaciones de la sociedad civil. El proceso evidenció amplios consensos sobre la urgencia de fortalecer respuestas integrales, preventivas y restaurativas, que permitan transformar los entornos educativos en espacios seguros, saludables, inclusivos y promotores de la paz. La violencia en los entornos educativos constituye una amenaza persistente al derecho a la educación, al bienestar de estudiantes y docentes, y a la construcción de sociedades más justas e inclusivas. Frente a este desafío, el Plan de Acción Regional se estructura en torno a cuatro pilares estratégicos: (1) investigación y generación de evidencia, (2) cooperación regional, (3) Observatorio Regional y (4) diálogo político y asistencia técnica, estableciendo un marco de acción a corto y mediano plazo que requiere apoyo técnico especializado para su implementación. Long Description ---------------- **Objetivo de la consultoría** El principal objetivo de esta consultoría es apoyar a la Unidad de Educación Transformativa mediante el diseño e implementación de actividades alineadas con la estrategia y el plan regional previamente mencionados. En particular, se enfocará en las actividades en América Latina y el Caribe relacionadas con el Resultado Estratégico 3: Todos los y las estudiantes tienen acceso a entornos de aprendizaje seguros e integradores, exentos de toda forma de violencia, acoso, estigma y discriminación. Como acción prioritaria de este resultado, el/la consultor/a contribuirá a la implementación del plan regional de prevención y abordaje de la violencia en el sector educativo. **Principales tareas** - Planificar, coordinar y ejecutar actividades vinculadas al Resultado Estratégico 3 de la Estrategia de la UNESCO sobre educación para la salud y el bienestar en América Latina y el Caribe. - Apoyar la implementación operativa del Plan de Acción Regional para la prevención y el abordaje de la violencia en el sector educativo, incluyendo: el levantamiento de información con las oficinas de la UNESCO y con contrapartes regionales; la sistematización y el análisis de insumos técnicos; y la coordinación y el seguimiento de acciones con las oficinas de la región. - Actualizar y consolidar el mapeo regional de iniciativas de educación para la salud y el bienestar implementadas durante 2025 por las oficinas de la UNESCO, asegurando la organización, validación y actualización periódica de la información. - Redactar y producir documentos técnicos y de difusión, tales como notas conceptuales, boletines, documentos de trabajo, publicaciones y otros productos escritos requeridos para la implementación y comunicación de las acciones regionales. - Preparar, revisar y dar seguimiento a documentos asociados a proyectos, incluyendo insumos técnicos, reportes y materiales de apoyo, en coordinación con la Unidad de Educación Transformativa y otras áreas pertinentes. **COMPETENCIES (Core / Managerial)** ------------------------------------ Professionalism (C) **-** ----- For detailed information, please consult the [UNESCO Competency Framework](https://en.unesco.org/sites/default/files/competency_framework_e.pdf). **CALIFICACIONES REQUERIDAS** ----------------------------- **Educación:** Grado superior universitario en las áreas de educación, políticas públicas, sociología y/u otra área relevante de las ciencias sociales. **Experiencia requerida:** Al menos 5 años de experiencia profesional demostrada en temas asociados a la consultoría. **Competencias:** - Contar con excelentes habilidades analíticas, de investigación y de identificación, sistematización y análisis de experiencias. - Contar con una comprensión y visión teórica y práctica sobre los campos temáticos vinculados a esta consultoría. - Tener excelentes habilidades interpersonales y comunicacionales, en particular en un contexto profesional. - Excelentes destrezas para la realización de presentaciones para distintos actores, con propósitos de consulta, revisión y/o diseminación. - Dominio avanzado del inglés para colaborar eficazmente con actores del Caribe angloparlante. **CALIFICACIONES DESEABLES** ---------------------------- - Estudios de maestría en Educación o áreas relacionadas. - Partner --> Daily Job Alerts: Stay Updated, Stay Ahead with Pro Membership UN Talent Pro Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Education Sector (ED) Duty Station: Paris Job Family: Education Type of contract : Non Staff Duration of contract : From 1 to 6 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Duty Station Time) : 05-JAN-2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **DESCRIPTION GÉNÉRALE DES FONCTIONS DU POSTE** ----------------------------------------------- **CONTEXTE** Le Gouvernement de la Guinée met en œuvre, depuis 2020, le Programme Décennal de l'Éducation (ProDEG) 2020-2029, une stratégie sectorielle établissant les orientations et priorités pour le développement du système éducatif national. Ce programme revêt un caractère participatif et constitue le cadre de référence pour l'ensemble des interventions dans le secteur de l'éducation. En accord avec la programmation initialement prévue, une évaluation à mi-parcours (2020-2024) du ProDEG est planifiée en 2025-2026. Cette évaluation vise à : (i) apprécier l'état d'avancement de la mise en œuvre du ProDEG au regard des objectifs initialement fixés ; (ii) identifier les facteurs ayant affecté les performances ; (iii) formuler des recommandations pour la mise à jour du programme en vue de sa deuxième phase de mise en œuvre. L'IIEP-UNESCO a été sélectionné par le Gouvernement de Guinée et ses partenaires au développement pour appuyer techniquement trois composantes : (i) une analyse approfondie du financement de l'éducation en Guinée complétant les informations existantes ; (ii) une revue à mi-parcours du ProDEG ; et (iii) une mise à jour du programme, incluant la révision du cadre de résultats, l'élaboration d'un modèle de simulation financière et économique, et la rédaction d'une note de cadrage politique sectorielle. Pour soutenir ces activités, l'IIEP-UNESCO sollicite un.e consultant.e spécialiste en planification et financement de l'éducation pour une durée de six (6) mois à partir de janvier 2026 pour appuyer la mise en œuvre des composantes ii) et iii). Long Description ---------------- **OBJECTIF GÉNÉRAL** Appuyer l'équipe IIEP-UNESCO dans la réalisation de l'analyse du financement de l'éducation, la conduite de l’évaluation à mi-parcours du ProDEG, et la mise à jour du programme, notamment par la révision du cadre de résultats, l'actualisation du modèle de simulation et l'élaboration de la note de cadrage. Objectifs spécifiques i) Appuyer la conduite de l’évaluation à mi-parcours participative du ProDEG, notamment par la formulation d'orientations méthodologiques et l'accompagnement des équipes sectorielles dans l'analyse de la mise en œuvre et des performances ; ii) Soutenir la mise à jour du ProDEG, en particulier par la révision du cadre de résultats, l'actualisation du modèle de simulation financière et économique, et la contribution à la rédaction de la note de cadrage de politique sectorielle. Long Description ---------------- **RÉSULTATS ATTENDUS ET TÂCHES PRINCIPALES** 3.1 Evaluation à mi-parcours du ProDEG La ou le consultant.e appuiera à l’évaluation à mi-parcours participative du ProDEG par : - L’appui technique à la collecte de données et à l’analyse de l'efficacité et de la pertinence de deux des six programmes prioritaires du ProDEG ; - L'appui à l'organisation et à la facilitation de deux ateliers résidentiels et de sessions en lignes avec les équipes nationales pour l’évaluation de deux programmes prioritaires ; - La contribution à la rédaction du rapport final de l’évaluation à mi-parcours, comprenant l'appréciation de la performance, de l’efficacité, de la pertinence et des recommandations pour ces deux programmes prioritaires. 3.3 Mise à jour du ProDEG La ou le consultant.e appuiera la mise à jour du ProDEG par : - La révision du cadre de résultats du ProDEG, en intégrant les conclusions de la revue à mi-parcours et en mettant à jour les indicateurs clés de performance ; - L'actualisation du modèle de simulation financière et économique pour intégrer les ajustements programmatiques et les scénarios de financement ; - La contribution à la rédaction de la note de cadrage de politique sectorielle qui consolidera les principes directeurs du ProDEG révisé pour sa deuxième phase de mise en œuvre (2025-2029) ; - L'organisation et la facilitation de réunions de concertation technique avec le Secrétariat Technique de Coordination et de Pilotage (ST/CP-ProDEG) et les partenaires au développement. **QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES** --------------------------- **Education** - Diplôme de Master minimum en économie, politiques publiques, gestion du secteur public, planification de l'éducation, ou domaine connexe ; **Expérience professionelle** - Minimum 10 années d'expérience professionnelle en planification et financement de l'éducation dans le contexte de pays en développement ; - Démonstration d'une expertise avérée en analyse du financement de l'éducation, financement des politiques éducatives, et gestion des finances publiques (GFP) appliquée au secteur éducatif ; - Connaissance approfondie des processus de planification sectorielle en éducation et des cadres de résultats ; - Expérience d'appui à des évaluations de programmes sectoriels ou à des revues de politiques dans le domaine de l'éducation. **Compétences techniques** - Excellentes aptitudes en analyse quantitative et qualitative, et en traitement statistique de données ; - Maîtrise des approches et méthodologies d'évaluation et d'analyse de politiques ; - Compétences en modélisation financière ou en utilisation d'outils d'analyse économiques ; - Aptitude à concevoir et à animer des processus participatifs d'analyse avec les équipes sectorielles ; - Excellentes capacités de rédaction, synthèse et traduction de concepts complexes en langage accessible ; - Maîtrise des outils informatiques standards (MS Office, Google Workspace) et familiarité avec les logiciels d'analyse de données (R, Python, STATA, ou similaires constituerait un atout). Long Description ---------------- **Langues** - Maîtrise du français (lu, écrit et parlé) : langue de travail principale ; - Anglais : souhaitable. **Qualités relationnelles** - Capacité à travailler en équipe et à collaborer efficacement avec des partenaires multiples (ministères, partenaires au développement, institutions universitaires) ; - Sensibilité aux enjeux de gouvernance, de participation et d'appropriation nationale ; - Rigueur méthodologique, capacité de gestion du temps et respect des délais ; - Sensibilité aux questions d'équité, d'inclusion et de genre dans l'analyse des politiques **DURÉE ET CALENDRIER** ----------------------- **Durée générale** Contrat de consultance de six (6) mois, de mi-janvier 2026 à mi-juillet 2026. **Missions et déplacements** Le consultant.e effectuera 3 à 4 missions de terrain à Conakry et/ou Kindia (Guinée) au cours de la période de janvier à juillet 2026. Le calendrier indicatif des missions est le suivant. Résultats et livrables attendus : 1\. Le consultant.e assurera la citation appropriée de toutes les sources et le respect de la confidentialité des informations sensibles. **PROCESSUS DE CANDIDATURE** ---------------------------- Les candidat·es remplissant les critères requis sont invité·es à soumettre leur candidature comprenant : 1\. Une proposition technique détaillant l’approche et la méthodologie (3 pages maximum), 2\. Une proposition financière, et 3\. Un CV mettant en avant l’expérience pertinente. Les candidatures ne comprenant pas ces informations ne seront pas prises en considération pour les phases suivantes du processus de sélection. Les documents doivent être envoyés à **au plus tard le 5 janvier 2026**. L’objet de l’email doit être : « IIEP Consultancy : PRODEG, 6 mois ». NOTE : Le CV, accompagné de la proposition technique et financière, doit être envoyé à l’adresse email [email protected] pour que le dossier soit éligible. **Seuls les candidats retenus seront contactés.** **SELECTION AND RECRUITMENT PROCESS** ------------------------------------- Please note that all candidates must complete an on-line application and provide complete and accurate information. postings.text: Environmental Restoration Technical consultant | UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Skip to main content Environmental Restoration Technical consultant UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Remote | Mexico City International CON level Speaks Spanish Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (19 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Environmental Restoration Technical Consultant will provide specialized technical assistance to support the structuring of a National Investment Portfolio of Priority Environmental Restoration Projects under the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026. The consultant will compile and systematize technical information, develop standardized methodologies, and create a consolidated project portfolio. This role involves collaboration with various stakeholders to enhance investment readiness and facilitate access to funding opportunities. The consultancy aims to strengthen Mexico's capacity to meet its National Biodiversity Targets. Candidate Requirements: University degree in relevant field Minimum two years of relevant experience Experience in ecosystem restoration or biodiversity conservation Experience with environmental project design or finance Fluency in written and spoken Spanish Result of Service The consultant will provide specialized technical assistance to support the structuring of a National Investment Portfolio of Priority Environmental Restoration Projects under the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026. Work Location Remote Expected duration 3 months Duties and Responsibilities The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system, and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s Ecosystems Division works with governments and partners to develop and promote ecosystem-based solutions that support sustainable development and biodiversity conservation. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership (NBSAP-AP) is a country-led global initiative that supports the development and implementation of ambitious National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). Through technical assistance, facilitation, capacity development, and strategic coordination, the Partnership supports countries in accelerating implementation of national biodiversity commitments through whole-of-government and whole-of-society approaches. Mexico has established an ambitious policy framework for ecosystem restoration through ENBioMex 2.0, the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2030, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), and its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0). The National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) has identified 80 priority restoration sites throughout the country, including 53 priority sites identified during 2025 and an additional 27 sites to be incorporated during 2026. These sites represent strategic opportunities for restoring priority ecosystems while contributing to biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation and adaptation, water security, disaster risk reduction, sustainable livelihoods and ecosystem services. Although significant progress has been made in identifying restoration priorities, one of the principal barriers to implementation is the absence of standardized methodologies for structuring restoration projects that meet the technical, financial and institutional requirements expected by financing institutions. Existing project information is heterogeneous, prepared under different methodologies, and frequently lacks the technical, economic and financial elements necessary to attract investment or access national and international funding opportunities. Strengthening the investment readiness of restoration projects has therefore become a strategic priority for the Directorate General for Environmental Restoration (DGRA) of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (SEMARNAT). Developing a standardized portfolio of investment-ready restoration projects will facilitate access to public budgets, international cooperation, biodiversity and climate finance, environmental compensation schemes, blended finance mechanisms and private sector investment. To address this challenge, the Directorate General for Environmental Restoration (DGRA of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (SEMARNAT) requires specialized technical assistance to consolidate information from the 80 priority restoration sites, develop a standardized project preparation methodology, structure a national restoration investment portfolio, apply practical project preparation tools, and identify information and financing needs that can support subsequent project development. This consultancy contributes directly to the implementation of National Biodiversity Targets (NBTs) 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 under ENBioMex 2.0, which collectively represent Mexico’s contribution to Global Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. These targets focus on restoring degraded terrestrial, freshwater, coastal and marine ecosystems, increasing ecological functionality, strengthening restoration governance and planning mechanisms, and enhancing the long-term sustainability of restoration efforts. The consultant will report to the Programme Management Officer of the Nature Frameworks Support Unit, in close collaboration with the NBSAP Accelerator Partnership Facilitator for Mexico and the Directorate General for Environmental Restoration (DGRA), SEMARNAT. Duties and Responsibilities The consultant will provide specialized technical assistance to support the structuring of a National Investment Portfolio of Priority Environmental Restoration Projects under the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026. Product 1: Institutional Baseline Assessment and Standardization of the PNRA Priority Restoration Project Portfolio (To be completed within four weeks from contract start) The consultant will: • Compile and systematize the technical information available for the 80 priority restoration sites included in the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026 portfolio. • Support DGRA technical teams in consolidating, organizing and completing the information corresponding to the priority restoration sites. • Design a standardized institutional project template to compile technical, environmental, ecological, territorial, social, financial and implementation information for each restoration project, providing a common framework for information collection across DGRA Directorates. • Review existing technical documentation, geographic information, restoration objectives, intervention types, implementation status, estimated costs, expected environmental and social benefits, as well as implementation requirements for each priority restoration site. • Identify the information currently available and determine the technical, ecological, territorial, institutional and financial information gaps required to complete each restoration project. • Organize project information into a consolidated institutional database, using the approved institutional project template. • Support technical working sessions with the Directorates responsible for ecosystem restoration within DGRA to validate the institutional template, review information gaps, and agree on the information required to complete each project. • Prepare a project-by-project information gap matrix identifying the missing information, the DGRA Directorate responsible for providing it, and the priority actions required to complete each project file. • Prepare a diagnostic report summarizing the quality, completeness and consistency of the available information, together with recommendations and information requirements needed to consolidate a standardized institutional restoration project portfolio Deliverables • Consolidated database of the 80 PNRA priority restoration sites, organized using a standardized institutional format. • Diagnostic assessment of technical, institutional and financial information, including an evaluation of its quality, completeness and consistency. • Gap analysis identifying missing information required to strengthen investment readiness of each restoration project, including project-specific information requirements. • Standardized technical fiches for all priority restoration sites, prepared using the approved institutional project template, including key indicators comparable between sites. • Presentation of findings and recommendations to DGRA and UNEP, including key information gaps and priority actions required to complete the institutional project portfolio Product 2: Development of a Standardized Institutional Methodology and Project Structuring Toolkit for Investment-Oriented Restoration Projects (To be completed within eight weeks from contract start) The consultant shall: • Review international best practices, methodologies, and standards for structuring investment-ready restoration and Nature-based Solutions (NbS) projects, including relevant experiences from multilateral development banks, international financial institutions, biodiversity finance initiatives, and environmental restoration programmes. • Review existing methodologies currently used by DGRA and other national institutions for project formulation and identify opportunities for harmonization, institutionalization, and future application by subnational governments. • Compile and adapt, in consultation with DGRA, technical criteria and minimum information requirements for project preparation, including implementation considerations, environmental safeguards and monitoring requirements. • Compile practical financial information requirements for project preparation, including estimated implementation costs, operation and maintenance needs, financing requirements, implementation schedules and potential co-financing opportunities. • Develop a standardized institutional restoration project template that can be used by federal, state and municipal governments to formulate, evaluate and structure restoration projects using a common institutional standard. • Develop a project prioritization framework including objective criteria to classify projects according to strategic importance, implementation readiness, restoration impact, biodiversity contribution, climate co-benefits, feasibility, and financing potential ensuring comparability among projects regardless of the implementing institution. • Develop a practical methodological guide describing the complete process for preparing investment-oriented restoration projects under the PNRA, including the application of the institutional project template by federal, state and municipal governments • Conduct technical validation sessions with DGRA to review and refine the proposed methodology and institutional tools, and assess its applicability with potential subnational users. Deliverables The consultant shall submit: • Institutional Methodological Guide for Structuring Investment-Oriented Restoration Projects. • Standardized Restoration Project Template for use by federal, state and municipal governments. • Institutional Project Prioritization Framework. • Project preparation checklist. • Recommendations for institutional adoption and implementation by federal, state and municipal governments. Product 3: Consolidated Restoration Project Portfolio and Financing Opportunities (To be completed within twelve weeks from contract start) The consultant shall: • Consolidate validated project information into a national portfolio of PNRA priority restoration projects. • Classify projects according to ecosystem type, restoration objectives, ge

postings.text: Document Management Assistant - Contract Agent FG III - EEAS Headquarters – Policy Coordination Division (SG.COORD) - Job No. 528663 | EEAS - European External Action Service Skip to main content Document Management Assistant - Contract Agent FG III - EEAS Headquarters – Policy Coordination Division (SG.COORD) - Job No. 528663 EEAS - European External Action Service Brussels Both national and international FG III, Function Group 3, Contract Agent level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The European External Action Service (EEAS) is seeking a Document Management Assistant to handle high-level correspondence for key EU officials. The role involves coordinating correspondence, ensuring compliance with protocols, and managing administrative processes. The successful candidate will work closely with various EEAS departments and contribute to the efficient handling of sensitive communications. This position is based in Brussels and is a contract agent role with potential for renewal. Candidate Requirements: Passed EPSO CAST exam or registered in EPSO Permanent CAST Post-secondary education diploma or secondary education diploma with 3 years of experience Fluency in English and French EU national with full citizenship rights Strong organizational and interpersonal skills Attention to detail and excellent time management Good knowledge of ARES and MS Office tools Contract type: Contract Agent Deadline for sending application: 25/11/2026   at 12.00 noon (CET) . WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. Within the EEAS, the Policy Coordination Division (SG.COORD) plays a central role to support the HRVP, the EEAS Secretary General and senior management in achieving policy priorities. Through a joined-up approach to inter-institutional coordination, the Division contributes to the effective and efficient conduct of policy and decision-making processes within the EEAS and with regard to the work of the Council and Commission. SG.COORD.Sector 4. manages high-level correspondence addressed to, or originating from, the HRVP, the President of the European Council as well as the President and Vice-Presidents of the Commission on matters relating to external action. It ensures that all correspondence is handled efficiently, accurately and in full compliance with the applicable rules and institutional standards. In line with transparency requirements as well as protocol and diplomatic practice, it oversees quality control and performs registration and transmission of correspondence. The team works closely with other EEAS departments and the relevant Cabinets, thereby contributing to consistent, timely and appropriate handling of sensitive and high-level communications. WE PROPOSE The position of Document Management Assistant – contract agent FGIII as per article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). Within the division, the post entails the end-to-end handling of high-level correspondence for the High Representative/ Vice-President of the European Commission, the President of the European Council, the President of the European Commission or Commission Vice-Presidents. It covers the preparation, quality control, registration, transmission and follow-up of correspondence, ensuring compliance with applicable procedures, protocol requirements, diplomatic standards and within the deadlines. The post also contributes to the smooth coordination of related administrative processes in close cooperation with relevant services. Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function group III), on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of one year that may be successively renewed up to a maximum duration of six years, subject to the maximum duration of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of different types. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT ‎EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available:  01/12/2026 LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION  The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof.  WE LOOK FOR Under the authority of the Head of Division, the successful candidate will ensure the end-to-end handling of high-level correspondence. The person will be entrusted with the following main tasks: coordinate within the EEAS the handing of correspondence for the President and Vice-Presidents of the European Commission, for the President of the European Council, the High Representative/Vice-President and for members of HR/VP's Cabinet; read, analyse and evaluate the incoming correspondence registered by the HR/VP Cabinet, the Secretariat-General of the Commission, or the General Secretariat of the Council and attribute them according to the document management rules and relevant procedures; ensure and monitor the timely preparation and submission of draft replies, carrying out the necessary follow-up to meet deadlines; prepare follow-up/monitoring table for the HR/VP Cabinet and for follow-up of the team's activity and deadlines; carry out quality control of all correspondence submitted for signature by the HR/VP or President of the European Council, President or Vice-Presidents of the Commission, ensuring compliance with protocol and diplomatic standards;  arrange translation requests of high-level correspondence as required and coordinate the linguistic quality control in any other EU language; prepare and submit the final draft of letters for the signature of the High Representative/Vice-President, the President of the European Council, the President or Vice-Presidents of the Commission, including the relevant cover note; finalise, register, transmit and archive the approved outgoing correspondence; in coordination with the relevant EEAS services, prepare, manage and send serial invitation letters for conferences and events, when there are signed by the HR/VP or co-signed; and support the services in relation to the handling of correspondence. Eligibility criteria Further to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in a valid function group for this post, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST in a valid function group for this post ( https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-procedures-always-open-registration ). In the latter case, while the registration will make the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; have a level of post-secondary education attested by a diploma or a level of secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education and appropriate professional experience of three year; have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties;  be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen. Selection criteria Candidates should have:  a high sense of initiative, responsibility and reliability; very good organisational and inter-personal skills as well as a strong service minded and flexible team player attitude; capacity to ensure quality, speed and accuracy in performing complex tasks; strong drafting and problem-solving skills combined with sound judgement; attention to detail; excellent time management skills and the ability to prioritise tasks within a given timeframe; ability to communicate clearly on complex procedures and answer technical questions related to the handling of correspondence; good knowledge of ARES, a strong propensity for IT and very good knowledge of all MS Office Tools, i.e. mail merge in Word, Excel tables; and good knowledge of oral and written English. Furthermore:  experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience in working with or within other EU institutions; knowledge of oral and written French; and good understanding or keen interest in EU external relations. will be considered assets. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest  ( see attached ). MEDICAL CLEARANCE The signature of the contract will be subject to prior favourable opinion of the Medical Service, unless the successful candidate is a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”) The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS. The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”) issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned.  Candidates who do not already have a valid PSC will be required to go through the security clearance vetting procedure of their Member State to obtain this clearance in accordance with national laws and regulations and with the procedure laid down in the  Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the  Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . Until the PSC is issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned, the selected candidate will not be authorised to access EUCI at the level of CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above, or to participate in any meetings or workflow where EUCI is processed. Please note that the necessary procedure for obtaining a PSC can be initiated on request of the employer only, and not by the individual candidate. In case of failure to obtain or renew the required PSC, the AACC may take the appropriate measures in accordance with Article 7 of the  Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Imple

postings.text: Consultoría A: Gestor de casos de identidad legal y normalización migratoria. | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content Consultoría A: Gestor de casos de identidad legal y normalización migratoria. IOM - International Organization for Migration San José Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Application deadline: November 19, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool IOM is seeking a consultant for case management services focused on legal identity and migration normalization for migrants in Costa Rica. The consultant will provide individualized support, conduct needs assessments, and facilitate access to legal documentation and services. Responsibilities include managing case portfolios, coordinating with governmental and consular services, and ensuring compliance with documentation standards. The role requires a commitment to human rights and confidentiality while supporting migrants' socio-economic integration. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Law, Social Work, International Relations, or related fields Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in case management for migrants Proven experience in comprehensive case management Knowledge of legal frameworks and inter-institutional coordination Ability to manage documentation and information systems Fluency in English (minimum B2 level) Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Naturaleza de la consultoría:   Consultoría individual Tipo A para la prestación de servicios especializados de gestión de casos dirigidos a personas migrantes beneficiarias de proyectos de la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) de Costa Rica, mediante el acompañamiento individualizado y el apoyo técnico en procesos de establecimiento de identidad legal, normalización migratoria y documentación.  Project Context and Scope:  El proyecto “Regularización Migratoria e Integración Socioeconómica para Personas Migrantes Recibidas por el Gobierno de Costa Rica”, implementado por la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) en Costa Rica, tiene como objetivo apoyar a las personas migrantes que deciden permanecer en el país, facilitando su acceso a una identidad legal, un estatus migratorio regular de largo plazo, servicios básicos y oportunidades para fortalecer sus medios de vida y avanzar en su integración socioeconómica.  En este contexto, la OIM requiere la contratación de personas consultoras especializadas en gestión de casos (case management)  para brindar atención y acompañamiento técnico individualizado a las personas beneficiarias interesadas permanecer en Costa Rica.  Las personas consultoras serán responsables de realizar perfilamientos y evaluaciones de necesidades relacionadas con la identidad legal, la recuperación documental, normalización migratoria y documentación ; elaborar expedientes individuales para su registro en las bases de datos institucionales; brindar orientación sobre los procesos de normalización migratoria y documentación; coordinar referencias a servicios especializados según las necesidades identificadas; dar seguimiento a casos prioritarios; y acompañar a las personas beneficiarias en el cumplimiento de sus objetivos de integración socioeconómica.  Asimismo, contribuirán a fortalecer el acceso de las personas migrantes a documentos que acrediten su identidad y nacionalidad , servicios consulares, mecanismos de normalización migratoria y otros recursos institucionales relevantes.  Departamento / Unidad a la que contribuye la persona consultora:  Unidad de Inmigración y Gobernanza de las Fronteras (IBG)  La persona consultora desempeñará sus funciones bajo la supervisión del especialista senior técnico (a) de identidad legal/ regularización migratoria, quien será responsable de la validación de casos complejos, la definición de rutas de atención y la coordinación institucional correspondiente.  Responsibilities Funciones a desempeñar:  Gestionar la cartera de casos asignada, realizando entrevistas, evaluaciones integrales y actualizaciones para identificar necesidades, riesgos, barreras y vacíos documentales relacionados con la identidad legal y la normalización migratoria.  Elaborar, implementar y actualizar planes individuales de gestión de casos, con metas, acciones, responsabilidades y cronogramas orientados a la obtención, recuperación, validación o regularización de la documentación requerida.  Orientar y acompañar a las personas beneficiarias en trámites de obtención, renovación, rectificación, reposición, verificación y recuperación de documentos de identidad, documentación civil y requisitos migratorios.  Identificar barreras documentales, jurídicas, administrativas, económicas o procedimentales, así como necesidades de protección o situaciones de vulnerabilidad, y proponer o activar las rutas de atención correspondientes.  Coordinar y dar seguimiento a gestiones y referencias con Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME), consulados, registros civiles, instituciones gubernamentales, socios implementadores y proveedores de servicios especializados, incluidos servicios de traducción, apostillado, legalización, certificación y verificación documental.  Verificar la calidad, integridad, vigencia, consistencia y suficiencia de la documentación recopilada, asegurando el cumplimiento de los requisitos establecidos por las autoridades competentes.  Mantener actualizados los expedientes físicos y digitales y registrar oportunamente las acciones, referencias, avances, resultados, obstáculos y medidas correctivas en los sistemas de información y monitoreo del proyecto.  Participar en jornadas de atención, sesiones informativas, visitas de campo y otras actividades operativas para identificar, orientar y atender a potenciales personas beneficiarias.  Elaborar informes periódicos sobre avances, resultados, desafíos, tendencias, cuellos de botella y lecciones aprendidas, y coordinar con el equipo técnico y las unidades especializadas para asegurar una respuesta integral y eficiente.  Aplicar en todas las etapas los enfoques de derechos humanos, protección, inclusión, diversidad, género, no discriminación y rendición de cuentas, garantizando la confidencialidad, el consentimiento informado, la protección de datos personales y el manejo seguro de información sensible.  Atender otras funciones delegadas por el manager del proyecto.  Indicadores de desempeño para la evaluación de resultados  Porcentaje de casos asignados con evaluación inicial y plan individual de gestión elaborados dentro de los plazos establecidos.  Porcentaje de expedientes físicos y digitales actualizados que cumplen con los estándares de calidad documental, registro, confidencialidad y protección de datos establecidos por el proyecto y la OIM.  Porcentaje de referencias y coordinaciones interinstitucionales gestionadas y documentadas conforme a los protocolos, con respuesta o atención de la entidad receptora.  Porcentaje de personas beneficiarias que alcanzan los hitos u objetivos definidos en sus planes individuales de identidad legal y normalización migratoria.  Porcentaje de informes y reportes de seguimiento entregados oportunamente y aprobados de conformidad con los requisitos de calidad del proyecto.  Qualifications Requisitos obligatorios  Título de bachillerato universitario  en Derecho, Trabajo Social, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Sociales, Administración Pública u otras disciplinas afines.  Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional relevante  en gestión de casos y atención a personas migrantes, refugiadas o en situación de vulnerabilidad, particularmente en identidad legal, documentación civil y regularización migratoria.  Experiencia comprobada en gestión integral de casos , incluyendo entrevistas, evaluación de necesidades, elaboración de planes individuales, acompañamiento técnico y seguimiento de múltiples casos.  Conocimiento del marco normativo y experiencia en coordinación interinstitucional  en materia migratoria, identidad legal y protección, con instituciones gubernamentales, consulados, registros civiles, organismos internacionales u organizaciones de la sociedad civil.  Capacidad para gestionar expedientes y sistemas de información , analizar documentación, utilizar bases de datos y herramientas de seguimiento, y elaborar informes técnicos claros; con dominio del inglés mínimo nivel B2.  Requisitos deseables Grado de Licenciatura  en las áreas antes indicadas.  Experiencia en procesos de normalización o regularización migratoria, recuperación de documentos de identidad, obtención de documentación emitida en países de origen, legalización, apostillado, traducción oficial o verificación documental.  Conocimiento de otros idiomas relevantes para los flujos migratorios de la región , incluyendo francés, árabe, ruso o mandarín.  Viajes requeridos: La persona consultora deberá contar con disponibilidad para realizar visitas de campo y misiones de monitoreo dentro de Costa Rica, previamente coordinadas y autorizadas por la supervisión de la consultoría. Cuando las necesidades operativas del proyecto así lo requieran, dichas visitas podrán incluir fines de semana, con la debida planificación previa.  Los viajes oficiales requeridos para el cumplimiento de las funciones de la consultoría serán organizados y cubiertos por la OIM de conformidad con las políticas, procedimientos y disposiciones aplicables en materia de viajes oficiales (Travel on Duty – TDY). 4  Competencias: Valores  Inclusión y respeto por la diversidad : respeta y promueve las diferencias individuales y culturales. Fomenta un entorno inclusivo en el que se valora la diversidad.  Integridad y transparencia : mantiene altos estándares éticos y actúa de manera coherente con los principios, normas y estándares de conducta de la Organización.  Profesionalismo : demuestra capacidad para desempeñar sus funciones de manera competente, responsable y comprometida, aplicando un juicio sólido para abordar desafíos y situaciones complejas.  Valentía:  demuestra disposición para asumir posiciones firmes y fundamentadas sobre asuntos relevantes, incluso en contextos complejos.  Empatía:  demuestra comprensión y consideración hacia las demás personas, contribuyendo a que se sientan seguras, respetadas y tratadas de manera justa. Competencias básicas – Indicadores conductuales  Trabajo en equipo : desarrolla y promueve una colaboración eficaz dentro del equipo y entre distintas áreas, socios y contrapartes para alcanzar objetivos comunes y optimizar resultados.  Orientación a resultados : produce y entrega resultados de calidad de manera oportuna y con orientación al servicio. postings.text: Environmental Restoration Technical consultant | UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Skip to main content Environmental Restoration Technical consultant UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Remote | Mexico City CON level Speaks Spanish Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (19 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Environmental Restoration Technical Consultant will provide specialized technical assistance to support the structuring of a National Investment Portfolio of Priority Environmental Restoration Projects under the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026. The consultant will compile and systematize technical information, develop standardized methodologies, and create a consolidated project portfolio to enhance investment readiness. This role requires collaboration with various stakeholders and aims to strengthen Mexico's capacity to meet its National Biodiversity Targets. The consultancy will last for three months and is remote. Candidate Requirements: University degree in relevant field Minimum two years of relevant experience Experience in ecosystem restoration or biodiversity conservation Experience with environmental project design or finance Fluency in written and spoken Spanish Result of Service The consultant will provide specialized technical assistance to support the structuring of a National Investment Portfolio of Priority Environmental Restoration Projects under the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026. Work Location Remote Expected duration 3 months Duties and Responsibilities The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system, and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s Ecosystems Division works with governments and partners to develop and promote ecosystem-based solutions that support sustainable development and biodiversity conservation. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership (NBSAP-AP) is a country-led global initiative that supports the development and implementation of ambitious National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). Through technical assistance, facilitation, capacity development, and strategic coordination, the Partnership supports countries in accelerating implementation of national biodiversity commitments through whole-of-government and whole-of-society approaches. Mexico has established an ambitious policy framework for ecosystem restoration through ENBioMex 2.0, the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2030, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), and its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0). The National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) has identified 80 priority restoration sites throughout the country, including 53 priority sites identified during 2025 and an additional 27 sites to be incorporated during 2026. These sites represent strategic opportunities for restoring priority ecosystems while contributing to biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation and adaptation, water security, disaster risk reduction, sustainable livelihoods and ecosystem services. Although significant progress has been made in identifying restoration priorities, one of the principal barriers to implementation is the absence of standardized methodologies for structuring restoration projects that meet the technical, financial and institutional requirements expected by financing institutions. Existing project information is heterogeneous, prepared under different methodologies, and frequently lacks the technical, economic and financial elements necessary to attract investment or access national and international funding opportunities. Strengthening the investment readiness of restoration projects has therefore become a strategic priority for the Directorate General for Environmental Restoration (DGRA) of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (SEMARNAT). Developing a standardized portfolio of investment-ready restoration projects will facilitate access to public budgets, international cooperation, biodiversity and climate finance, environmental compensation schemes, blended finance mechanisms and private sector investment. To address this challenge, the Directorate General for Environmental Restoration (DGRA of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (SEMARNAT) requires specialized technical assistance to consolidate information from the 80 priority restoration sites, develop a standardized project preparation methodology, structure a national restoration investment portfolio, apply practical project preparation tools, and identify information and financing needs that can support subsequent project development. This consultancy contributes directly to the implementation of National Biodiversity Targets (NBTs) 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 under ENBioMex 2.0, which collectively represent Mexico’s contribution to Global Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. These targets focus on restoring degraded terrestrial, freshwater, coastal and marine ecosystems, increasing ecological functionality, strengthening restoration governance and planning mechanisms, and enhancing the long-term sustainability of restoration efforts. The consultant will report to the Programme Management Officer of the Nature Frameworks Support Unit, in close collaboration with the NBSAP Accelerator Partnership Facilitator for Mexico and the Directorate General for Environmental Restoration (DGRA), SEMARNAT. Duties and Responsibilities The consultant will provide specialized technical assistance to support the structuring of a National Investment Portfolio of Priority Environmental Restoration Projects under the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026. Product 1: Institutional Baseline Assessment and Standardization of the PNRA Priority Restoration Project Portfolio (To be completed within four weeks from contract start) The consultant will: • Compile and systematize the technical information available for the 80 priority restoration sites included in the National Environmental Restoration Programme (PNRA) 2025–2026 portfolio. • Support DGRA technical teams in consolidating, organizing and completing the information corresponding to the priority restoration sites. • Design a standardized institutional project template to compile technical, environmental, ecological, territorial, social, financial and implementation information for each restoration project, providing a common framework for information collection across DGRA Directorates. • Review existing technical documentation, geographic information, restoration objectives, intervention types, implementation status, estimated costs, expected environmental and social benefits, as well as implementation requirements for each priority restoration site. • Identify the information currently available and determine the technical, ecological, territorial, institutional and financial information gaps required to complete each restoration project. • Organize project information into a consolidated institutional database, using the approved institutional project template. • Support technical working sessions with the Directorates responsible for ecosystem restoration within DGRA to validate the institutional template, review information gaps, and agree on the information required to complete each project. • Prepare a project-by-project information gap matrix identifying the missing information, the DGRA Directorate responsible for providing it, and the priority actions required to complete each project file. • Prepare a diagnostic report summarizing the quality, completeness and consistency of the available information, together with recommendations and information requirements needed to consolidate a standardized institutional restoration project portfolio Deliverables • Consolidated database of the 80 PNRA priority restoration sites, organized using a standardized institutional format. • Diagnostic assessment of technical, institutional and financial information, including an evaluation of its quality, completeness and consistency. • Gap analysis identifying missing information required to strengthen investment readiness of each restoration project, including project-specific information requirements. • Standardized technical fiches for all priority restoration sites, prepared using the approved institutional project template, including key indicators comparable between sites. • Presentation of findings and recommendations to DGRA and UNEP, including key information gaps and priority actions required to complete the institutional project portfolio Product 2: Development of a Standardized Institutional Methodology and Project Structuring Toolkit for Investment-Oriented Restoration Projects (To be completed within eight weeks from contract start) The consultant shall: • Review international best practices, methodologies, and standards for structuring investment-ready restoration and Nature-based Solutions (NbS) projects, including relevant experiences from multilateral development banks, international financial institutions, biodiversity finance initiatives, and environmental restoration programmes. • Review existing methodologies currently used by DGRA and other national institutions for project formulation and identify opportunities for harmonization, institutionalization, and future application by subnational governments. • Compile and adapt, in consultation with DGRA, technical criteria and minimum information requirements for project preparation, including implementation considerations, environmental safeguards and monitoring requirements. • Compile practical financial information requirements for project preparation, including estimated implementation costs, operation and maintenance needs, financing requirements, implementation schedules and potential co-financing opportunities. • Develop a standardized institutional restoration project template that can be used by federal, state and municipal governments to formulate, evaluate and structure restoration projects using a common institutional standard. • Develop a project prioritization framework including objective criteria to classify projects according to strategic importance, implementation readiness, restoration impact, biodiversity contribution, climate co-benefits, feasibility, and financing potential ensuring comparability among projects regardless of the implementing institution. • Develop a practical methodological guide describing the complete process for preparing investment-oriented restoration projects under the PNRA, including the application of the institutional project template by federal, state and municipal governments • Conduct technical validation sessions with DGRA to review and refine the proposed methodology and institutional tools, and assess its applicability with potential subnational users. Deliverables The consultant shall submit: • Institutional Methodological Guide for Structuring Investment-Oriented Restoration Projects. • Standardized Restoration Project Template for use by federal, state and municipal governments. • Institutional Project Prioritization Framework. • Project preparation checklist. • Recommendations for institutional adoption and implementation by federal, state and municipal governments. Product 3: Consolidated Restoration Project Portfolio and Financing Opportunities (To be completed within twelve weeks from contract start) The consultant shall: • Consolidate validated project information into a national portfolio of PNRA priority restoration projects. • Classify projects according to ecosystem type, restoration objectives, geographic region,
