UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Open positions at UNESCO Panama Consultant Show advice for this position Application deadline 9 months ago : Tuesday 20 Jan 2026 at 23:59 UTC Open application form Overview Coordinate and strengthen institutional capacities for enhanced governance and project management. You have: University degree in fields related to the service required including education sciences, economics, political sciences, international relations, sociology, and other related areas. Postgraduate certifications in areas of coordination and project management, education, technical education, higher education, or other related areas. At least four (4) years of proven experience in project coordination related to institutional strengthening, governance, and regulations including rules, procedures, indicators, technical studies, diagnostics, marketing, and detailed engineering. Experience in preparing Terms of Reference for public procurement of goods or services. Excellent planning, decision-making, and team coordination skills. Excellent interpersonal skills. Very good command of communication technologies and information. Native Spanish speaker or advanced level proof. Very good oral and written command of English. Contract This is a Consultancy contract. More about Consultancy contracts . Partner --> AI Application Assistant: Maximize your UN job search. AI Application Assistant Details **OVERVIEW** ------------ Parent Sector : Field Office Duty Station: Panama Job Family: Education Type of contract : Non Staff Duration of contract : From 7 to 11 months Recruitment open to : External candidates Application Deadline (Midnight Duty Station Time) : 20/01/2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism **Applicants must be entitled to work in Panama** **DESCRIPCIÓN DE LA POSICIÓN Y SUS FUNCIONES** ---------------------------------------------- **Antecedentes** El Instituto Técnico Superior Especializado (ITSE), mediante la Ley 71 del 8 de noviembre de 2017, como institución de educación superior, cuya oferta académica mantiene alrededor de cuatro escuelas. En su primera fase de desarrollo, el ITSE realizó inversiones para contar con infraestructura y mecanismos de formación docente mediante la capacitación a instructores que se realizó en varios países desarrollados. Con esta base, el Instituto pudo iniciar sus operaciones. Los programas del ITSE confieren títulos de Técnico Superior, cuya validación se da en virtud del carácter autónomo de la institución. En diciembre de 2022, el Banco de Desarrollo de América Latina (CAF) aprobó una segunda operación de crédito para apoyar el desarrollo completo de las dimensiones académica, institucional y de gobernanza del ITSE; con este apoyo se busca, además, culminar la dotación de mobiliario y equipamiento del Instituto y realizar intervenciones complementarias a la infraestructura. Para iniciar la ejecución de esta nueva operación, el ITSE ha incluido al Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) a través del Proyecto “Desarrollo de nueva oferta educativa en el ITSE y consolidación de gestión académica”, como socio dinamizador. El Proyecto tiene por objeto apoyar al Instituto Técnico Superior Especializado (ITSE) a conducir, fortalecer y articular el sistema académico con el sector productivo para gestionar la generación de conocimiento basado en ciencia, tecnología e innovación y ponerla al servicio de los objetivos de desarrollo económico, productivo y social del país, en el marco de los objetivos de la Ley 71 de 2017, mediante la cual se crea el ITSE. Con el Proyecto se busca continuar avanzando en la senda de alinear al ITSE con el sector productivo y social a fin de elevar la calidad de la educación técnica superior, preparando a los estudiantes para integrarse de manera exitosa en el mercado laboral, brindándoles las destrezas y los conocimientos que requiere dicho mercado. Long Description ---------------- Mediante la alianza PNUD-ITSE se establecen las bases para una oferta educativa, de alta calidad académica, que sea pertinente, oportuna, incluyente y sensible al género, contribuyendo así a consolidar la competitividad de país en el mediano y largo plazo en el marco de la economía global. En línea con esta alianza, el ITSE y el PNUD identificaron a la UNESCO, a través de su Oficina Regional para América Central, México y Colombia, como el socio para apoyar técnicamente la conformación y gestión de una Gerencia Externa Especializada (GEE). En el marco del proyecto “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades del Instituto Técnico Superior Especializado para la contratación y ejecución de los paquetes de trabajo en el componente de fortalecimiento académico, institucional y gobernanza”, la GEE tiene por objetivo general apoyar a la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto (en adelante UEP) del ITSE en el desarrollo de las actividades de planificación, preparación técnica y administrativa para la contratación y ejecución de los paquetes de trabajo, aportando conocimiento sobre mejores prácticas nacionales e internacionales en el ámbito de cada componente, y aplicando criterios sistematizados de experiencias exitosas e innovadoras a ser replicadas o adaptadas en la ejecución de los componentes. La GEE realizará la planificación, definición de requisitos técnicos, el acompañamiento durante los procesos de licitación y la supervisión de la ejecución de los paquetes de trabajo del componente de fortalecimiento académico, institucional y gobernanza, incluyendo sus diversos subcomponentes. Esto implica proporcionar asesoramiento técnico especializado tanto a la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto (UEP) como a los demás participantes del ITSE, para garantizar la ejecución integral de las actividades dentro del plazo contemplado. De igual forma, se espera que la GEE desarrolle planes de fortalecimiento institucional para dejar capacidad instaladas en los equipos del ITSE en todos los ámbitos de las intervenciones a desarrollar. Long Description ---------------- **Objetivo de la consultoría** Bajo la supervisión directa del sector educación de la Oficina de la UNESCO para América Central, México y Colombia, y la persona Director /a de la GEE, la persona contratada tendrá el rol de coordinador/a del paquete de trabajo para el fortalecimiento institucional y colaborar en el paquete de trabajo de fortalecimiento de la gobernanza que estará a cargo de la persona Director/a del proyecto. El paquete de trabajo del fortalecimiento institucional incluirá temáticas como: diseño e implementación del Programa para la transferencia de conocimiento, innovación y emprendimiento; rediseño de laboratorios; proyecto “Alumni”; oficina de Empleo; y Estudios de factibilidad. En tanto el relativo al fortalecimiento de la gobernanza, incluirá dimensiones en estos temas: gobernanza base para la gestión; modelo económico; estructura organizativa; normatividad del ITSE; plan de vinculación; y CIIECYT (Gestión), **Funciones** En su rol de coordinador/a, deberá: - llevar adelante de forma completa el apoyo técnico a la UEP - la Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto PNUD-ITSE-, en la implementación del paquete de fortalecimiento institucional. - colaborar con el director/a de la GEE en la implementación del paquete de trabajo relativo al fortalecimiento de la gobernanza. - asegurar la ejecución integral de las actividades previstas en el paquete de trabajo de fortalecimiento institucional en los plazos definidos junto con la UEP- la Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto PNUD-ITSE-, con eficiencia, efectividad, sostenibilidad y excelencia técnica, humana e institucional. - realizar junto al director/a del proyecto, permanentes ejercicio de planificación y monitoreo, sugiriendo y llevando adelante ajustes a los procesos de preparación técnica y administrativa para la contratación y ejecución del respectivo paquete de trabajo. - mantener permanente comunicación con los miembros de la UEP, la UNESCO San José y el personal junto al cual conformará la GEE (1 director/a, 1 coordinador/a) - participación en reuniones dentro de la GEE, con la UEP- la Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto PNUD-ITSE-, UNESCO y otros actores claves, preparando informes, reportes y presentaciones cuando fuera requerido. - Desempeñar otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del proyecto. Las funciones antes descritas se llevarán a cabo tomando en consideración los documentos que orientan las tareas de la Gerencia Externa Especializada, tales como el Término de Referencia de la GEE, el Manual Operativo del Proyecto (MOP), el documento de préstamo de la CAF y el documento de proyecto PNUD-ITSE, entre otros. **INFORMACIÓN RELEVANTE DE LA CONSULTORÍA** **Aplicantes:** Solo pueden presentarse a esta convocatoria y ser consideradas, las personas que tengan permiso de trabajo para Panamá. **Lugar:** Oficinas del ITSE. Contar con certificaciones de posgrado en áreas de coordinación y gestión de proyectos, educación, educación técnica, educación superior, o en otras áreas relacionadas. *Laboral:* -Título Universitario a nivel de licenciatura en carreras relacionadas con el objeto de servicio requerido en este documento. -Experiencia comprobada de al menos cuatro (4) años en coordinación de proyectos relacionados con los paquetes de trabajo de fortalecimiento institucional, gobernanza y normatividad incluyendo reglamentos, procedimientos, indicadores, estudios técnicos, diagnósticos, mercadotecnia e ingeniería de detalles. -Experiencia en elaboración de Términos de Referencia para contrataciones públicas de bienes o servicios. -Excelentes habilidades de planificación, toma de decisiones y coordinación de equipos. -Excelentes habilidades interpersonales. -Excelentes habilidades para realizar distintos tipos de documentos, como informes sobre tareas realizadas, reportes de actividades y presentaciones a distintos públicos. -Muy buen manejo de las tecnologías de la comunicación y la información. *Idiomas:* -Nativo en español o nivel avanzado comprobable. -Muy buen dominio oral y escrito del idioma inglés. postings.text: Paraguay: Consultoría Actualización Plan Nacional Para La Prevención Y El Combate De La Trata De Personas. - Partners Of The Americas Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab RFP : Paraguay: Consultoría actualización Plan Nacional para la prevención y el combate de la trata de personas. Country: Paraguay Posting Date: July 15, 2026 Time Zone: (UTC−06:00) Guatemala City, Guatemala Deadline: August 2, 2026 11:59 pm Status: Open Contact for Enquiries: afigueredo@partners.net Proyecto: Ñangareko Hağua Fuente de financiamiento: U.S. Department of State – Office to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons (TIP Office) Implementado por: Partners of the Americas (POA) Proyecto La trata de personas constituye un fenómeno que afecta gravemente la dignidad y los derechos de las personas, y continúa representando una problemática vigente en la República del Paraguay. En el país, los varones adultos representan aproximadamente un tercio de las víctimas, lo que convierte a este grupo en uno de los más afectados. Provienen en su mayoría de zonas rurales y son explotados principalmente en el sector ganadero del Chaco, así como a través de redes transfronterizas hacia países vecinos. En los últimos años, los casos registrados en zonas de frontera han ido en aumento, tendencia que se ve agravada por el avance de la Ruta Bioceánica, cuyo trazado por el Chaco intensifica los riesgos tanto a escala nacional como regional. En este marco se inscribe el proyecto “Ñangareko Hağua”, financiado por el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos y ejecutado por Partners of the Americas, cuyo objetivo es fortalecer los servicios de protección para varones adultos víctimas de trata, así como la capacidad del personal de albergues no especializados para brindar una atención adaptada al trauma y centrada en las víctimas. En este marco, el proyecto brindará apoyo técnico para la actualización del “Plan Nacional para la Prevención y el Combate de la Trata de Personas en la República del Paraguay (PNTP) 2026-2030” , a fin de incorporar en dicho instrumento los avances, desafíos y prioridades actuales en materia de prevención, combate, atención y protección, incluyendo a varones adultos. Objetivo General de la consultoría Actualizar el “Plan Nacional para la Prevención y el Combate de la Trata de Personas en la República del Paraguay (PNTP) 2026-2030”, a la luz de los aprendizajes, las acciones realizadas y los desafíos identificados en el plan fenecido, mediante un proceso técnico y participativo que incorpore el análisis del contexto actual del fenómeno de la trata de personas en el país, a fin de dotar al Estado paraguayo de un instrumento de planificación actualizado, pertinente y alineado con los estándares nacionales e internacionales vigentes en la materia. ¡Se extiende el plazo de entrega al domingo 02 de agosto hasta las 23.59hrs! Aquí se encuentra la convocatoria completa: TDR_Plan Nacional

postings.title: Research assistant on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)
postings.organization: Ministry of Economy and Finance of the Republic of Uzbekistan
postings.posting_type: Request for Expression of Interest / Individual Consultant Selection
postings.text: TERMS OF REFERENCE  For research assistant on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education) Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) – Uzbekistan Student Loan Program: I. Background The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at expanding equitable access to higher education and strengthening the effectiveness, sustainability, and inclusiveness of student financing mechanisms. As higher education participation continues to increase, ensuring adequate, equitable, and effective financing has become a key priority to support equal educational opportunities and long-term sector development. To support these reforms, the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) represents a strategic investment of US$2 million, financed by the World Bank, to support the preparation and implementation readiness of the Student Loan Program in Uzbekistan. The GFPP finances analytical studies, institutional capacity building, implementation support, and policy development to establish a sustainable and efficient student financing system. The facility supports comprehensive analytical work to assess the current student financing landscape, conduct stakeholder consultations, evaluate international good practices, and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. It also strengthens implementation capacity through the recruitment of specialized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff and fiduciary experts, while supporting national and international training programs for representatives of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES), and other relevant stakeholders. These reforms take place in a context of rapid expansion. Gross enrolment in higher education rose from 9 percent to 21 percent between 2016 and 2022, the number of HEIs grew from 70 to 194, and the Government aims to reach 50 percent enrolment by 2030. Admission is still largely managed through centrally set quotas of places, which are increased every year.2 Public spending on tertiary education has risen more than fivefold in five years to about 0.89 percent of GDP, close to the OECD average. However, the financing model continues to rely heavily on households: around 68 percent of public higher education institutions’ (HEIs’) revenues come from tuition fees; free (state-funded) places, held by about 17 percent of students, are allocated on admission test scores and benefit mostly students from middle- and higher-income families; and government funding to HEIs is based on enrolment alone, so it does not reward labour market outcomes, curricular innovation or industry links.1 The regional “dual-track” model of budget-funded and fee-paying places, combined with centralised quotas that may not correspond to demand for specific programmes, has been found to create an incentive for institutions to retain fee-paying students at the expense of academic standards.2 World Bank analysis has pointed to a package of system-level financing reforms, including a transparent funding formula that combines enrolment with performance on strategic indicators, competitive grants, diversification of institutional revenues and reform of student financial aid. These reforms depend on greater institutional financial and academic autonomy and on reliable data on graduate outcomes.1 The Government recognizes the importance of evidence-based analysis to inform future reforms of the financing of tertiary education, covering both technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and higher education (HE). It also places high value on learning from good practice in relevant and comparable international cases, so that design choices for Uzbekistan are informed by what other systems have done, what results they achieved, and under which conditions. II. The assignment To inform these reforms, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the PIU have engaged an international consultant to carry out research on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and HE). The research covers the general design of TVET and HE financing systems in a selection of relevant and comparable countries, including their institutional and legal frameworks, the incentives they create and their impact on the sector; and countries’ experiences in phasing out admission quotas for students entering TVET and HE, including the finance-related aspects of this transition. It will assess how far these arrangements fit, or would need to be adapted to, the Uzbek context. The work runs from October to December 2026. It starts with an initial review of how TVET and HE are currently financed in Uzbekistan and exploratory desk research on international experience, through which the analytical framework will be refined. It then includes a selection of country cases with national counterparts, in-depth interviews with stakeholders in the selected countries and, subject to confirmation, a mission to Tashkent in mid-November 2026. III. Objective The objective of this assignment is to provide research support to the international consultant throughout the study, by collecting, organising, analysing and synthesising evidence and data on the financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan and in the selected countries, and by supporting interviews, the mission to Tashkent and the preparation of the report. IV. Scope of Work and Deliverables Under the guidance and supervision of the international consultant, who defines the overall methodology of the research, the research assistant will carry out the following tasks: Review of the current system in Uzbekistan. Collect and organise documents and data on the current financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan (e.g., laws and regulations, budget and enrolment data, admission quota decisions, available studies), in coordination with the PIU, and prepare summary tables and notes as requested by the consultant. Exploratory and in-depth desk research. Identify, collect and review relevant documents on the financing of TVET and HE and on admission quotas in other countries (laws and regulations, policy documents, funding rules, evaluations, academic and grey literature), first to help identify countries for the long-list and then in more depth for the selected cases. Data collection and analysis. Where necessary, extract data from available national and international databases (e.g., UNESCO UIS, OECD, Eurostat, World Bank and national statistics) and run specific analyses as requested by the consultant, such as comparisons of funding levels, enrolment and outcomes across countries. Case profiles. Draft short country profiles using common templates developed by the consultant, which will be refined as the research progresses. Evidence management. Set up and maintain a library of sources and references and an evidence matrix that brings together the information collected across countries, flagging gaps and inconsistencies to be checked in interviews. Support to interviews. Support the consultant, who will lead the interviews, by helping to prepare interview guides; identify and contact potential interviewees and schedule interviews; take notes and prepare written summaries of interviews. Support to the mission to Tashkent. Subject to confirmation, travel to Uzbekistan on the same dates as the consultant; support the preparation of meetings in coordination with the PIU; collect documents and data shared by national counterparts; take notes and prepare summary notes of meetings and consultations. Support to reporting. Prepare tables, figures and annexes; check facts and references; and proofread and format drafts of the inception note and report. Deliverables: (1) Collection of documents and data on the current financing system in Uzbekistan, with summary tables; library of sources; and first draft case profiles of long-listed countries; (2) Summary notes of meetings held during the mission to Tashkent (if it takes place); (3) Interview notes, completed case profiles for the selected countries, evidence matrix, and datasets and outputs of the data analyses carried out; (4) Tables, annexes and reference list for the final report. The indicative timetable is as follows: # Activity / Deliverable Indicative days Timeline 1 Collection of documents and data on the current financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan; exploratory desk research on international cases; sources library and first case profiles (Deliverable 1) ~5 days By 20 Nov 2026 2 Support to selection of cases and preparation of interviews and consultations (interview guides, list and scheduling of interviewees) ~2 days 23–25 Nov 2026 3 Support to the mission to Tashkent (if confirmed), incl. note-taking and summary notes of meetings (Deliverable 2) ~4 days November 2026 (same dates as the consultant) 4 In-depth research on selected cases; data collection and analysis; interview notes; evidence matrix (Deliverable 3) ~6 days By 12 Dec 2026 5 Support to finalisation of the report: tables, annexes, references and proofreading (Deliverable 4) ~2 days By 28 Dec 2026 V. Timeline, estimated efforts, and reporting arrangement The assignment will run from 16rd November to 31 December 2026 , for an estimated 20 working days . It may involve travel to Uzbekistan on the same dates as the international consultant (indicatively -November 2026, dates to be confirmed). The assignment is financed under the GFPP. The research assistant will work under the day-to-day guidance and supervision of the international consultant and will report to Zulfiya Mamadalieva (mamadaliyeva.zulfiya@mail.ru) at the MEF. Deliverables will be approved by the MEF and the PIU on the advice of the international consultant. VI. Qualifications Required Master’s degree in economics, education, public policy, social science or other relevant field At least 5 years of experience in policy research or analysis, preferably in education, TVET or public finance Familiarity with tertiary education policy and financing; knowledge of international comparative work is an advantage Strong desk research skills, including working with legal and policy documents Good quantitative skills and experience of working with international and national statistical databases; knowledge of statistical software (e.g., Stata, R or SPSS) is an advantage Excellent organisational skills and ability to manage sources and evidence systematically Excellent written and oral English; knowledge of Russian and/or Uzbek is an advantage Ability to work independently and to meet deadlines Good IT skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and reference management tools Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form in English or Russian languages to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by November 13, 2026. Uzbekistan, 100017, Tashkent, Niyozbek yo'li, 1 Tel:(+99897) 447-86-11 E-mail: gfppp181956@gmail.com Web site: https://www.imv.uz/ Abdurashid Abdurakhmanov   References 1 Bhatta, S.D., V. Babakhodjaeva, M. Kalbfuss, K. McDonall, and M.M. Ferreyra (2024). Advancing Higher Education for Economic Transformation in Uzbekistan. Policy Note. Washington, DC: World Bank. 2 Ambasz, D., D. Nikolaev, S. Malinovskiy, A. Olszak-Olszewski, P. Zavalina, and J. Botero Álvarez (2023). Towards Higher Education Excellence in Central Asia: A Roadmap for Improving the Quality of Education and Research through Regional Integration. Washington, DC: World Bank.

postings.text: NATIONAL INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AUTHORITY – UGANDA (NITA-U)    REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET) PROJECT ID: P171305 LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980   REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00027   ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)   The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)   The consultant will have the overall responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens. The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capability and experience is:   The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are: A minimum of eight (8) years of core business experience in ICT digital skills training, capacity building and skills development consultancy. Demonstrated successful completion of at least five (5) assignments in atleast two or more assignments involving: digital-skills training, digital literacy upskilling, ICT competency development, education technology, or large-scale capacity-building programmes within the past seven (7) years.  Evidence should indicate the client, scope, duration, and status/completion of each assignment. Presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas of; Coordinator/team leader, Trainer-of-trainers, digital skills trainers, Curriculum development specialist, assessment and certification specialist, cybersecurity/digital safety specialist, gender and disability inclusion officer, research/data science officer, and monitoring and evaluation. Please do not submit CVs or biodata of individual experts at this stage .   The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non- Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations “Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025”. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the address below 08:00 to 17:00 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below. Expressions of Interest (One original plus two copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before Wednesday, 18th November, 2026 at 11:00am. The packages must be clearly marked : “Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for the Implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP).”   Address for submission National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U) Palm Courts, Plot 7A Rotary Avenue, 1st Floor Kampala, Uganda Email: jacqueline.musimenta@nita.go.ug   Any form of canvassing or lobbying for the tender shall lead to automatic disqualification   EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

postings.title: International short-term consultant on International good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)
postings.organization: Ministry of Economy and Finance of the Republic of Uzbekistan
postings.posting_type: Request for Expression of Interest / Individual Consultant Selection
postings.text: TERMS OF REFERENCE   For International short-term consultant on International good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education) Grant facility for project preparation (GFPP) – Uzbekistan Student Loan Program I. Background The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at expanding equitable access to higher education and strengthening the effectiveness, sustainability, and inclusiveness of student financing mechanisms. As higher education participation continues to increase, ensuring adequate, equitable, and effective financing has become a key priority to support equal educational opportunities and long-term sector development. To support these reforms, the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) represents a strategic investment of US$2 million, financed by the World Bank, to support the preparation and implementation readiness of the Student Loan Program in Uzbekistan. The GFPP finances analytical studies, institutional capacity building, implementation support, and policy development to establish a sustainable and efficient student financing system. The facility supports comprehensive analytical work to assess the current student financing landscape, conduct stakeholder consultations, evaluate international good practices, and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. It also strengthens implementation capacity through the recruitment of specialized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff and fiduciary experts, while supporting national and international training programs for representatives of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES), and other relevant stakeholders. These reforms take place in a context of rapid expansion. Gross enrolment in higher education rose from 9 percent to 21 percent between 2016 and 2022, the number of HEIs grew from 70 to 194, and the Government aims to reach 50 percent enrolment by 2030. Admission is still largely managed through centrally set quotas of places, which are increased every year.2 Public spending on tertiary education has risen more than fivefold in five years to about 0.89 percent of GDP, close to the OECD average. However, the financing model continues to rely heavily on households: around 68 percent of public higher education institutions’ (HEIs’) revenues come from tuition fees; free (state-funded) places, held by about 17 percent of students, are allocated on admission test scores and benefit mostly students from middle- and higher-income families; and government funding to HEIs is based on enrolment alone, so it does not reward labour market outcomes, curricular innovation or industry links.1 The regional “dual-track” model of budget-funded and fee-paying places, combined with centralised quotas that may not correspond to demand for specific programmes, has been found to create an incentive for institutions to retain fee-paying students at the expense of academic standards.2 World Bank analysis has pointed to a package of system-level financing reforms, including a transparent funding formula that combines enrolment with performance on strategic indicators, competitive grants, diversification of institutional revenues and reform of student financial aid. These reforms depend on greater institutional financial and academic autonomy and on reliable data on graduate outcomes.1 The Government recognizes the importance of evidence-based analysis to inform future reforms of the financing of tertiary education, covering both technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and higher education (HE). It also places high value on learning from good practice in relevant and comparable international cases, so that design choices for Uzbekistan are informed by what other systems have done, what results they achieved, and under which conditions. II. International good practice and strategic choices in tertiary education (TVET and HE) financing Financing systems are not neutral. How public and private resources are allocated to institutions and students – for example through negotiated or input-based budgets, enrolment-based or formula funding, performance-based funding, competitive and grant-based funding, or cost-sharing with students and employers – and the legal and institutional framework that governs these flows shape what is incentivised in the system. Over time, these choices influence which models of TVET and HE emerge (for example, broad mass access versus a more differentiated system with centres of excellence; demand-led versus centrally steered provision; the balance and pathways between TVET and HE), and which outcomes the system tends to produce in terms of access and equity, completion, quality, labour market relevance, research, and the sustainability and predictability of public spending. International experience shows that similar arrangements can lead to very different results depending on their design, on how they are combined, and on the institutional context in which they operate (e.g., system governance, institutional autonomy, quality assurance and data systems). A related question for Uzbekistan is how to manage the number and distribution of places. Several countries have moved away from centrally set quotas for students entering TVET and HE, and the experience of these transitions, including the financial incentives and changes in funding allocation that made them possible, is directly relevant. A structured review of selected international cases will help the Government consider which options, or combination of options, best fit Uzbekistan’s strategic intentions for the sector, and what adaptations would be required. III. Objectives The objective of this consultancy is to support the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the PIU, in coordination with the MoES and other relevant stakeholders, by carrying out research on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and HE). Specifically, the consultant will: review and analyse the general design of TVET and HE financing systems in a selection of relevant and comparable countries, including their institutional and legal frameworks; show how different financing arrangements link to different strategic visions for the sector, what they incentivise, and what impact they have had on the sector, including their benefits and risks; review countries’ experiences with admission quotas for students entering TVET and HE, and the steps governments took to phase them out, with particular attention to the finance-related aspects of this transition (e.g., use of financial incentives, or changes in how funds are allocated and managed in the sector); and assess the extent to which these arrangements are a good fit for, or would need to be adapted to, the Uzbek context and the Government’s strategic intentions. IV. Scope of Work and Deliverables Working with the MEF and the PIU, the consultant will carry out the following tasks: Review of the current financing system in Uzbekistan. Carry out an initial review of how TVET and HE are currently financed in Uzbekistan, including the main sources and flows of funds, the allocation of state-funded and fee-paying places, and the related legal and institutional framework. The review will draw on available documents and data and on discussions with the MEF, the PIU, the MoES and other relevant stakeholders, and will provide the baseline against which international experience is assessed. Methodology and analytical approach. Define the overall methodology of the research, including the approach to case selection, desk research, data analysis and interviews, and an initial framework for comparing financing systems. The framework will be kept broad at the outset and refined as the exploratory research and the review of the Uzbek system identify the most relevant dimensions and questions. Long-list of cases. Through desk research, identify and briefly profile a long-list of countries with relevant experience, based on criteria agreed with the MEF and the PIU (e.g., comparability with Uzbekistan, recent reform of the financing system, experience in phasing out admission quotas, strength of the TVET system). Selection of cases. Present the long-list to the MEF, the PIU, the MoES and other relevant stakeholders and agree on a short-list of cases (indicatively 6–7) for in-depth review. National consultations. Subject to confirmation, undertake a mission to Tashkent in mid-November 2026 to consult and interview national stakeholders (e.g., MEF, MoES, PIU, TVET and HE institutions), in order to deepen the understanding of the current financing system and the quota system and to discuss reform priorities. In-depth review and interviews. Carry out further research on the selected cases and lead in-depth interviews, with the support of the research assistant, with stakeholders and staff of the relevant ministries, agencies, funding bodies and/or institutions, to verify and complement information collected online. Analysis of admission quotas. Review the experience of selected countries in setting and phasing out quotas for students entering TVET and HE, including the sequencing of reforms and the role of financing instruments and fund-management arrangements in the transition. Analysis and recommendations. For each case and across cases, analyse design, legal and institutional arrangements, implementation, costs, impact on the sector, benefits and risks, and preconditions. Assess the fit of each option with the Uzbek context and identify the adaptations, sequencing and preconditions that a transition would require. Coordination of research. Coordinate and quality-assure the research process, including guiding and supervising a research assistant: allocating research tasks, specifying the data to be collected from available databases and the analyses to be run, developing common templates for case profiles and interview notes, managing sources, and collating and synthesising the evidence collected into an evidence matrix that underpins the report. Reporting and dissemination. Prepare the deliverables below, incorporate comments from the MEF, the PIU and other relevant stakeholders, and present findings as agreed with the MEF and the PIU. Deliverables: (1) Inception note with an initial overview of the current financing system in Uzbekistan, the methodology and initial analytical framework, work plan and long-list of cases; (2) Preliminary draft report; (3) Revised draft report, including an executive summary and a summary presentation (PPT). The report will be in English, of approximately 40-50 pages plus annexes with case profiles. The indicative timetable is as follows: S No Activity / Milestone Responsibility Timeline 1 Kick-off meeting with MEF and the PIU; agree methodology and work plan (including tasks of the research assistant); collection of documents and data on the current financing system MEF/PIU & consultant 16-17 Nov 2026 2 Initial review of the current financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan; desk research; long-list of country cases with a short profile of each; Inception note (Deliverable 1) Consultant, with research assistant 18 Nov – 20 Nov 2026 3 Discussion of long-list with MEF, PIU, MoES and other relevant stakeholders; selection of short-list of cases for in-depth review MEF/PIU, Government & consultant 23–24 Nov 2026 4 Mission to Tashkent (if confirmed): consultations and interviews with national stakeholders on the current TVET and HE financing system, admission quotas and reform priorities, and on report outline. Consultant, with support of MEF/PIU November 2026 (dates tbc) 5 In-depth research on selected cases; in-depth interviews with stakeholders and staff in the selected countries to verify and complement information collected online; collation of evidence Consu

postings.title: Consultancy services for the development of Utilities Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPS) in participating countries.
postings.organization: African Union Development Agency - New Partnership for Africa's Development
postings.posting_type: Request for Expression of Interest / Quality And Cost-Based Selection
postings.text: _____________________________________________________ REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)   Country: Multinational Name of Project: Accelerating Access to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in the Eastern and Southern Africa Region Project Grant No .: P506439 Assignment Title: Procurement of consultancy services for Utility Diagnostics, Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPs), Digitalization Maturity Assessment and New IBNET Benchmarking under the AFE WASH MPA Regional Support Project Reference No : 006/AUDA/DITIR/QCBS/2027 Method: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)   Introduction The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “ Procurement of consultancy services for Utility Diagnostics, Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPs), Digitalization Maturity Assessment and New IBNET Benchmarking under the AFE WASH MPA Regional Support Project ”   Description of Services The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Inception and Utility Prioritization : confirms full alignment of the baseline diagnostic methodology with the AFE WASH MPA PAD (P506439), Component 3 results framework, and World Bank ESF requirements , applies a Utility Prioritization Framework ranking utilities. The consultant will work with a maximum list of 06 proposed utilities by the MPA participating countries, and build a database using, key baseline data on utility characteristics, size and performance, but also considering the characteristics of the enabling environment including criteria related to accountability, transparency, government reform commitment, and climate vulnerability to produce the final utility list and country sequencing for Round 1 (Months 1 to 10) and Round 2 (Months 8 to 20) etc; Task 2: NewIBNET Benchmarking including Digital Maturity: conduct a data audit assessing completeness and reliability of existing performance data against NewIBNET KPI requirements (including but not limiting to - NRW rates, billing and collection efficiency, energy consumption per m³, staffing ratios, O&M and capital expenditure per connection), provide hands-on support for data collection, cleaning, formatting, and platform submission, confirm national adoption of the NewIBNET as a preferred/standradized tool for performance assessment, which will translate into successful enrolment within six months of contract effectiveness etc; Task 3: Utility Diagnostic Baseline Assessments: Operational: NRW loss component analysis separating real losses (leakage, overflows) from apparent losses (meter error, illegal connections, data errors); service continuity by zone; production capacity versus demand; O&M practices and maintenance management systems etc; Task 4:Costed Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPs): Costed priority interventions, sequenced in time, assessing impact and feasibility, linked explicitly to the diagnostic root causes they address, and organised by reform dimension, SMART targets for example: reduce NRW from the diagnosed rate to the realistic target / as per resources available to implement the PIAP, by Month X; achieve operational cost recovery of 100% by Month Y; reduce specific energy consumption to the benchmark value by Month Z. These targets should then be calibrated against NewIBNET regional benchmarks etc; Task 5: Capacity Building and Regional Training: Module 1: PIAP Implementation and Utility Turnaround: translating diagnostic findings into managed reform; performance contracting (include successful cases); and turnaround case studies from the AFE region, Module 2:  Leadership and Corporate Governance: board effectiveness; CEO accountability frameworks; performance-based management; customer service culture etc; Task 6:  Knowledge Management and Regional Learning: The Firm shall synthesise all assignment outputs into reusable regional knowledge products and facilitate cross-country learning: minimum five knowledge products in English, French, Portuguese (Regional Utility Performance Report; NewIBNET Participation Guide; PIAP Preparation Methodology Guide; PIAP modelling tool, Utility Digitalisation Primer; Rural Operator Professionalization Framework); at least two regional knowledge-sharing events; postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Georgia Preparation Grant for Georgia Water Supply, Sanitation, Wastewater, and Hazardous Waste Project Grant Number: P518850 Assignment Title: Preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and Associated Environmental and Social Instruments for the Proposed Hazardous Waste Treatment and Landfill Facility in Georgia Reference No .: GFPP /CS/CQS-02 The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Preparation Grant for Georgia Water Supply, Sanitation, Wastewater, and Hazardous Waste Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and associated environmental and social instruments for the hazardous waste management facilities proposed under the Feasibility Study (FS). These may include pre-treatment facilities (for example, segregation, dewatering and conditioning of oily sludges, contaminated soils and chemical residues); treatment facilities (such as physico-chemical treatment, neutralization and stabilization/solidification, thermal treatment); an engineered hazardous waste landfill; and associated storage, regional waste acceptance and temporary storage facilities, access roads, utilities and transport interfaces, as confirmed through the FS and agreed project scope. The main facility may be located near Marneuli, Kvemo Kartli, Georgia, at the site previously assessed for a non-hazardous waste (municipal) landfill, subject to confirmation. Building on the FS, the 2016 municipal landfill ESIA and available studies, the Consultant will undertake inception and scoping, review and validate existing information, identify data gaps and carry out targeted environmental and social baseline surveys and sampling; assess Georgian environmental assessment, screening, registration and permitting requirements for each relevant facility, alongside applicable World Bank Environmental and Social Standards and EHS Guidelines; describe reasonable alternatives considered in the FS and assess the preferred configuration without repeating technical selection or conceptual design; assess construction, operational, closure and post-closure impacts, including groundwater and soil contamination, emissions, effluents and leachate, hazardous waste handling and transport, worker and community health and safety, credible accidents, emergency preparedness, and climate and natural-hazard risks; undertake stakeholder engagement and disclosure; prepare a detailed, costed Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) and agreed additional instruments (in particular, Stakeholder Engagement Plan and Labor Management Procedures); and support statutory scoping, consultation and regulatory review. The ESIA will be coordinated with the FS and engineering teams and will address regional storage and acceptance facilities to the extent required by their confirmed activities, capacities and applicable regulatory pathways. The indicative implementation period is approximately 14 weeks from commencement, plus mandatory statutory review and consultation periods, where applicable. The expected start date is [TO BE CONFIRMED]. Estimated level of effort (professional staff-months): [TO BE CONFIRMED]. The schedule will be coordinated with the availability of FS outputs and applicable regulatory procedures. The eligibility/minimum qualification criteria are: No. Criterion Mandatory minimum requirement Documents / evidence to be submitted 1 Legal status and eligibility Legally registered consulting firm eligible under the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations; no applicable debarment, sanction or prohibited conflict of interest. Registration certificate or equivalent; signed eligibility and conflict-of-interest declaration for each firm/JV member; JV agreement or letter of intent, if applicable. 2 Legal and financial standing Not subject to bankruptcy, insolvency or liquidation proceedings that materially impair performance; no litigation or enforcement action that materially threatens contract delivery. Signed declaration by each firm/JV member; supporting official records if requested. 3 Financial capacity Demonstrated financial capacity to undertake a multidisciplinary ESIA, including field investigations and specialist studies. [Any minimum turnover threshold to be confirmed by the Client.] Summary of annual consulting turnover for the last three completed financial years and audited or certified financial statements, as applicable. 4 Environmental and social assessment experience At least eight years of consulting experience in environmental and social assessment, management or due diligence for infrastructure, waste management or industrial facilities. Company profile and dated list of relevant assignments identifying client, location, scope and services. 5 Comparable ESIA assignments At least two completed ESIAs or equivalent comprehensive E&S assessments within the last ten years for industrial, waste treatment/disposal or other high-risk infrastructure facilities; at least one should concern hazardous waste or comparably complex industrial pollution risks. Assignment reference sheets with client, country, dates, contract role, facility type, E&S scope, principal deliverables and client contact/reference where available. 6 Hazardous waste and pollution-risk expertise Demonstrated firm-level experience assessing hazardous waste treatment, storage or disposal risks, including groundwater/soil protection, emissions, occupational/community safety or accident scenarios. Descriptions of relevant completed assignments and the firm’s actual role; illustrative deliverables or executive summaries where disclosure is permitted. 7 Georgian and international E&S requirements Experience with Georgian environmental assessment and permitting processes and World Bank ESF/ESS or comparable international lender E&S standards including social assessment, stakeholder engagement and land acquisition, demonstrated by the firm or proposed JV/subconsulting arrangement. References describing Georgian regulatory assignments and internationally financed E&S assignments, indicating the standards and approval/disclosure support provided. 8 Organisational and technical capacity Capacity to manage multidisciplinary E&S studies, consultations, baseline fieldwork, sampling/laboratory quality control, specialist inputs and preparation of implementable ESMPs. Organisation chart; summary of QA/QC and project management arrangements; available specialist disciplines and proposed partner/subconsultant roles; relevant laboratory arrangements if applicable. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Georgia Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project No: P173975 Loan No. 9239-GE Assignment Title: Digital Transformation Expert Reference No. GE-GEDC-CS-IC-45 Introduction JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank (WB) intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services of a Digital Transformation Expert, who will operate under the World Bank MSMEs Project structure, while being functionally integrated with GEDC’s Growth Hubs network. The Project Development Objective for the Relief and Recovery for MSME operation is to provide relief to MSMEs and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance. Project Description The Project is implemented nationwide and consist of four components: Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading Component 3 – Project management and Monitoring Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 is implemented by GEDC. It comprises of the following sub-components: Sub-component 1.1 - micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms. Sub-component 1.2 - co-financing interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs). Sub-component 1.3 - partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs. Sub-component 1.4 - technical assistance for COVID-proofing and digitalization of MSMEs. Objectives of the assignment Subcomponent 1.4 of the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project aims to support both the design and the provision of technical assistance to firms to adjust to the post Covid environment through the adoption of relevant managerial, digital, and other relevant practices and supporting the creation of a market for such services. The objective is to supplement the financial support under other subcomponents with technical assistance to address outstanding firm needs in key sectors, informed by stakeholder outreach. This subcomponent will also aim to gauge the feasibility of establishing and eventually scaling the most relevant of managerial capability and digitization programs in the context of Georgia. It will also pilot activities aimed at creation of a local market for firm consultancy services. In order to effectively provide support services mentioned above and ensure coverage and accessibility in all regions, GEDC will be developing Growth Hubs in all regional centres. Scope of Work of the Digital Transformation Expert The Expert will support the implementation of Subcomponent 1.4's digitalization component, ensuring alignment with GEDC’s strategic digital transformation agenda and Growth Hub service portfolio. The Digital Transformation Expert will report to the Head of Business Services Development Division and coordinate closely with the Strategic Development Unit within GEDC’s M&E Department, as necessary, particularly on monitoring, reporting, and knowledge-sharing related to digitalization activities at the Central Office of GEDC. The Expert will play a pivotal role in enabling digital transformation among MSMEs supported through the Growth Hub network. This includes conducting digital diagnostics, recommending tailored digital solutions, supporting implementation, and contributing to knowledge development across regions and sectors. Key responsibilities include: Conduct digital maturity assessments to MSMEs identified through the Growth Hub’s diagnostics, analyze their existing digital maturity level, their business processes, assess the existing technological infrastructure, and identify opportunities and draft a tailored digitalization plan to recommend how to digitally transform their business operations based on their outstanding needs; Provide technical support to MSMEs during the rollout of selected digital tools and solutions, as defined by their digitalization plans; Contribute to building the capacity of Growth Hub staff and partner consultants to apply digital diagnostic tools and support MSMEs’ digitalization efforts; Identify and maintain a roster of credible technology vendors and digital service providers, in coordination with GEDC procurement and technical teams; Recommend appropriate technology platforms for individual MSMEs, considering their size, industry, and operational capacity; Develop and implement, and periodically update/improve methodologies for assessing digital maturity of businesses and contribute to the creation of sector-specific digital transformation roadmaps; Create and maintain a structured catalog of digital tools, platforms, and their providers available on the Georgian market; Collaborate effectively with project partners, internal teams, and external contractors to align on shared goals and work streams; Actively participate in the planning and delivery of educational and awareness-raising activities to promote digital literacy and transformation among current and potential beneficiaries; Engage proactively with MSMEs, responding to inquiries and providing follow-up guidance throughout the digitalization process; Monitor the adoption and effectiveness of digital solutions after implementation, and issue recommendations to ensure sustained impact; Participate in the development of content and input for project progress reports related to digitalization; Perform other related tasks within the scope of the assignment, as required to support the successful implementation of digital transformation initiatives within the project, and as assigned by management; Provide data and inputs on digitalization activities, indicators, and results to the Strategic Development Unit for inclusion in MSME Project monitoring and evaluation reports. Reporting and Deliverables The Digital Transformation Expert shall perform the above responsibilities continuously throughout the duration of the assignment, under the direction of the Head of Business Services Development Division. The specific deliverables include: Monthly contribution to project progress reports, including a summary of digital assessments conducted, tools recommended or implemented, and overall MSME engagement; Quarterly summary of digitalization results, including number of MSMEs assessed, number of digitalization plans developed, and key outcomes achieved, to feed into Subcomponent 1.4 reporting; Maintain and quarterly update a catalog of vetted digital tools and solution providers relevant for MSMEs; Documentation of digital maturity assessments and sector-specific roadmaps developed or updated during the reporting period; Reports on post-implementation monitoring, outlining the effectiveness and outcomes of deployed solutions; Individual Digitalization plans produced for each MSME undergoing digital maturity assessments; Other deliverables or briefings as requested by the Head of Business Services Development Division, related to the digitalization pillar of the Growth Hub project. Document and share case studies or success stories of MSME digital transformation to inform Growth Hub learning and communication efforts Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client: The Client shall provide office area and facilities, office equipment and communication necessary to carry out the assignment. The Client shall also provide all necessary information and documents for that purposes. Qualification and Experience: Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field; At least 5 years of work experience in a position related to the described responsibilities; Practical experience in implementing modern and up-to-date technologies; Experience preparing analytical and performance reports related to digital adoption or SME support Familiarity with enterprise diagnostics, digitalization frameworks, or SME capacity-building programs. Experience in the digitalization of small and medium-sized enterprises; Ability to collaborate effectively with teams involved in or connected to the project; Fluency in Georgian and a strong command of English is preferred. Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client: The Client shall provide office area and facilities, office equipment and communication necessary to carry out the services. The Client shall also provide all necessary information and documents for that purposes. Duration Consultant will be hired under the full-time employment contract. Interested consultants may obtain further information by email: hr@gedc.ge CVs of candidates in English language must be submitted electronically to the address below not later than 15th November. E-mail To: hr@gedc.ge Please include the title of the announced position in subject line of the email.

postings.text: Invitation for Proposals (Consulting Services) UKRAINE Project:                                             Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine (LEARN) Project Grant no.:                                        TF0D0612 Name of the Contract:                     Consulting Services for the Technical Assistance in the design and implementation of the “First Steps Forward” plans in participating hromadas   Contract number:                            LEARN -ECE-1.2-FSF   Ukraine received the Grant No. TF0D0612 from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) in US dollars to finance the Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project and intends to use part of the funds to make payments under the Contract No. LEARN -ECE-1.2-FSF " Consulting Services for the Technical Assistance in the design and implementation of the “First Steps Forward” plans in participating hromadas " .   The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine invites eligible participants (Consultant; Participant) to submit sealed proposals for the provision of the following services: Consulting Services for the Technical Assistance in the design and implementation of the “First Steps Forward” plans in participating hromadas (“Services”). The technical proposals of the consultants will be evaluated in two parts. The following are the mandatory criteria that the consultants must meet. In the case of a JVCA, the Lead Member should have at least 1 assignment specified above while the combination of members must fully meet the requirement. The projects claimed by each JVCA member should be substantially completed during the above period either alone or as a member of a past JVCA with a minimum share of 50%. In case of experience in the role of a member of a past JVCA and/or Subconsultant, the experience and amount will be determined based on the Consultant’s share and responsibility in the past JVCA or the amount of the Subconsultant’s contract. postings.text: KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA NATION RELIGION KING   Skills for Better Jobs Project (SBJ) IDA Credit No. 75480-KH   Request for Expression of Interest (REoI)   CONSULTING SERVICES OF THE FIRM to Consultancy Firm to Support the Upgrading of the Job Matching Portal (Digital) of the National Employment Agency and Developing the Labour Market Information System (LMIS) (MLVT-CS-20-A)   Cambodia Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MLVT) Skills for Better Jobs Project (SBJ) World Bank: IDA Credit No. 75480-KH   Request for Expression of Interest Date: 03 November 2026   Procurement Tittle:   Consultancy Firm to Support the Upgrading of the Job Matching Portal (Digital) of the National Employment Agency and Developing the Labour Market Information System (LMIS) Procurement No.:     MLVT-CS-20-A   The Royal Government of Cambodia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Skills for Better Jobs Project (SBJ) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.   The consulting services (“the Services”) is to address these challenges, MLVT intends to strengthen two key components of the LMIS ecosystem: (i) the development of an integrated LMIS website to disseminate structured labour market information to jobseekers, employers, policymakers, and training providers. It must include the following: Job-matching portal; Counseling Service portal (the Developed Digital Self-Assessment Tool, Graduate survey, Tracer study, Migration data); and Labour Market Intelligence portal. (ii) the enhancement of the NEA Job Matching Portal to improve the quality and transparency of job matching services. These two components will operate as complementary systems that share common taxonomies, datasets, and API services. For in depth understanding of the required services under this assignment, please referred to the ToR of this consultancy for your reference.   The SBJ Project is now invites eligible Consulting firm’ “consultants” to support the Upgrading of the Job Matching Portal (Digital) of the National Employment Agency and Developing the Labour Market Information System (LMIS). The specific objectives of the consultancy are to strengthen selected components of Cambodia’s LMIS by: (1) Providing the technical upgrade of the Job Matching Portal, LMIS website, and supporting infrastructure; (2) Strengthening data and taxonomy governance for consistent classification and interoperability; (3) Enhancing institutional capacity to support effective management and maintenance; The assignment aims to create an integrated digital ecosystem in which it embeds relevant labour market information and insights (e.g., occupational demand trends, skills gap alerts) into the job-matching portal interface to guide informed decisions by jobseekers and employers. The shortlisting criteria are:   The consulting firm must demonstrate substantial institutional experience, technical capability, and a proven record of delivering sustainable digital systems in the employment, labour market, or public-sector domain. Firm must have international experience particularly in system architecture, taxonomy, job matching. The firm must show that it can successfully execute the project within the required timeline and governance environment.   Minimum qualifications include: Minimum 10 years of experience in designing, developing, or job matching systems, MIS solutions, or other large-scale government digital systems involving structured datasets and multi-stakeholder workflows. Experience implementing a job portal or a web-based platform for a Public Employment Service (PES) in a country with a population of at least 5 million is an advantage. (please provide reference) Completion of at least three contracts involving: Development and implementation of bidirectional job matching technology for Public Employment Services Agency is an advantage; Implementation of user-facing dashboards and data-driven search or filter features with API-based integration or modular system development for future scalability; knowledge of system interoperability; and Implementation of structured gap analysis or career pathway module.   Demonstrated at least 3 projects or contracts in developing explainable, rule based, weighted, and bi directional matching algorithms, including transparency features, scoring breakdowns, and fairness considerations and Capability in database restructuring, performance optimisation, data quality assurance, identity resolution, and long-term data governance across bilingual datasets. Demonstrated at least 3 projects or contracts in LMIS or similar labour market analytics solutions, including labour market indicators, Labour Market Taxonomy, dashboards, and data pipelines integrating multiple data sources. Demonstrated at least 3 projects or contracts in CMS implementation for government or private sector or donor-funded content workflows, structured metadata, and accessibility compliance is highly desirable.   Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.   The   detailed   Terms   of   Reference (ToR) for   the   assignment   can   be   found   at   the   link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kKkN11mtxpGJleYKvYZxknn14CxtOUGc/view?usp=sharing     The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, latest revised September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.     Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.   A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the procedures of Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.   Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30AM to 17:30PM at Directorate General of Technical Vocational Education and Training (DGTVET) under Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training, Building 3, Russian Federation Blvd., Toek Laak I, Toul Kork, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, Tel: (855) 17 864 934, Email: moeungjolita@gmail.com   Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 03 December 2026 at 17:00 Local time .   To: Directorate General of Technical Vocational Education and Training (DGTVET) under Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training   Attn: Mr. Thorng Samon Project Manager, SBJ Deputy Director General of DGTVET Building 3, Russian Federation Blvd., Toek Laak I, Toul Kork, Phnom Penh, Cambodia Tel: (855) 17 864 934 E-mail: thorng_samon@yahoo.com , & Cc: moeungjolita@gmail.com , thorng.samon@mlvt.gov.kh
