postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (LEARN-2.6--4-R – Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)   UKRAINE Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program GPE TF0D0613   Assignment Title: Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning) No . LEARN-2.6--4-R Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system. The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources. The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”).  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.   The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest. The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.   TERMS OF REFERENCE for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant) Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning) Contract No. LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project GPE TF0D0613 I. Background Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan). The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan. The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln. The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million. Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million. More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171 The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by: • financing activities for the development of preschool education; • providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms. In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning. II. Objective The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources. III. Scope of services The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to: Analyze the current system of budgetary and strategic planning within the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES), including the application of the program-based budgeting approach; Analyze the alignment of budget programs with strategic objectives and national policy priorities in the education and science sector; Develop recommendations for aligning strategic documents (strategies, operational plans) with MoES budget programs; Ensure integration of strategic objectives and priorities into the budget process (including preparation of budget requests, budget program passports, and reporting); Contribute to the improvement of the structure of budget programs, performance indicators, and effectiveness metrics; Support medium-term budget planning in line with strategic documents; Provide methodological support on the application of the program-based budgeting approach within MoES; Coordinate with the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine on budget planning and alignment of budget programs; Provide methodological and analytical support for public expenditure reviews in relevant MoES sectors; Develop proposals for implementing recommendations from expenditure reviews and ensure their incorporation into future budget planning cycles; Support the implementation of results-based management approaches in the budget process; Assess the effectiveness of MoES budget programs; Prepare analytical materials on the efficiency of public expenditure and achievement of results. Expected Deliverables: Regular reports on the progress of aligning budgetary and strategic planning; Analytical notes on the effectiveness of budget programs and their alignment with strategic objectives; Proposals for improving the MoES budget process: consulting and practical support to the Ministry of Education and Science in implementing results-oriented management approaches; conducting analysis and assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of budget programs of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine; Analyze the implementation of previously provided recommendations and their impact on MoES budget indicators in the medium term, including collection and systematization of recommendations provided by the Accounting Chamber, the State Audit Service, and expenditure reviews conducted during the previous three years, as well as assessment of their implementation status.   IV. Reporting The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Project Co-Coordinator and work in coordination with the Deputy Ministers of Education and Science of Ukraine, relevant MoES directorates, and project managers involved in the implementation of Project activities. On operational matters, the Consultant shall cooperate with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Team. The Consultant shall submit monthly reports to Project coordinator / Project Co-coordinator in hard copy. The reports shall include a description of services provided during the reporting period.   V. Provided resources   MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES may provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).   VI.  Qualification requirements   Minimum requirements (mandatory):   Master’s degree or higher

postings.text: SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT SÉLECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE RÉPUBLIQUE DU NIGER MINISTÈRE DE LA SANTE ET DE L’HYGIENE PUBLIQUE PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES DES FEMMES ET DES FILLES A DES SERVICES DE SANTE ET DE NUTRITION RENFORCES DANS LES ZONES PRIORITAIRES LAFIA IYALI (P171767) Recrutement d’un cabinet chargé de l’audit externe des comptes du Projet LAFIA IYALI au titre des exercices 2026 et 2027, y compris la période de clôture N° de Crédit/Don : 6984-NE/D 904-NE/TF0B6336/E6210 N° de référence : NE-PAAFFSSN-574882-CS-QCBS Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger a reçu un financement de l’Association internationale de développement (IDA) et du Mécanisme de financement mondial (GFF) pour la mise en œuvre du Projet LAFIA IYALI. Il a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif à l’audit externe des comptes du Projet pour les exercices 2026 et 2027, y compris la période de clôture. Les services de consultant (« Services ») consistent à réaliser l’audit financier et comptable du Projet et à produire les rapports correspondants, conformément aux termes de référence, pour les périodes suivantes : du 1er janvier au 31 décembre 2026 ; du 1er janvier au 30 juin 2027 ; du 1er juillet au 31 octobre 2027, au titre des opérations de clôture. Les termes de référence peuvent être obtenus par courrier électronique à l’adresse   lafiaiyaliniger@gmail.com avec copie à aivodji@yahoo.fr et goni_mahamadou@yahoo.fr . Le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique à travers le Projet LAFIA IYALI invite les consultants firmes (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont : Être un Cabinet d’Audit et d’Expertise Comptable indépendant, faisant profession habituelle de réviser les comptes, régulièrement inscrit au Tableau d’un Ordre des Experts Comptables reconnu au plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF ; Justifier d’une expérience d’au moins dix (10) ans, confirmée dans l’audit financier et comptable des programmes sectoriels nationaux financés par la Banque mondiale ; Fournir les références de projets de développement audités en précisant l’exercice concerné. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.15 et 3.16 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants - Juillet 2016, édition de Septembre 2025), relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection de Consultants Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) par mise en concurrence ouverte, telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque Mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants - Juillet 2016, édition de Septembre 2025). Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : Lundi au Jeudi de 8h à 13h et de 15h à 17h30, et le Vendredi de 8h à 12h30 . Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées en personne ou par courrier postal à l’adresse : Unité de Gestion du Projet LAFIA IYALI sise au Quartier Plateau II, Rue Issa Béri, TEL + 227 20 72 63 63/92 11 66 99 , ou par courrier électronique aux adresses suivantes : lafiaiyaliniger@gmail.com avec copie à aivodji@yhahoo.fr et goni_mahamadou@yahoo.fr , au plus tard le 25 novembre 2026 à 17h00 min heure locale . Les manifestations d’intérêt envoyées électroniquement doivent être des fichiers non modifiables ( PDF ). En cas de transmission électronique des dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt et de non-confirmation de leur réception dans les 24 heures ouvrables après leur transmission, le consultant doit relancer toutes les adresses électroniques mentionnées ci-dessus pour s’en assurer.   Termes De Référence Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès des Femmes et des Filles à des Services de Santé et de Nutrition renforcés dans les zones prioritaires LAFIA IYALI (P171767) Recrutement d’un cabinet chargé de l’audit externe des comptes du Projet LAFIA IYALI au titre des exercices 2026 et 2027, y compris la période de clôture 1. CONTEXTE L'amélioration des résultats en matière de santé et de nutrition, d'autonomisation des filles et des femmes pour accélérer la transition démographique pour contribuer à l'amélioration du capital humain au Niger demandera une vision transformationnelle et un engagement dans des efforts à long terme. Le Gouvernement du Niger, s’est inscrit dans une Approche Programmatique Multi-Phases (APM) avec pour Objectif de Développement du Programme de réduire le retard de croissance et de réguler la fécondité chez les adolescentes. L’APM facilitera la réalisation de l’objectif d’améliorer les résultats en matière de capital humain grâce à un engagement à plus long terme, adaptatif, innovant et continu. Les réalisations dans ces domaines, soutenues par les améliorations nécessaires des systèmes et des capacités, ainsi que par la convergence et la coordination multisectorielles, devraient permettre d'améliorer la nutrition, de réduire les maladies des femmes enceintes et des enfants, ce qui, à son tour, devrait entraîner une réduction de la prévalence des retards de croissance et un meilleur développement physique et cognitif chez les enfants. En outre, l'amélioration des comportements et des normes sociétales existantes et profondément ancrées, ainsi que l'amélioration des opportunités de santé et d'éducation pour les filles et les adolescents, devraient entraîner une réduction de la fécondité chez les adolescents. Pour maximiser son impact, le programme devra être étendu et élargi en termes de portée, pour inclure, par exemple, des services ciblant les adolescents. Il visera également à renforcer la convergence avec d'autres secteurs afin de s'attaquer à certaines causes profondes des retards de croissance et de la fertilité chez les adolescents, comme l'accès à l'éducation, l'approvisionnement en eau, l'assainissement et l'hygiène (WASH), la protection sociale et l'agriculture, tout en continuant à travailler sur la création d'un environnement favorable en renforçant les systèmes. Le Gouvernement du Niger, a sollicité et obtenu des appuis financiers de la Banque mondiale et du Mécanisme de Financement mondial (GFF) à travers le Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès des Femmes et des Filles à des Services de Santé et Nutrition (PAAFFSSN) renforcées dans les zones prioritaires (LAFIA-IYALI). Ce Projet s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Plan d'accélération du Capital Humain 2035 adopté par le Gouvernement en 2018 et du Dossier d’Investissement (DI) via le GFF dont le Niger est un pays prioritaire. LAFIA-IYALI se concentrera sur l’élargissement de l’accès et l’utilisation d’un ensemble de services de Santé Reproductive, Maternelle, Néonatale, de l’Enfant et des Adolescents et de la Nutrition (SRMNEA-N). Il couvrira les régions de Maradi et Zinder qui ont les taux les plus élevés de retard de croissance (50%) et de fécondité des adolescentes (plus de 200 naissances pour 100 femmes entre 15 et 19 ans). L’objectif de Développement du Projet qui porte sur une durée de 5 ans est d’accroître l’utilisation d’un ensemble de services SRMNEA-N de qualité et d’améliorer les comportements clés dans les zones ciblées. Les composantes du Projet sont : Augmenter la couverture, l'utilisation et la qualité du paquet intégré SRMNEA-N ; Soutenir la demande pour des services de santé et de nutrition ; Renforcer la gestion de Projet et la capacité institutionnelle ; Composante d’intervention d’urgence (CERC). Il a été prévu qu’une partie des fonds soit utilisée pour le recrutement d’un Cabinet pour les audits des comptes du Projet. 2. OBJECTIF DE L’AUDIT L’objectif de l’audit financier et comptable du Projet d'Amélioration de l'Accès des Femmes et des filles à des Services de Santé et de Nutrition améliorés dans les zones prioritaires (PAAFFSN) est de permettre à un auditeur externe d’exprimer une opinion professionnelle sur la situation financière du Projet à la fin de chaque exercice fiscal et de s’assurer que les ressources mises à la disposition du Gouvernement du Niger par la Banque mondiale à travers le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique (MS/HP) sont utilisées aux fins pour lesquelles elles ont été octroyées.  Les états financiers qui sont produits sont établis de manière à rendre compte de leurs transactions financières respectives. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet LAFIA IAYLI a en charge de maintenir un système de contrôle interne adéquat ainsi qu’une documentation acceptable des transactions. 3. PREPARATION DES ETATS FINANCIERS ANNUELS La responsabilité de la préparation des états financiers, incluant les notes annexes relève de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP) en conformité avec les principes du Système Comptable en vigueur dans l’espace OHADA (Organisation pour l’Harmonisation en Afrique du Droit des Affaires) et plus particulièrement

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Project: Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II) Assignment Title: Consultancy service for Detail Design for Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha] Credit No.: IDA- 7519-ET Procurement Reference No.: ET-DR-RPCU-571065-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank (IDA) and IFAD toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the detailed design of the Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha] in Aseliso Woreda. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following : The objective of the assignment is to prepare a bankable, climate-resilient, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and implementation-ready irrigation scheme in accordance with national standards, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFAD SECAP. Specifically, the Consultant shall: Verify existing groundwater investigations (hydrogeology, boreholes, pumping tests, water quality) and assess long-term sustainability of abstraction; no new production well design is envisaged unless instructed; Undertake baseline, socioeconomic, gender and social inclusion, soil and land suitability, agronomic and agricultural economics studies, and a climate-risk assessment; Carry out topographic and geotechnical surveys and the feasibility study, including technical, economic and financial analysis of alternatives; Prepare the ESIA and applicable ESF instruments (ESMP, SEP, LMP, IPMP, GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment); Prepare detailed designs of the solar-pumped, pipe-supported surface irrigation system and drainage, drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities, cost estimates, tender documents and construction readiness package; and Develop the operation and maintenance framework and Water Users Association arrangements, and build the capacity of stakeholders. The Consultant shall carry out all investigations, surveys, analyses, assessments, stakeholder consultations, designs, cost estimates and tender document preparation to achieve the objectives above, in accordance with generally accepted professional standards, whether or not a specific activity is cited in the Terms of Reference. The estimated level of effort is 25.25 key-expert staff-months. The assignment duration is three (3) calendar months (twelve weeks) from the contract commencement date, and the assignment is expected to start on February 25th, 2027 . The Dire Dawa Administration Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau, LLRP-II Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and services. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address given below. 3. The shortlisting criteria are: Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in irrigation and water resources engineering consultancy services; provide the company profile, registration certificate, and number of years in business; Relevant experience: proven experience during the last ten (10) years in feasibility studies, detailed design and ESIA of irrigation and drainage schemes (preferably groundwater-based and/or solar-powered schemes) and preparation of tender documents; experience on World Bank- or IFAD-financed projects is an advantage. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, irrigated area, contract value, duration and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates; Technical and managerial capability of the firm: managerial and organizational structure, survey and field equipment, design software (e.g. for hydraulic and pipe network design), quality assurance systems and capacity to mobilize field teams. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. 4.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: the selected Consultant will prepare the detailed design, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates, and tender documents for the construction of the irrigation scheme. Accordingly, the Consultant and any of its affiliates, joint venture partners and sub-consultants shall be disqualified from providing goods, works or non-consulting services resulting from or directly related to this assignment, including the construction works and the supply and installation of the solar pumping system. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 8:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m. (East Africa Time) on working days. Expressions of interest must be submitted in written form in English by mail to the e-mail address: diredawallrp2@gmail.com, or in person by November 25, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. (East Africa Time) or The address referred to above is: Dire Dawa Administration Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau / LLRP-II Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU) Street Address: Through Number One Street, Near Dire Dawa Food Complex or in front of Old Dire Dawa Prison, in Dire Dawa Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau at LLRP-II Office, Ground Floor, Room No. 1. Attention: Procurement Officer and Infrastructure Engineer . Mobile No.: +251 920 407 179 and +251 913 354 785.    E-mail: diredawallrp2@gmail.com.   Dire Dawa, Ethiopia Dire Dawa Administration Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II)

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine (MRIT) Housing Repair for People’s Empowerment Project (HOPE) Implementation, Analytical Support and Technical Support Services for the State Register of Damaged and Destroyed Property (RDDP) OPEN INTERNATIONAL PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE Consultancy Services – Firms Selection Country Ukraine Project ID No. P181200 Assignment Title Implementation, Analytical Support and Technical Support Services for the State Register of Damaged and Destroyed Property (RDDP) Reference No. HOPE-C3-17.3 Selection method Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) Contract type Time-Based Ukraine has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Housing Repair for People’s Empowerment Project (HOPE) (the “Project”) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services under Component 3 “Project Management and Capacity Strengthening”. The consulting services (the “Services”) comprise implementation, analytical support and technical support for the State Register of Damaged and Destroyed Property (RDDP or the “Register”). The assignment aims to support the continuous functioning and effective use of the Register and the services implemented on its basis, and to strengthen the Client’s institutional capacity. The Services cover five principal service areas: First-line support and service request analysis: receive, register, classify and analyse user requests; resolve routine issues; escalate matters requiring the Registry Administrator (L2) or the Client (L3); track requests through resolution; and identify recurring issues and best practices. Implementation support: support the roll-out and use of RDDP services and new or updated functionality, update user instructions and collect feedback on implementation. Knowledge Base: maintain, populate, structure and update the RDDP Knowledge Base, including guidance, frequently asked questions and documented resolution practices. User training and methodological support: deliver regular training, webinars and consultations; prepare learning materials; and transfer practical knowledge to users and designated MRIT representatives. Data analytics and dashboards: configure, maintain and develop Power BI dashboards and analytical reports; support data integration, ETL processes and data quality; and transfer dashboards, documentation and configurations to the Client. Duration and contract arrangements The Services are expected to commence upon the contract’s entry into force, and continue until November 30, 2027 . The contract duration may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties in the event of an extension of the Project implementation timelines. The Services shall be provided under a Time-Based contract , with payment based on actual person-hours worked, supported by approved monthly timesheets and Consolidated Reports. Approval is subject to the applicable service levels and reporting requirements specified in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The estimated level of effort is up to 45,360 person-hours . This estimate is indicative and non-binding; the Client has no obligation to utilise the full estimated number of hours. The Consultant shall use Jira Service Management or an equivalent service request management system and other software necessary for the assignment. Microsoft Power BI licences shall be procured and administered by the Consultant as reimbursable costs, subject to the Client’s prior approval and evidence of price reasonableness, in accordance with the ToR and the Contract. L1 ticket receipt, logging, handling and resolution shall be provided from 08:00 to 20:00 on Business Days (12×5) , with escalation and continued monitoring of Critical Tickets as specified in the SLA. Weekly operational reports and monthly consolidated and time and effort reports shall be submitted in accordance with the ToR. Detailed information on the scope, deliverables, reporting, staffing and Service Level Agreement (SLA) is provided in the attached Terms of Reference . Qualification criteria for the Consultant firm The Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine (MRIT) (the “Client”) invites eligible consulting firms (the “Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating the qualifications and relevant experience required to perform the Services. The firm-level criteria are set out below. No. Criterion and Requirement Assessment 1. Financial Capabilities Minimum average annual turnover of USD 600 000 equivalent, calculated as total certified payments received for contracts in progress and/or completed within the last 3 (three) years, divided by 3 (three) years. Pass/Fail 2. Experience in Similar Contracts Successful implementation of 2 contracts within the last 5 years, each of which included: technical support (helpdesk/service desk) of an information system with at least 1,000 active users; at least 1 of the 2 contracts shall have been performed in the area of public registries or the public sector in Ukraine. Experience with public registries developed on the “Diia.Engine Platform”, in particular in terms of their technical support, maintenance, or implementation of changes, will be an advantage. Pass/Fail for mandatory requirements. Diia.Engine experience is an optional advantage for shortlisting 3. Experience with IFIs or Donors Confirmed experience of successful performance of at least one contract within the last 5 (five) years financed by International Financial Institutions (IFIs) or International Donor Organizations, involving the provision of services for the development, implementation, or technical support of information systems, shall be considered an advantage. Optional advantage for shortlisting 4. Experience in Data Analytics and Dashboard Development Confirmed experience in the development and implementation of interactive analytical dashboards for data visualization in at least one public sector project or comparable institutional/client-facing project implemented within the last 5 (five) years, using specialized business intelligence tools, including Power BI or functionally equivalent platforms. Pass/Fail 5. Experience in Knowledge Base Development and Maintenance Confirmed experience in creating, populating and maintaining a structured Knowledge Base for a technical support system in at least 1 project within the last 5 (five) years. Pass/Fail 6. Experience in Training for Government Bodies or Large User Groups Confirmed experience in organizing and delivering training activities (webinars, training sessions) for employees of central or local government bodies, commissions, notaries, or other large user groups with a total number of participants of at least 500 persons. Pass/Fail 7. Mobilization Capacity and Operational Readiness The Consultant shall demonstrate the organizational and operational capacity to mobilize the required team and commence service delivery within 10 calendar days of contract signing. To confirm this, the Consultant shall provide a concise mobilization plan and staffing availability confirmation. Pass/Fail The requirements above reproduce the firm qualification criteria in the ToR. Mandatory qualification requirements shall be assessed on a Pass/Fail basis. Experience described as an advantage is not a mandatory qualification requirement. For a JV, the combined assessment rules set out under “Associations and conflict of interest” shall apply. The Pass/Fail assessment shall apply to the JV as a whole. The mobilization plan and staffing availability confirmation shall cover the JV’s proposed service delivery arrangements, identifying the responsibilities and resources of the relevant members. Key Experts will not be evaluated at this stage of the procurement process. Individual CVs and full Technical and Financial Proposals are not required with the EOI. Key personnel qualifications will be reviewed at the proposal stage in accordance with the RFP and the ToR. Information to be included in the Expression of Interest To demonstrate its qualifications and experience, each Consultant shall submit: A letter expressing interest in the assignment, identifying the Consultant and any proposed association, and providing the name and contact details of the authorised representative. A description of the firm’s core business, organisation, technical and managerial capacity, and staffing resources relevant to the Services. Information substantiating average annual turnover under Criterion 1, including certified payment amounts for the last three years, the calculation of the average and supporting financial records. Relevant contract/project references demonstrating compliance with the mandatory experience requirements and, where provided, experience described in the ToR as an advantage. Each reference shall state the project title, client, country/location, funding source, objectives and a brief description of the project, contract value, commencement and completion dates, current status, the firm’s role and percentage share of participation in the contract (both in percentage and monetary terms), and the functions and outputs actually delivered. Any affiliated or parent firm and its role shall be identified separately. Supporting evidence for the cited assignments, such as relevant contract extracts, completion or acceptance certificates, client references or other documents confirming successful performance and the claimed experience. References shall clearly identify the information-system user numbers, public-sector/registry context, BI tools, Knowledge Base activities and training participant numbers, as applicable. Each contract or project reference and each training participant total claimed under Criteria 2–6 shall identify the JV member whose experience is being relied upon, its role and the services it actually performed. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II)   Credit No.: 7519-ET   Assignment Title: :  Feasibility Study & Detail Designs of  8 (Eight ) Water Supply & Sanitation schemes from existing Boreholes Reference No .: ET-AFR-RPCU-569660-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include : prepare bankable, climate-resilient, technically sound, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and implementation-ready feasibility studies, environmental and social safeguard instruments, detailed engineering designs, cost estimates, and procurement documents for rural water supply and sanitation systems. The Services comprise: surveys, feasibility studies, assessments, engineering designs, environmental and social safeguard instruments, cost estimates, procurement documents, implementation planning, and capacity-building activities necessary to deliver technically sound, economically viable, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, climate-resilient, and implementation-ready rural water supply and sanitation systems in the targeted woredas (teru, dubti, afdera, argoba, hadeleela, semurobi) woredas  of afar region. The implementation period is three (3) calendar months from the date of commencement. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below. The Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business  is in the provision of professional consultancy services related to water supply and sanitation infrastructure development, including planning, feasibility studies, hydrogeological investigations, environmental and social impact assessments, detailed engineering design, preparation of technical specifications, cost estimates, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), and procurement documents. The firm shall have a minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience in providing consultancy services in water supply, sanitation, water resources development, and related infrastructure projects. Experience in rural and multi-village water supply systems, climate-resilient infrastructure.   (b)      General experience: he consulting firm shall demonstrate adequate institutional capacity and experience in providing consultancy services related to water supply, sanitation, feasibility studies, environmental and social assessments, detailed engineering design, and preparation of procurement documents. The proposed key experts shall possess the minimum general professional experience specified in the Terms of Reference, ranging from 6 to 12 years, depending on their respective positions. (c)  Specific experience: Proven   experience  in Water Supply Planning and Feasibility Studies,   planning and conducting feasibility studies for rural, urban, piped, and multi-village water supply systems., detailed engineering design of water supply infrastructure, including groundwater abstraction, pumping stations, transmission pipelines, storage reservoirs, and distribution networks , hydrogeological investigations, groundwater source assessment, borehole evaluation, pumping-test analysis, and sustainable water-resource development., WASH:  planning and designing rural sanitation systems, public sanitation facilities, institutional WASH facilities, preparing Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMP), Resettlement Action Plans (RAP), and other applicable World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) instruments.. Climate-Resilient Infrastructure:  climate-risk assessment and designing climate-resilient water supply and sanitation infrastructure, including solar-powered pumping systems., preparing detailed engineering drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), engineer's cost estimates, experienced in consultancy assignments financed by the World Bank, IFAD, or other international development partners is desirable. (d)        Technical and managerial capability of the firm:  organizational capacity and experience in managing multidisciplinary consultancy assignments related to rural water supply and sanitation planning, feasibility studies, environmental and social impact assessments, detailed engineering design, and preparation of procurement documents. Availability of qualified technical professionals covering water supply engineering, hydrogeology, hydraulic engineering, civil/structural engineering, sanitation, electromechanical and solar energy systems, geotechnical investigations, surveying, environmental and social safeguards, and cost estimation.        Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 7:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. ( east Africa time ), on working days. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) by  20 November 2026 at 9:00 A.M. East Africa Time (EAT). The address referred above is: Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II), Afar Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU) Attn: Procurement Officer Tadesse Gebeyehu , Room No. 7 Tel: +251 33 666 0188, /  +251-912- 68- 90- 22/ +251- 933-80-62-44 E-mail: afarllrp@gmail.com; llrpafar@gmail.com; Semera, Afar, Ethiopia

postings.text: No. 1 Pam Alamba Street, off Mandela, Minna, Niger State, Nigeria | 09054544448, 09033300337 | nigerspinpiu@gmail.com   REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) IDA CREDIT NO.: IDA-76370   CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE PREPARATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT (ESIA) AND RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN (RAP) FOR RABBAH IRRIGATION SCHEME, MOKWA LGA, NIGER STATE REFERENCE NO: NG-NIGER STATE SPIN-580030-CS-CQS PUBLICATION DATE: Friday 6th November, 2026 The Niger State Government, through the Federal Republic of Nigeria, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for payment of the Consultancy Services for the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Rabbah Irrigation Scheme, Niger State. The consulting services (“the Services”) include conducting an ESIA and preparing a RAP for the rehabilitation of the Rabbah Irrigation Scheme, a 1,830 ha net irrigable area (1,960 ha gross command area) on the River Niger in Rabba community, Mokwa Local Government Area. The rehabilitation works include an 11.4 km protective dyke, a new river intake, delivery sump and rising main, rehabilitation of the main, secondary and tertiary canals with their drainage and hydraulic structures, 55.8 km of access and service roads, a 1,308 kWp solar photovoltaic pumping system and a Water User Association office and shed. The Services include the preparation of the Scoping, Draft and Final ESIA and RAP Reports, including the Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), a Critical Habitat Assessment and Biodiversity Management Plan, a Climate Change Risk Assessment, a Pest Management Plan and Integrated Vector Management Plan, labour influx, SEA/SH and occupational health and safety plans, a grievance redress mechanism, a 100% census and asset inventory of Project Affected Persons, stakeholder consultations, time-based technical support for RAP implementation, and all other deliverables specified in the Terms of Reference (ToRs), in accordance with applicable national regulations and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). The detailed Terms of Reference (ToRs) for the assignment is available upon request via: nigerspinprocurement@gmail.com The Niger State Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: 1.       Proven experience as an Environmental and Social Management consulting firm in the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) for irrigation, water resources, dam rehabilitation, agricultural or similar infrastructure projects. 2.       Demonstrated working knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), particularly ESS1, ESS5, ESS6 and ESS10, gained through hands-on experience in preparing and implementing environmental and social instruments for World Bank-financed or equivalent donor-funded projects. 3.       A minimum of eight (8) years’ relevant experience in environmental and social assessment and resettlement planning for irrigation, water resources, dam rehabilitation or similar infrastructure projects, including a minimum of five (5) years’ experience in civil works contracts requiring environmental management procedures and mitigation measures. 4.       Successful completion of at least three (3) similar ESIA and RAP assignments for World Bank-financed or equivalent donor-funded projects. 5.       Demonstrated experience in: environmental and social baseline studies, impact assessment and stakeholder engagement, including engagement with farmers, herders and water users; socio-economic surveys, census, asset inventory and valuation, and livelihood restoration planning; Critical Habitat Assessment and biodiversity management under ESS6, climate change risk assessment and hydrological modelling for riverine irrigation systems; occupational health and safety, gender and GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment, and preparation of ESMPs; and work in Nigeria or in a developing country under similar conditions, preferably in savanna agro-ecological zones similar to Mokwa LGA.   6.       Availability of adequate organizational and technical capacity, including access to a multidisciplinary team capable of undertaking assignments of similar scope and complexity, and field personnel fluent in Nupe, Hausa or Fulfulde. 7.       Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and report-writing skills. Please note: The Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, Paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Seventh Edition, September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Interested Consulting Firms must be independent of and have no affiliation with any firm engaged in the design or construction of the Project. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The consultancy services are expected to be completed within sixteen (16) weeks from the commencement date, during which the Consultant shall undertake the ESIA and RAP assignments concurrently in accordance with the Terms of Reference (ToRs). The Scoping Reports are due four (4) weeks, and the Draft Reports twelve (12) weeks, after contract signing. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8:00 am to 4:00 pm (local time). Expressions of Interest must be delivered in writing to the address below, both in person and by e-mail, on or before Friday, 20th November, 2026 by 12 noon . The State Project Coordinator, Attn: The State Project Coordinator Niger State Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project Implementation Unit, No. 1 Pam Alamba Street, off Mandela, Minna, Niger State, Nigeria Tel: 09054544448, 09033300337 Email address: nigerspinprocurement@gmail.com     Signed: State Project Coordinator

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES -INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) The AmharaNationalRegional State Bureau of Labour and Skill invites qualified and eligible applicants for the position of Youth Employment Specialist under the Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP) financed by the World Bank. Youth Employment Specialist for the following city City Required No. Procurement Reference Number Debre Brehan 1 ET-AMHARA UDIB-561136-CS-INDV   The Consulting Service (The Services) include the Youth Employment Specialist will lead, coordinate, and provide technical expertise for all youth-focused activities at the city level. Duties and responsibilities: A. Planning and Strategy Develop a city-level annual work plan and budget for youth employment activities. Identify and map potential host employers (private companies, NGOs, and public institutions) for the Apprenticeship Program. Design outreach strategies to recruit eligible vulnerable youth according to project guidelines. B. Implementation of the Apprenticeship Program Facilitate the matching process between youth interests/skills and employer needs. Draft and manage Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between the project, host employers, and apprentices. Organize and deliver pre-apprenticeship orientation and soft skills training (e.g., work ethics, communication, Life skill). Ensure the timely payment of stipends or subsidies to participants. C. Stakeholder Engagement Establish and maintain a City Youth Employment Taskforce or Committee. Liaise with Vocational Training Centers (TVETs) to align training with market demand. Advocate for the permanent hiring of apprentices by host employers upon program completion. D. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) Conduct regular site visits to monitor the quality of mentorship and safety at host workplaces. Maintain an accurate database of all program participants and their employment status. Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual progress reports highlighting achievements, challenges, and lessons learned. The duration of assignment will be for one-year contract, with a possibility of extension upon satisfactory performance of the consultant.   Required Competencies The Youth Employment Specialistshould have the following required experience and qualification to properly carryout the assignment: Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Management, Sociology, Development Studies, Business administration, Public administration, Business management, or a related field. Experience: * Minimum of 5 or 3 years of professional experience in youth development, employment services, or labor market programs. Proven experience in managing apprenticeship or internship schemes . Familiarity with the urban poverty context and social protection programs (experience with World Bank-funded projects is a plus). Skills: * Strong networking and negotiation skills with private sector actors. Excellent report writing and data management capabilities. Fluency in the local language and the official working language.   The Bureau now invites eligible individual consultants/Specialists to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Academic Qualification and Experience as youth employment specialist, Technical Expertise : Proven track record in designing and managing Apprenticeship Programs or large-scale internship schemes, Stakeholder Engagement : Demonstrated ability to negotiate with private sector employers and coordinate with government offices, Reporting & MIS : Experience in data collection, using MIS tools for project tracking, and high-quality technical report writingand Relevant training :Life skill, Job searching,digital skill, Peer meeting facilitation, Training of trainers  and Entrepreneurship. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III paragraph 3.16 and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Procurement In Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (recent Edition) (“Procurement Regulation”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  A Consultant will be selected in accordance to Section VII para 7.34 to 7.39 of The World Bank Procurement Regulation based on qualification and relevant experience of the applicants to the assignment. Remunerations: will be as per the Ministry of Finance channel one salary scale. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 2:30  to 6:30in the morning and from 7:30 pm to 11:30 local time in the afternoon. Expressions of interest (including recent and comprehensive CV with a letter of application indicating the city and other relevant supporting documents) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by  Nov 18, 2026  on or before 4:00pm The address:- Attn: Ato Fikremariam Yeneabat Representative Deputy Bureau Head (job creation sector) Fourth Floor, Office No: 402 E-mail : yeneabatfikremariam@gmail.com Tel: 0582201372 Amhara National Regional State Bureau of Labour and Skill Country :- Bahir Dar, Ethiopia

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES -INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION) The AmharaNationalRegional State Bureau of Labour and Skill invites qualified and eligible applicants for the position of Youth Employment Specialist under the Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP) financed by the World Bank. Youth Employment Specialist for the following city City Required No. Procurement Reference Number DebreMarkos 1 ET-AMHARA UDIB-561143-CS-INDV   The Consulting Service (The Services) include the Youth Employment Specialist will lead, coordinate, and provide technical expertise for all youth-focused activities at the city level. Duties and responsibilities: A. Planning and Strategy Develop a city-level annual work plan and budget for youth employment activities. Identify and map potential host employers (private companies, NGOs, and public institutions) for the Apprenticeship Program. Design outreach strategies to recruit eligible vulnerable youth according to project guidelines. B. Implementation of the Apprenticeship Program Facilitate the matching process between youth interests/skills and employer needs. Draft and manage Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between the project, host employers, and apprentices. Organize and deliver pre-apprenticeship orientation and soft skills training (e.g., work ethics, communication, Life skill). Ensure the timely payment of stipends or subsidies to participants. C. Stakeholder Engagement Establish and maintain a City Youth Employment Taskforce or Committee. Liaise with Vocational Training Centers (TVETs) to align training with market demand. Advocate for the permanent hiring of apprentices by host employers upon program completion. D. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) Conduct regular site visits to monitor the quality of mentorship and safety at host workplaces. Maintain an accurate database of all program participants and their employment status. Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual progress reports highlighting achievements, challenges, and lessons learned. The duration of assignment will be for one-year contract, with a possibility of extension upon satisfactory performance of the consultant.   Required Competencies The Youth Employment Specialistshould have the following required experience and qualification to properly carryout the assignment: Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Management, Sociology, Development Studies, Business administration, Public administration, Business management, or a related field. Experience: * Minimum of 5 or 3 years of professional experience in youth development, employment services, or labor market programs. Proven experience in managing apprenticeship or internship schemes . Familiarity with the urban poverty context and social protection programs (experience with World Bank-funded projects is a plus). Skills: * Strong networking and negotiation skills with private sector actors. Excellent report writing and data management capabilities. Fluency in the local language and the official working language.   The Bureau now invites eligible individual consultants/Specialists to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Academic Qualification and Experience as youth employment specialist, Technical Expertise : Proven track record in designing and managing Apprenticeship Programs or large-scale internship schemes, Stakeholder Engagement : Demonstrated ability to negotiate with private sector employers and coordinate with government offices, Reporting & MIS : Experience in data collection, using MIS tools for project tracking, and high-quality technical report writingand Relevant training :Life skill, Job searching,digital skill, Peer meeting facilitation, Training of trainers  and Entrepreneurship. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III paragraph 3.16 and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Procurement In Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (recent Edition) (“Procurement Regulation”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  A Consultant will be selected in accordance to Section VII para 7.34 to 7.39 of The World Bank Procurement Regulation based on qualification and relevant experience of the applicants to the assignment. Remunerations: will be as per the Ministry of Finance channel one salary scale. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 2:30  to 6:30in the morning and from 7:30 pm to 11:30 local time in the afternoon. Expressions of interest (including recent and comprehensive CV with a letter of application indicating the city and other relevant supporting documents) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by  November 18, 2026  on or before 4:00pm The address:- Attn: Ato Fikremariam Yeneabat Representative Deputy Bureau Head (job creation sector) Fourth Floor, Office No: 402 E-mail : yeneabatfikremariam@gmail.com Tel: 0582201372 Amhara National Regional State Bureau of Labour and Skill Country :- Bahir Dar, Ethiopia

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (Consulting Services – Individual Selection) Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor Country Ethiopia Project Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Project ID P179040 Assignment Title Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor Reference No. ET-NIDP-573612-CS-INDV The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds to select an individual consultant. The National ID Program is looking for a Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor located at the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) to support the implementation of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project with respect to providing high-level technical expertise in translating the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation into practical and technically implementable standards, safeguards, and supervisory mechanisms, among others. The primary objective of the assignment is to provide high-level technical expertise to support ECA in translating the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation into practical and technically implementable standards, safeguards, and supervisory mechanisms. The Advisor will bridge technology, cybersecurity, data governance and privacy, enabling ECA to assess risks associated with existing and emerging technologies, strengthen technical compliance audits and DPIA assessments, develop appropriate standards and assessment tools, advise on data localization and cross-border data transfers, support breach-response mechanisms, and enhance the Authority’s oversight of digital platforms and data markets. Scope of Service and specific tasks      Scope of Services The Technical Advisor shall provide specialized technical advisory, assessment, regulatory development, capacity-building, and supervisory support to the Authority in the implementation and enforcement of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and other applicable legal and regulatory instruments. The scope of services shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Technology Foresight and Advisory: Advise ECA on the privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory implications of existing and emerging technologies. Technical Standards Development : Develop technical standards, guidelines, and security baselines for secure personal data processing, storage, and transfer. Technical Risk Assessments : Conduct system reviews, security assessments, and DPIAs for high-risk personal data processing activities. Technical Compliance and Supervision: Develop audit tools and support ECA's inspections and technical compliance assessments of data controllers and processors. Breach and Incident Response : Develop incident-response procedures and support technical investigations, root-cause analysis, and remediation monitoring. Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement: Develop training materials and deliver technical training and workshops for ECA staff and relevant stakeholders. Technical Coordination and Other Duties: Collaborate with relevant ECA departments and stakeholders and undertake related assignments directed by ECA leadership within the scope of the assignment.     Specific Tasks Based on the above Scope of Service, the Technical Advisor shall perform the following specific tasks: Technology Foresight and Strategic Technical Advisory Development of Technical Standards and Security Baselines Technical Assessments, System Reviews, and DPIAs Technical Compliance Audits and Supervisory Support Personal Data Breach and Security Incident Management Technical Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Additional Assignments Minimum Qualifications and Experience The candidate is required to have the following minimum Qualifications and Experience: A Master's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Telecommunications/Communications Engineering or a related field; At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience in cyber security, technology strategy, digital transformation, data architecture, emerging technologies, technology governance or a related field; Strong knowledge and demonstrated practical understanding of AI, biometrics, digital identity, cloud computing, privacy-enhancing technologies, data technologies and other emerging technologies; Good understanding of personal data protection, privacy by design and by default, and technology-related regulatory requirements; Experience working with digital public infrastructure, telecommunications, financial services or other complex technology environments is an advantage; Experience or knowledge in RegTech and technology-enabled regulatory solutions is desirable; Strong analytical, research, communication and report-writing skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues to legal, policy and regulatory audiences; Relevant professional certifications in data protection, privacy, cybersecurity, information technology or related fields are an advantage; and Excellent command of written and spoken English and Amharic. Duration and Location The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopian Communication Authority (ECA) The Technical Advisor shall report to the Director General or the designated Deputy Director General/Director responsible for personal data protection, or another designated ECA supervisor. The Advisor shall work in close coordination with the Personal Data Protection Directorate and other relevant ECA departments. The Advisor shall submit deliverables in editable electronic format, together with supporting technical documentation, assessment tools, and presentation materials where applicable. Reports containing sensitive information shall be handled in accordance with ECA's applicable confidentiality, information-security, and records-management requirements. Selection Method The selection method is based on paragraphs 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016, as revised, including February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Submission of Expression of Interest National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Expression of Interest should include a CV, formal application/cover letter, and documentary evidence supporting the stated qualifications and experience, including descriptions of relevant assignments and experience in similar conditions. Expressions of interest must be submitted by e-mail on or before November 16, 2026. Further information may be obtained by e-mail during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time. Submission Address: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, National ID Program (NIDP) Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project Attn: Dr. Mesfin Belachew - Project Management Unit (PMU) Director Attn: Project Management Unit (PMU), Address: Welosefer Bole, Ethio-China St, INSA Building, 15th Floor, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Tele- +251 911 791462 or +251-912-200295 E-mail: mesfin@id.gov.et and copy to nejmedin@id.et Website: https://id.gov.et/ Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

The Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development (MIRD) and the P.I. “Office for External Assistance Programs Management” (OEAPM) Project Implementation Unit (PIU) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria is: At least 5 (five) years of experience in combining seismic/RVS methodology knowledge, building screening and vulnerability assessment, GIS/spatial data modelling, data quality control and QA/UAT design , together with IT business analysis for digital data-collection systems. Only the firm’s relevant experience and qualifications will be assessed at the shortlisting stage. Key Experts are not required to be proposed and will not be evaluated at this stage.   The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. deliverables. 21 Technical meetings and consultations. 21           Background and Rationale The Government of the Republic of Moldova is implementing the Strengthening Moldova's Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project (SMORE), financed by the World Bank. The Project aims to strengthen the country's preparedness and resilience to natural hazards and climate-related shocks, including through improved policy, regulatory and technical instruments for disaster risk reduction. This assignment is part of Subcomponent 3.1 – Policy, Regulatory, and Feasibility Study Support to Reduce Seismic Risk. Within this Subcomponent, the Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) of buildings represents one of the foundational mechanisms for collecting standardized exposure and vulnerability information at building level. RVS data feed directly into the seismic risk assessment chain — combined with the seismic hazard outputs developed under Activity 1a and with the seismic risk map methodology developed under Activity 1c — and constitute a primary input for prioritization of risk reduction interventions, retrofit feasibility studies, public-investment planning and emergency preparedness. The Republic of Moldova is exposed to significant seismic hazard, primarily generated by the Vrancea intermediate-depth seismic source (Romania), which has historically affected the entire territory of the country. The 1940 (M 7.4) and 1977 (M 7.2) earthquakes demonstrated the vulnerability of the existing building stock and underlined the need for a systematic, standardized and traceable building inventory and screening process. In this context, RVS is recognized internationally — through methodologies such as FEMA P-154/P-155, EMS-98 vulnerability classification and EU national approaches — as a cost-effective first-tier tool for building-level screening prior to detailed engineering assessment. Role and scope of the RVS mobile application The RVS mobile application is, by design, an operational tool for standardized field data collection, executed in accordance with the RVS methodology described in Government Decision No. 334 of 05.06.2025 and with the quality-assurance requirements applicable under the Project. Together with the web-based administration and data-management portal defined in Section 3.4, it forms a single digital data-collection solution operating on one controlled backend database. The application shall ensure that building-level exposure and vulnerability information is collected in a uniform, controlled and traceable manner, so that the resulting dataset is fit-for-purpose for seismic risk assessment, GIS integration, prioritization and future regulatory or investment decisions. The mobile application shall not, however, be treated as the primary technical substance of this assignment. The critical quality risk under Activity 1b is not the coding of a mobile application as such, but the correct translation of seismic risk principles, RVS methodology, building typology, vulnerability indicators, field screening logic, scoring rules, data validation and GIS/export requirements into a clear, complete, testable and procurement-ready functional and technical specification. The future software solution is expected to implement standard mobile data-collection functions — structured forms, role-based access, mandatory fields, photo and GPS capture, offline operation, synchronization, review/validation status, export and audit trail — and is not expected to perform complex seismic modelling or scientific hazard calculations within the application itself. Justification and need The Republic of Moldova currently lacks a unified, digital building inventory aligned with modern RVS practice and with the requirements of GD 334/2025. Existing building data are fragmented across cadastral, statistical and sectoral sources, are not structured around vulnerability/exposure indicators, do not follow a controlled data dictionary, and are not directly usable as input for seismic risk analysis. A procurement-ready specification for an RVS mobile application and the underlying data-collection workflow is therefore a precondition for: the practical operationalization of the RVS methodology established by GD 334/2025; the production of a building-level dataset compatible with the seismic risk map methodology developed under Activity 1c; the integration of exposure and vulnerability data with the seismic hazard zoning produced under Activity 1a; the prioritization of buildings for detailed seismic assessment, retrofit feasibility studies and/or public-investment decisions; the alignment of national practice with EU and international RVS methodologies (FEMA P-154/P-155, EMS-98, GNDT and equivalent); the preparation of a defensible, technology-neutral procurement of the future application development service, in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations. Accordingly, this assignment is required to translate the RVS methodology, institutional needs and QAP requirements into a clear, procurement-ready functional and technical specification for digital data-collection solution (mobile application and administration portal)and the associated data-collection workflow.
