Cross-ToR coordination and Common Data Standard. 13 Quality Assurance and Technical Requirements. 14 Compatibility with Eurocode 8 and relevant NCM framework. 14 Technical traceability of data, assumptions and calculations. 15 Internal QA/QC.. 15 Peer-review, if required. 15 Version Log, Comment Log and Data Register 15 GIS metadata and digital package. 16 Acceptance of deliverables by the Beneficiary. 16 Deliverables and Timeline. 17 Reporting and Format of Deliverables. 18 Language of deliverables, reporting process and final submission package. 18 Required formats: DOCX, PDF, XLSX/CSV, GIS files, maps, metadata, calculation annexes and editable files. 18 Key Qualification Requirements. 19 Key Expert 1 — Team Leader / Senior Seismic Design, Hazard Interpretation and Methodology Specialist 19 Key Expert 2 — Geotechnical / Engineering Geology Specialist 20 Key Expert 3 — Seismic Design and Application Rules Specialist (EC) 20 Key Expert 4 — Seismologist / Seismic Hazard Specialist (PSHA-GMPE) 21 Non-Key Experts / Support Experts. 21 Client’s Inputs and Institutional Coordination. 22 Available documents. 22 Coordination with MIRD and OEAPM/PIU.. 22 Access to available data. 22 Comments on deliverables. 23 Technical meetings and consultations. 23       Background and Rationale The Government of the Republic of Moldova is implementing the Strengthening Moldova’s Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project (SMORE), financed by the World Bank. The Project aims to strengthen the country’s preparedness and resilience to natural hazards and climate-related shocks, including through improved policy, regulatory and technical instruments for disaster risk reduction.   This assignment is part of Subcomponent 3.1 – Policy, Regulatory, and Feasibility Study Support to Reduce Seismic Risk, which includes technical assistance for the development of methodologies, regulatory documents and supporting tools aimed at reducing seismic risk in the Republic of Moldova. Within this framework, the development of a methodology for seismic hazard design parameters for ultimate and serviceability limit states at the finest administrative unit level is required as a key technical input for seismic design, seismic hazard assessment and future seismic risk mapping.   The methodology will support the modernization and harmonization of the national construction regulatory framework with relevant European standards, in particular Eurocode 8 and the corresponding Moldovan construction norms (NCM). It will also provide the technical basis for the preparation of seismic zoning maps and associated GIS datasets, to be used by public authorities, designers, engineers and other relevant stakeholders.   The zoning of design acceleration is a fundamental element for both: i) the seismic design and verification of buildings and structures according to applicable technical regulations; and ii) the development of seismic risk assessment tools, including seismic risk maps, where hazard information must be combined with exposure and vulnerability data. Subcomponent 3.1 treats this deliverable as a core technical product that must be scientifically justified, traceable, reproducible and compatible with GIS-based risk analysis.   Therefore, the purpose of this assignment is to ensure that the Republic of Moldova has a clear, technically sound and nationally applicable methodology for zoning seismic hazard design parameters for ultimate and serviceability limit states at the finest administrative unit level, supported by documented assumptions, validated input data, transparent calculations, maps, GIS files, metadata and quality assurance records. The resulting methodology will contribute to strengthening seismic safety, improving the consistency of future NCM provisions and supporting evidence-based seismic risk reduction decisions.   Currently, the Republic of Moldova does not have an updated national seismic hazard methodology and zoning map fully harmonized with European practice (Eurocode 8). The existing regulatory framework relies on legacy provisions that no longer reflect the state of the art in probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA), updated seismicity catalogues, modern ground-motion prediction equations (GMPE), or the harmonization requirements with the Romanian seismic zoning (essential for coherent values in border areas). The development of a robust, traceable, and reproducible methodology for seismic hazard zoning is a precondition for: the elaboration of the NCM "Seismic design of buildings" harmonized with Eurocode 8; the elaboration of the national Interactive Seismic Risk Map; the application of the Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) methodology under GD 334/2025; the prioritization of public-building retrofit and feasibility-study activities; the alignment with EU practice and with neighbouring countries (in particular Romania), ensuring coherent hazard values in border areas. Objective of the Assignment The general objective of the assignment is to develop a clear, technically sound and nationally applicable methodology for the zoning seismic hazard design parameters for both the ultimate limit state (ULS) and the serviceability limit state (SLS), at the finest administrative-territorial unit level (level I administrative-territorial units — communes, towns/cities and municipalities), on the territory of the Republic of Moldova. The methodology shall provide the technical basis for defining seismic design parameters to be used in construction design, assessment and future regulatory updates, while ensuring compatibility with the national construction framework, relevant Moldovan Construction Norms and the principles of Eurocode 8. The seismic hazard design parameters shall be expressed as free-field ground-surface values, in accordance with the site-condition treatment defined in Section 3.5, and not as values for engineering bedrock or for a single uniform reference ground class. The assignment aims to establish a transparent and justified methodological approach for assessing seismic hazard and translating the results into zoning maps and design values applicable across the territory of the Republic of Moldova. The Consultant shall define the required input data, assumptions, calculation approach, seismic hazard parameters, zoning rules, validation steps and the structure of the final technical outputs, including maps and GIS/digital datasets. The specific objective of the services is to ensure that the resulting methodology can be used by public authorities, technical committees, designers, engineers and other relevant stakeholders as a reliable reference for seismic design and seismic risk reduction. postings.text: Request for Expression of Interest  Country: Kosovo  Project IDs: P507659 and P507881  Reference Nr.:  TTFP-CS-IC-3.026  Project Names: Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 (WBTTFP) and Kosovo Financial Sector Development (FinDev)     Position: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist  Background  The Government of Kosovo (GoK), with support from World Bank financing, has established the Central Support Division for Implementing Development Projects (CSD) within the Ministry of Finance (MF). The CSD will serve as a centralized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for selected development projects where the GoK or independent public institutions are direct beneficiaries.   The CSD and its PIU will support the implementation of two World Bank-financed projects: the Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 Project (P507659) and the Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project (P507881).  The Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 Project is supported through a combination of EUR 12 million grant financing and EUR 34.7 million loan financing. Its objective is to increase trade and transport efficiency and strengthen quality infrastructure in Kosovo and the Western Balkans region. The project will finance improvements at key Border Crossing Points, modernization of customs and border services infrastructure, procurement of equipment, and digitalization of trade-related procedures through systems such as the National Single Window (NSW), the New Computerized Transit System (NCTS), and upgrades to ASYCUDA. It will also support investments to improve market competitiveness, including laboratory equipment for quality testing, an e-tolling system, 5G corridor infrastructure, road safety improvements, and rail safety upgrades at selected railway level crossings.  The Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project is supported through an EUR 49.3 million loan and aims to improve financial stability and inclusion in Kosovo. The project will support the strengthening of the Deposit Insurance Fund of Kosovo, by providing the capital needed to increase the deposit insurance coverage limit and reduce the payout period for insured depositors following an insured event. It will also expand access to finance for underserved firms through Partial Credit Guarantees via the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund, support the development of a National Development Bank, and finance the development of a modern and interoperable Fast Payment System to promote faster and more efficient digital payments.  Both projects include activities aimed at strengthening project management and implementation capacity, including capacity building for the CSD, PIU staff, and relevant public institutions involved in project implementation. The PIU will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination and implementation of project activities, including fiduciary, technical, monitoring, reporting, and coordination functions, in cooperation with the relevant beneficiary institutions and World Bank task teams.  Responsibilities of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist  The objective of this consultancy is to establish, operationalize, and maintain a robust, integrated Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) system for TTFP 2.0 and FinDev in Kosovo. The M&E Specialist will ensure systematic tracking, validation, analysis, and reporting of all Project Development Objectives (PDO) indicators, Intermediate Results Indicators (IRIs), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) metrics, and citizen engagement/gender indicators in strict alignment with the Project Results Framework, Project Operations Manual (POM), and World Bank reporting guidelines.  The M&E Specialist will ensure that project activities for both projects are systematically monitored, evaluated, and reported in alignment with World Bank standards and the project’s results framework. The role will also contribute to strengthening institutional capacity for M&E within the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and beneficiary agencies, with a particular focus on stakeholder engagement and gender-responsive monitoring.  Minimum (Mandatory) Qualifications:  Education:  Master's degree in economics, Public Policy, Statistics, Social Sciences, Business Administration, or related fields.  Professional Experience:  General Experience: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public sector or donor-funded development projects.  Specific M&E Experience: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public sector or donor-funded development projects, with experience with projects financed by international financial institutions (ex: World Bank, EBRD, KfW, EIB, etc.) or development agencies (UN, GIZ, etc.) considered as an advantage.   Cross-Cutting Tracking: Proven track record in tracking Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) metrics, Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GM), gender targets, and citizen engagement indicators.    Additional (Desired) qualifications:  Methodological Expertise: Technical knowledge of Time Release Studies (TRS), WCO Data Models, Global Quality Infrastructure Index (GQII) methodologies, or transport sector performance metrics is an advantage.  Fiduciary Systems: Familiarity with World Bank IPF reporting is an advantage.  Advanced proficiency in statistical and data management software (e.g., SPSS, Stata, Power BI, Excel, or R).  Languages & Technical Skills:  Fluency in Albanian and English is required; English proficiency will be assessed against proof of certificates received (TOEFL, IELTS, etc), and/or documented work experience in an international or English-speaking setting and/or reference to English language proficiency in a reference letter.  Duration of the Assignment  Initial 12-month full- time contract, with the possibility of extension for the full projects' duration (3–5 years) subject to satisfactory annual performance evaluation and project requirements. The engagement is expected to continue until the closing dates of the FinDev Project in June 2030 and the WBTTFP Project in December 2031, including any extensions approved by the World Bank. The contract shall include a six-month probationary period. Continuation and renewal shall be subject to satisfactory performance, based on a written evaluation prepared by the Head of PIU and endorsed by the Director of the Department of Financing.  Application Procedure  All interested applicants shall submit the following documents:  Curriculum Vitae (CV);  Letter of interest (500 words maximum)  Copies of relevant certificates and diplomas;  At least one (1) and up to three (3) reference letters from previous employers or clients, including official contact details (email and telephone number), or other documentary evidence demonstrating the required experience, such as contract award letters, certificates of completion, employer confirmations, service certificates, or similar references.    Selection Process  Experienced and qualified individuals shall be selected in accordance with the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated September 2023, through an open competitive selection process.  Evaluation Criteria:  General Experience                     (60 Points)   Specific M&E Experience           (40 Points)  Interested Individual Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours: 08:00 - 16:00 hrs. (Monday to Friday)  Expression of interest including a CV and a Motivation Letter must be submitted to fsdp.info@rks-gov.net  by November 12, 2026, at 16:00 hrs.  Ministry of Finance  Contact person: Agon Hysaj, Procurement Specialist  Address: Government Building, 12th Floor, Square “Mother Theresa “-10000, Pristina,  Telephone Number: +383 38 200 34 373  E-mail: fsdp.info@rks-gov.net  To download the ToR please click the link below:  https://mf.rks-gov.net/desk/content/media/088fec3d-4d27-4f60-9f93-ce61dafd9778.pdf

postings.text: Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication   Terms of Reference   for   Project Manager   Micro Small Medium Enterprises (MSME) and Related Technical Assistance World Bank / NRPB SPEAR Project – Sint Maarten                           Background and context Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) constitute approximately 95% of all businesses in Sint Maarten and form the backbone of employment, entrepreneurship, and economic resilience. Recognizing their central role, the Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication (MinTEATT), through the Department of Economy, Transport and Telecommunication (ETT), is undertaking a comprehensive update of four (4) interrelated MSME-related policies, and the MSME institutional strengthening support programs. These two projects are being implemented under The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project, funded by the Government of the Netherlands through the Sint Maarten Reconstruction, Recovery, and Resilience Trust Fund (TF) administered through the World Bank and implemented through the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)[1].   The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project is a strategic initiative led by the Government of Sint Maarten and the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB), with support from the Sint Maarten Trust Fund. It aims to enhance the operational effectiveness of recovery efforts and build long-term institutional resilience. The Trust Fund is governed by a tripartite Steering Committee composed of representatives from Sint Maarten, the Netherlands, and the World Bank, which allocates resources to short-, medium-and long-term recovery and capacity-building initiatives.  SPEAR has the following objectives: Enhance the operational capacity and effectiveness of the National Recovery Program Bureau, and Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Government of Sint Maarten to ensure sustainability of investments. Scope of Work This task falls within the second component of SPEAR. A Policy Consultant or firm is engaged to lead the development of four (4) policy documents: These policies form the foundation of Sint Maarten’s MSME business environment. Updating these policies is essential to reflect the current realities, economic conditions, and evolving dynamics of the local business climate—while also anticipating future needs. At the heart of these policy updates is the goal of fostering a supportive, enabling environment in which entrepreneurs and businesses can thrive and operate efficiently. These revisions aim to strike a thoughtful balance between encouraging economic activity and safeguarding the quality of life, ensuring that Sint Maarten remains a safe, vibrant, and sustainable place to live, work, and do business. The policies are: The National MSME Policy The Investment and Diversification Policy The Residential Economic Policy (REP) The Beach and Vending Policy The policy revisions are intended to align and update these policies to reflect current day realities on Island. The update is expected to be informed by data-driven strategies including the proposed World Bank Enterprise Survey[2]. Such data along with the revised policy documents are essential to sustaining progress and achieving inclusive economic growth in the vital Medium Micro and Small Enterprise (MSME) sector in Sint Maarten.  Therefore, the updates, will be critical to ensure alignment between these operational aspects, policy development, MinTEATT priorities, and overall GoSXM priorities. In parallel to the policy revisions, MinTEATT has requested technical assistance from the ongoing Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the same Trust Fund, to support the execution of the operational aspects of MSME programs. This assistance focuses on institutional strengthening of MSME related institutions including the Sint Maarten Entrepreneurship Development Center (SEDC) and the Chamber of Commerce (COCI). The MSME support areas are:     Governance and Oversight Framework: The objective is to strengthen the Ministry’s oversight and governance of MSME support Monitoring and Evaluation’ (M&E) framework: Development of an M&E framework for MSME support programs. Standard Operating procedures (SOPs): Establish SOPs for MSME support programs in key aspects to include basic business training, one-on-one business advisory, and business coaching. Funding mechanisms for MSME support programs. Terms of reference for these activities are being developed. Role of the Project Manager The Project Manager will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the SPEAR Project policy development and the ESP MSME institutional strengthening support programs components. This responsibility includes coordinating with the Policy Consultant and other Consultants hired through ESP, managing project workflow, coordinating with Min TEATT/ETT, facilitating stakeholder engagement and ensuring compliance with all project requirements.   The Project Manager will also be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day execution of the project process; maintaining project timelines; ensuring compliance with Government of Sint Maarten requirements; and facilitating the successful delivery of all project outputs. In this role, the project manager shall organize and supervise the identification, formulation, approval, implementation and completion of all activities under the component and liaise with the Project Implementation Unit at the Ministry of Finance (SPEAR) and National Recovery Program Bureau (ESP). Functional responsibilities for the role include: Project Management and Coordination Communication with Relevant Stakeholders Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation Oversight and Quality Management Under the supervision of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for overall project coordination and administrative oversight, and of the Ministry of TEATT, through ETT, for policy direction and substantive technical oversight, the Project Manager is expected to perform the following tasks. ETT will guide the policy content, review and validate project outputs, and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s priorities, with final policy approval remaining with the competent authorities: Project Management and Coordination Oversee the execution of the policy development update process and the development of MSME Support Programs ensuring that activities, deliverables and timelines across both workstreams progress in line with approved plans Coordinate with Policy Consultants to monitor the project’s progress, address challenges, and ensure alignment with project objectives and timelines. Facilitate and participate in regular project meetings with MinTEATT/ETT, NRPB, Ministry of Finance, the Policy Consultant and other relevant stakeholders. Work directly with project counterparts and relevant stakeholders to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. This will involve coordinating with departments within the Government as well as external counterparts, including NRPB, to ensure all aspects of each project are compatible and to clarify specific requirements of each project. Ensure project milestones are achieved on-time and that deliverables meet the required quality standards. Identify and manage project risks, developing mitigation strategies as needed. Manage the project budget, track expenditures and ensure allocated resources are used in accordance with approved plans. Participate as a member of the bid evaluation team during the contracting process. Support the selection of new project staff or consultants as needed. Support the revision process of operational project documents (e.g., project operations manual, procurement plan, and environmental and social management plan), as needed. Participate and/or lead technical meetings with agency counterparts and project participant Regularly supervise and report on project execution progress and budget performance Assist with the preparation of progress reports and actionable information as required by Government to support its reporting commitments to the Council of Ministers, the Trust Fund Steering Committee and the World Bank, as needed. Ensure timely reporting, briefing notes, and updates to the Ministry of Finance and other governing bodies as required. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) REPUBLIC OF TAJIKISTAN TAJIKISTAN DIGITAL FOUNDATIONS PROJECT Date: November 9, 2026 Assignment Title:  Consultancy Service for Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals Reference No .: PIC-TDFP-CS-3 State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan is implementing Tajikistan Digital Foundation Project (thereafter referred to as Project) co-financed by the World Bank and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC). The total cost of the project is US$46.2 million, of which the IDA grant is $30M, SDC Trust fund is $14.8M and GoTJ share is $1.4M. and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals   The consultant will have to perform the following tasks: Tasks shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Program Design and Preparation Develop a time-bound implementation plan which includes target numbers of trainees to be trained, and description of monitoring mechanisms of the training program execution and quality of training offered Develop modular digital skills training programs or use off the shelf courses on AI, Cloud, Network, System Administration and Cybersecurity aligned with labor market relevance in Tajikistan and addressing language requirements, inclusivity considerations, infrastructure constraints, and applicability of skills. Develop of complementary business soft skills training modules , that will be delivered in Russian and Tajik to enhance participants’ readiness for employment and further skills development. Ensure blended and online delivery modalities through the Platform for Educational Needs, describing delivery options, sequencing, and implementation considerations to support regional equity of access and sustainability beyond the project period. Develop an inclusive outreach and participant selection framework, including eligibility criteria and targeting approaches, to support the participation of youth, NEET populations, women, persons with disabilities, and beneficiaries in line with the inclusion targets defined in the Objective section. Develop and adapt training curricula and learning materials in Russian, English, and/or Tajik, leveraging and contextualizing existing resources available in Tajikistan and identifying gaps where supplementary materials may be required. Develop and implement employer engagement mechanisms to facilitate internships and job matching for the course beneficiaries. The Consultant shall track employment outcomes for at least six (6) months following graduation. Collaborate with other training centers to achieve the objectives of this assignment. Develop an implementation plan with milestones, deliverables, and performance indicators. Coordinate with the PIC EOP and relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment with Component 2 objectives. Transfer full documentation, training materials (free of copyrights) to PIC EOP upon contract completion.   Duration The total duration of the contract is 24 months .   The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment  can be found at the following website: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1avZ1BiaGMRme-LLyzJU5MgukzT2-brdg/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=101229496586602350179&rtpof=true&sd=true The State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (i) At least 3 years of experience in designing and delivering educational programs. (ii) Demonstrated experience in designing and implementation managing large-scale digital skills and workforce development programs of at least 800–1000 participants within a single project or across multiple concurrent projects. (iii) Minimum 2 successfully completed contracts in digital skills and workforce development training within the past 3 years, with a total contract value of not less than USD 150,000. (iv) Demonstrated experience in integrating advanced technical digital skills and employability or soft skills components within program design frameworks, aligned with labor market relevance and contextual constraints (v) Demonstrated ability to engage and coordinate with public and private sector institutions, and stakeholders, training or education providers in the context of advanced digital skills or workforce development initiatives. The consultancy is expected to be completed within two (2) months from the start date of services, which is considered to be the time required to complete these tasks. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Georgia Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project No: P173975 Loan No. 9239-GE Assignment Title: Procurement Manager Reference No. GE-GEDC-CS-IC-48   Introduction JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank (WB) intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services of Procurement Manager (National Consultant). The Project Development Objective for the Relief and Recovery for MSME operation is to provide relief to MSMEs and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance.   Project Description The Project is being implemented nationwide and consist of four components: Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading Component 3 – Project management and monitoring Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. The component will support the expansion of the following financial instruments implemented by GEDC: (a) grants for MSMEs through GEDC’s Micro and Small Entrepreneurship Support Program, (b) co-financing of interest payments through GEDC’s Produce in Georgia Program, and (c) partial credit guarantees (PCGs). The component will also provide non-financial support in the form of training and technical assistance to help firms adjust to new conditions, improve their business skills, and increase their resilience. Sub-component 1.1 provide micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms. Sub-component 1.2 co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs). Sub-component 1.3 provide partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs. Sub-component 1.4 provide technical assistance for COVID-proofing and digitalization of MSMEs. Scope of Work Procurement Manager / Individual Consultant shall assist the GEDC in all procurement activities related to implementation of WB financed MSMEs Project in accordance with the New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025. This includes not only procurement activities where GEDC is the beneficiary of the loan proceeds, but also the activities where GEDC is acting as a procuring agency for other agencies, which are final beneficiaries (GEDC’s fiduciary responsibilities are defined in the Loan Agreement). Anticipated Procurement Activities The remaining procurement activities under the Project may include, but are not limited to: Event Organization Services: Procurement of services related to the organization and technical support of business events and other similar activities under the Project. Consulting Services: Procurement of consulting services for feasibility studies, assessments, and other analytical activities supporting the Project's objectives. The scope and selection methods of these activities will be determined based on the Project's needs and the approved Procurement Plan, in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations. Key Responsibilities In order to achieve the objective of this contract, the Procurement Manager / Individual Consultant shall: Lead the process of preparation of Project Procurement Plan, its update on a regular basis in close partnership with the GEDC in alignment with the WB rules and regulations; Administer the entire process for the procurement cycle, ensuring compliance with the WB regulations:  selection of the appropriate procurement methods, preparation of the Terms of References, cost estimates, Requests for Expression of Interest, Requests for Quotations/Bids/Proposals, evaluation reports, participation in contracts’ negotiations and awards, as well as in contracts’ execution, getting the WB approvals, as appropriate. Lead contract administration, including framework agreements and managing call-off contracts in each framework agreement.   Keep all relevant procurement documentation on file in an orderly manner and make it available for the authorized national inspecting agencies, auditors, and the WB upon request; Enter all up-to-date procurement related information, both post and prior review, in STEP; Prepare quarterly and annual procurement reports including contract monitoring and management; Cooperate with the GEDC for regular preparation of Project Management/Financial Reports, as part of the WB project and financial reporting requirements; Participate in contract management, monitoring and supervision, including but not limited to ensuring timely submission of all deliverables specified under the contract. Perform other procurement related tasks as required.   Qualification and experience University-level degree in business administration, finance, law, or related discipline; 5 (Five) years of practical experience as a procurement or contract specialist; At least 3 (three) years of working experience in procurement and contract management of projects funded by the WB and/or other International Financial Institutions (IFIs); Knowledge of the World Bank procurement regulations, local taxation, banking and other pertinent regulations affecting national and international procurement; Experience with World Bank Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) portal; Proven teamwork skills; Superior verbal and writing communication skills in Georgian; Strong verbal, reading and writing skills in English; Good negotiating skills; Proficiency in various software under OS Windows (MS Office, Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, Adobe). Reporting The Individual Consultant shall directly report to the Project Manager. Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client The Client shall provide office area and facilities, office equipment and communication necessary to carry out the services. The Client shall also provide all necessary information and documents for that purposes. Duration The assignment will be time-based, continuing until the Project’s closing date of June 30, 2027. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14 “Conflict of Interest” of the World Bank’s Guidelines: New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The Consultant shall not receive any remuneration in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the client under the contract. The contract shall include provisions limiting future engagement of the consultant for other services resulting from or directly related to the firm’s consulting services in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the Guidelines. An individual consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in World Bank’s Guidelines: New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025. “Selection of Individual Consultants”. Interested consultants may obtain further information by email: hr@gedc.ge CVs of candidates in English language must be submitted electronically to the address below not later than 23 November, 2026 E-mail To: hr@gedc.ge Please include the title of the announced position in subject line of the email.

postings.text: Request for Expressions of Interest                                                             (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)                                                                                      Finance Officer Item Details Project Name Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project Project Number and Website P502591 https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P502591  Activity and Reference Number (STEP) Finance Officer: FJ-PIFS-575741-CS-INDV Implementing Agency Names Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat Country FIJI   The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) and eight Pacific Island member countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) have received financing (grants and credits) from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) towards the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project (the Project) and will apply part of these proceeds to the contract below for Consulting Services. The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is seeking a qualified and experienced national Finance Officer (FO) to support the financial management and administration of the Project, including financial reporting, budget monitoring, maintenance of financial records, and compliance with World Bank and PIFS requirements. The Finance Officer will report to the Project Coordinator and will work closely with the Financial Management Specialist on a daily basis and with other PIFS staff, as relevant. This is a full-time work assignment at the PMU housed within the PIFS office in Suva. In line with the project timeline, the engagement will initially be for two (2) years with an extension of a further two years (based on consultant's performance evaluations and project needs) thereafter, until 2030. Under the overall direction of the Project Coordinator and the direct supervision of the Financial Management Specialist, the Finance Officer will support the financial management and administration of the Project, including: Processing and recording financial transactions. Maintaining financial records and supporting documentation. Monitoring project budgets and expenditures. Supporting the preparation of financial reports, withdrawal applications, and other financial documentation. Coordinating project payments and maintaining financial registers. Supporting audits, reconciliations, and compliance activities. Maintaining project financial filing systems. Providing financial and administrative support to project activities, workshops, meetings, and missions. Undertaking other finance-related duties as assigned.   Applicants will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Mandatory Criteria Mandatory Criteria Description Education A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, or a related field from a recognized institution. Experience A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in finance, accounting, bookkeeping, financial administration, or financial management, including experience supporting donor-funded, government-funded, regional, or development partner-funded projects. Eligibility to Work in Fiji The applicant must have the legal right to live and work in Fiji at the time of application and throughout the duration of the assignment. Applicants should clearly state their citizenship, residency, or work authorization status in their application.   Evaluated Criteria Evaluated Criteria Points Experience supporting financial management of donor-funded or development projects, including preparation of financial reports and supporting documentation. 35 Demonstrated experience using accounting software such as MYOB, QuickBooks, Sage, Peachtree, or similar financial management systems. 25 Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial data analysis, reconciliation, and reporting. 20 Experience supporting audits, compliance reviews, and maintenance of financial records and registers. 10 Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in diverse teams and manage multiple priorities with strong attention to detail. 10 Total 100   Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS), on behalf of the participating member countries, now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae and a cover letter with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process. The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached and provides details of the scope of services required along with the expected deliverables. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09.00 to 17.00 hrs Fiji Time.   Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) no later than Monday, 23 November 2026, 17:00 hrs (Fiji Time). Address for Enquiries and Submission of EOIs Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat Attn: Deepak Naicker, Procurement Officer Private Mail Bag, Suva PO Box 856, Suva, Fiji Tel: 679-3312600 E-mail: cbrprocurement@forumsec.org    For escalation matters only: Ajay Jagannath, Project Coordinator E-mail: ajayj@forumsec.org -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------                                                            TERMS OF REFERENCE                              CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION                                                             FINANCE OFFICER   Project Overview Project Name Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project Activity Reference Number (STEP) FJ-PIFS-575741-CS-INDV Position Title Finance Officer Location of Role The position will be based at the Project PMU Office in PIFS, Suva, Fiji with possible travel to participating countries. Eligibility Must have the legal right to live and work in Fiji Implementing Agency Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) https://forumsec.org Duration of Assignment An initial two-year contract, with the possibility of a further two-year extension based on satisfactory performance, or until the Project's closing date of August 2030, whichever is earlier. Agency Description The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members' shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu. The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region. Participating Countries The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Solomon Islands, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu. Overall Project Objective The Project Development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries. Project Length August 2024 to September 2030   Project Background The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) and will act as the Implementing Agency for the regional Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project (the Project), which will enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in Pacific Island Countries (PICs). The PICs covered by the regional project include Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu. Financial systems in PICs are characterized by low levels of financial access and uneven development of national payment systems. Commercial banks dominate the financial sector in all PICs. In several countries, significant portions of the population lack access to basic transaction accounts, limiting their ability to participate in economic activity and access financial services. Correspondent Banking Relationships (CBRs) underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, and humanitarian financial flows. The withdrawal of these relationships presents significant risks to economic development and financial inclusion across the Pacific region. To address these challenges, the World Bank is providing funding to PIFS to implement the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project. The Project includes two components: (i) Temporary Correspondent Banking Services and (ii) Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization. The Project is being implemented by a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) within PIFS. PIFS seeks to recruit a qualified and experienced Finance Officer to support project financial management and administration functions within the PMU. The selection will be undertaken in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable project procedures.   2. postings.text: REPUBLIC OF LIBERIA MINISTRY OF GENDER, CHILDREN, AND SOCIAL PROTECTION Ministerial Complex, Congo Town 1000 Monrovia 10, Liberia, West Africa   REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)   COUNTRY:                  Republic of Liberia   NAME OF PROJECT:  Liberia Women Empowerment Project   PROJECT ID:               P173677                         CREDIT/GRANT No.:  IDA-7168-LR and E0910-LR              ASSIGNMENT:     Consulting Services for the Development, Deployment, Rollout and Post-Deployment Support for a Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) REFERENCE No.:     LR-MOGCSP-546313-CS-CQS The Government of the Republic of Liberia through the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Liberia Women Empowerment Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the Consulting Services for the Development, Deployment, Rollout and Post-Deployment Support of a Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MGCSP)   Objective of the Assignment   The objective of the consultancy is to develop and operationalize an integrated Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) for the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MGCSP) that will enhance the Ministry’s institutional capacity to systematically collect, capture, store, manage, analyze, visualize, and report gender-related data and information. The system is expected to improve the availability, quality, accessibility, timeliness, and use of sex- and gender-disaggregated data to support evidence-based policy and program planning, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, coordination, and decision-making at national and sub-national levels The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (“the Client”) now invites eligible Consultants to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) in providing the Services. Have experience implementing at least 2 assignments for government institutions, donor-funded, or development partner-financed programs, preferably in the social, gender, GBV, or related sectors. Experience in West Africa is an advantage. Demonstrated experience in delivering end-to-end digital solutions, including system design, development, integration, deployment, training, documentation, and postdeployment support. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT) Senior Consultant for VROMI Support to Repair EDMP Procured Equipment The Emergency Debris Management Project Assignment Title: Senior Consultant for VROMI Support to Repair EDMP Procured Equipment Credit/Loan no.: TF-B9747 Reference no.: SX-NRPB-574596-CS-INDV The Government of Sint Maarten has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Emergency Debris Management Project (EDMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The objective of the assignment is to engage a Senior Consultant to coordinate, manage and finalize the repair of heavy equipment procured under the Emergency Debris Management Project (EDMP), restoring operational capacity for the solid waste management division of the Ministry of Public Housing, Spatial Planning, Environment and Infrastructure (VROMI). The Consultant will review technical repair scopes, validate supplier quotations, track warranties, review invoices, coordinate shipments and confirm acceptance testing. The assignment will also strengthen VROMI’s capacity for sustainable maintenance and asset management through practical procedures, preventive maintenance schedules, an Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Plan, operational protocols and staff capacity building. The Consultant will deliver the following: Inception report and work plan, including an equipment assessment, prioritized repair coordination plan and stakeholder communication strategy. Coordination of equipment repairs, including an equipment inventory, review of maintenance records and supplier assessments, repair and shipment tracking, warranty monitoring, invoicing, handover and acceptance testing, with quarterly progress reporting. A comprehensive asset management program, including a review of existing procedures and technical capacity, prioritized recommendations, a preventive maintenance schedule and budget linked to the financial framework, an O&M Plan, operational protocols, standard operating procedures and a staff training session. Final equipment repair coordination and asset management report, including financial reconciliation, final recommendations and a handover note for VROMI. Final assignment report covering achievements, lessons learned, challenges and recommendations.   The assignment is expected to last six months, including approximately 60 cumulative days in Sint Maarten through periodic missions, with remaining activities performed remotely. Indicative milestones are Week 1 for inception, quarterly progress reports, Week 20 for the final equipment repair coordination and asset management report, and Week 22 for the final assignment report. The Consultant will report to the EDMP Project Manager, coordinate directly with VROMI and remain available until repair services are finalized.   Activities shall comply with applicable environmental, safety and health requirements and good international industry practice.   The National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB) now invites eligible consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The selection criteria are:   · An advanced degree in Environmental Engineering, Waste Management, Environmental Policy, Public Administration, Civil Engineering or a related discipline. · At least 10 years of professional experience in the operation and maintenance of technical equipment or infrastructure assets. · Experience preparing O&M manuals, standard operating procedures and maintenance documentation · Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple actors. · National experience working with the Government and/or its agencies. · Demonstrated experience independently conducting activities in a broad context and implementing capacity-building initiatives. · Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation, analytical and report-writing skills.   Other skills: · Experience with World Bank or other multilateral donor-funded projects is an advantage · Proficiency in Dutch is an advantage, and conversational Spanish is an asset.   Applicants are free to choose a format for their Expression of Interest. At this stage, Consultants are expected to provide: 1. postings.text: Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services – Firms Selection) Country: IGAD Secretariat Name of project:   Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa         Project No.:     P178566 Grant No.:       IDA-E0820 Assignment Title: Study to Develop Cross-Border Digital Soil for a Pilot Area in the IGAD Region, Including Digital Soil Property Maps, and Uncertainty Layers  Reference/Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567697-CS-CQS 1.    The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 2.    The consulting services (“the Services”) includes i) The review of cross border areas in the IGAD region that have existing or planned IGAD Ground Water Information System (GWIS) in place, and identify the most suitable pilot area based on agreed technical, institutional and data-availability criteria. ii) To conduct soil field sampling, laboratory analysis, and quality controlled data compilation one cross border pilot area with a Ground Water Information System in place. iii)To generate updated, harmonized and decision-ready digital soil maps for the selected cross-border pilot area, including key soil properties, soil constraints, land-suitability information and uncertainty estimates. iv)To compile and harmonise existing soil, water, land-use, climate, terrain and remote-sensing datasets relevant to the selected pilot area and ensure compatibility with IGAD’s GeoNode repository, dashboards, DACAS and related decision-support tools. v)To develop a scalable workflow, data standard and implementation approach that can later be extended to other IGAD cross-border clusters. The assignment is expected to take 175 Calendar Days from the date of contract commencement.  3.    The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://igad.int/consultancies  or can be obtained at the address given below. 4.    The The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The shortlisting criteria: i)    The firm should have at least 10 years of experience in conducting soil mapping (soil field sampling, laboratory analysis, and quality controlled data compliation; and generation of harmonised and decision-ready digital soil maps and other tasks in line with the objectives of the assignment) ii)    Satisfactory completion of three similar assignments in the past 10 years  iii)    Availability of the below key experts with the required profiles as detailed in the Terms of Reference  (i) Team Leader: Overall lead of the assignment,(ii) Soil Scientist: Conducts soil characterization, fertility assessment, and land capability evaluation, (iii) Digital Soil Mapping Specialist: Develops digital soil maps using spatial modeling, machine learning, and geostatistics, (iv) GIS and Remote Sensing Specialist: Processes satellite imagery, spatial data, and develops geospatial products, (vi) Agronomist/Crop Production Specialist: Interprets soil information into crop-specific management recommendations. At the proposal stage, the consulting firm must provide a staffing plan with names, roles, and CVs for the core project team as part of the proposal. 5.    The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and revised Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 6.    Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 7.    A Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant`s Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. 8.    Further information can be obtained at the address below during the following office hours 0900 and 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours East African Time (EAT) and public holidays. Expression of interest shall be sent by e-mail to the address below by 18/11/2026 at 1700hours EAT. to:  procurement@igad.int  with copy to hassan.salah@igad.int  and quote the Assignment title and Contract No (Study to Develop Cross-Border Digital Soil for a Pilot Area in the IGAD Region, Including Digital Soil Property Maps, and Uncertainty Layers, Reference/Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567697-CS-CQS) in the subject row.

postings.text: AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR L 'EVALUATION DE L'USAGE DU SYSTEME FID                           Pays  : République du Bénin   Nom du projet  : Projet d’Identification Unique pour l’Intégration Régionale et l’Inclusion en Afrique de l’Ouest (WURI-BÉNIN)   Numéro du Don  : Don N° D610-BJ / Crédit IDA N°6611-BJ   Référence : BJ-WURI - BENIN-565381-CS-CQS du ………………………   Intitulé de la Mission : AVIS À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR L'ÉVALUATION DE L'USAGE DU SYSTÈME FID N° de référence : BJ-WURI - BENIN-565381-CS-CQS du…………………   Le Gouvernement de la République du Bénin a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet d’identification unique pour l’intégration et l’inclusion en Afrique de l’Ouest (WURI) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultants.  La mission du consultant (cabinet) consistera à apprécier, de manière objective et indépendante, le niveau, la qualité et les effets de l'usage du système d'identification unique fID mis en place dans le cadre du Projet WURI Bénin, d'en identifier les facteurs de réussite et les freins, et de formuler des recommandations opérationnelles pour intensifier, sécuriser et pérenniser cet usage, y compris à travers un dispositif de supervision continue de l'utilisation des systèmes d'identification. De façon spécifique, il s’agira de : dresser la cartographie des cas d'usage effectifs et potentiels du fID, ainsi que celle des entités utilisatrices publiques et privées connectées au système ; mesurer l'usage effectif de l'identifiant unique par les populations enrôlées pour l'accès aux services analyser l'adoption du système d'identification par les fournisseurs de services (administrations, banques, opérateurs de téléphonie mobile, structures sanitaires, établissements scolaires, etc.) et le niveau d'intégration/interopérabilité avec leurs systèmes ; identifier les facteurs facilitateurs et les obstacles (techniques, socioculturels, économiques, liés au genre, à l'accessibilité, à la connaissance) à l'usage du système d'identification, notamment pour les groupes vulnérables (femmes, personnes en situation de handicap, populations rurales, personnes déplacées, etc.) ; évaluer la perception et le niveau de confiance des usagers vis-à-vis du système (protection des données personnelles, sécurité, fiabilité) ; apprécier la contribution du système d'identification à l'inclusion sociale, financière et économique des bénéficiaires ; formuler des recommandations opérationnelles et stratégiques pour améliorer le taux d'usage du système et sécuriser l'atteinte des indicateurs de résultats du Projet. La durée de réalisation de la mission sera de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours à partir de la date de notification de service, y compris les délais de validation et de livraison du rapport final. Le Coordonnateur National du Projet WURI BENIN, représentant l’Autorité Contractante, par la présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt, invite les consultants (cabinets) admissibles à présenter leur candidature pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. A ce titre, les agences intéressées doivent fournir les informations indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter les services. Le dossier de candidature comprendra : Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt précisant la mission ; Le registre de commerce ou tout autre document similaire pouvant prouver les années d’exercices et domaines d’activité ; Les références techniques accompagnées des preuves (attestation de bonne fin d’exécution ou procès-verbaux de réceptions). Le cabinet sera sélectionné par la méthode de « Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications de Consultant (QC) » décrite au paragraphe 7.11 du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale en date de septembre 2025. A l’issue de l’évaluation des références, le consultant ayant présenté le meilleur niveau de qualification et d’expériences en rapport avec la mission, sera invité à soumettre des propositions technique et financière puis à négocier le contrat. L’attention des agences intéressées est attirée sur les paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale, qui décrivent la politique de la Banque en matière de conflits d’intérêts. Les cabinets peuvent s’associer avec d’autres cabinets sous forme de groupement de firmes ou d’un accord de sous-traitance en vue du renforcement de leurs qualifications. Dans le cas d’un Groupement, tous les partenaires du Groupement seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat. Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française en quatre (04) exemplaires (1 original et 3 copies plus une version scannée sur clé USB), portant la mention « MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR L 'EVALUATION DE L'USAGE DU SYSTEME FID  » doivent être déposées au plus tard le ……………… 2026 à 10 heures 00 minute (heure de Cotonou) à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : Secrétariat du Projet WURI, sis dans la rue de Golden Tulip à 150 m de la plage Obama Beach, Cotonou, République du Bénin, téléphone : +229 01 21 60 29 50/ 01 91 51 10 10, email : contact@wuri-benin.org Et l’ouverture des plis aura lieu à la même adresse, le même jour, soit le ……………… 2026 à 10 heures 30 minute (heure de Cotonou).  Les consultants peuvent avoir plus d’informations au Secrétariat de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet WURI BENIN ayant son siège à Cotonou, rue de Golden Tulip, 150 m de la plage Obama Beach Tél : 91 51 10 10, e-mail : contact@wuri-benin.org tous les jours ouvrables de 08 heures à 12 heures 30 minutes et de 14 heures 00 à 17 heures 30 minutes . Les critères d’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt sont présentés dans le tableau ci-dessous : N° Critères/Sous-critères Note sur 100 1 Qualifications générales du consultant 30 1.1 Être un cabinet ou groupement de cabinets ou bureau d'études spécialisé en évaluation de politiques, programmes et projets de développement et le justifier par l’original ou la copie légalisée du registre de commerce 05 1.2 Disposer d’une expérience avérée dans le domaine de l'identification numérique, ou des services publics numériques ou de la gouvernance des données ou d’une plateforme d'authentification / d'interopérabilité et la justifier par l’original ou la copie légalisée de l’attestation de bonne fin d’exécution 10 1.3 Justifier par des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution (original ou copie légalisée) d’au moins cinq (05) années d’expérience dans la conduite d'études ou d'évaluations de projets, de document de stratégie ou de politique publique 3x5=15 2 Expériences spécifiques du Consultant 65 2.1 Justifier par des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution, d’au moins trois (03) missions similaires d'évaluation, d'étude d'usage ou d'audit fonctionnel de systèmes numériques ou de projets de développement financés par des bailleurs 15x3=45 2.2 Justifier par une attestation de bonne fin d’exécution, de connaissances et d'expérience avérées en matière de gouvernance et de protection des données à caractère personnel 20 3 Présentation du dossier 5 3.1 Dossier bien lisible, bien relié, paginé de façon continue, avec présentant un sommaire et les références techniques classées selon chaque rubrique 5   TOTAL 100 NB  : En cas d’égalité du nombre total de points, la priorité sera accordée au cabinet ou au groupement de cabinets justifiant du plus grand nombre de références spécifiques similaires d'évaluation, d'étude d'usage ou d'audit fonctionnel de systèmes numériques ou de projets de développement financés par des bailleurs (telles q ue définies au point 2.1 de la grille)  ; En cas de groupement, au moins un des consultants doit être spécialisé en évaluation de politiques, programmes et projets de développement ; Les dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt doivent être reliés, paginés de manière continue, et les références techniques classées selon l’ordre de présentation de la grille d’évaluation.                                                                   Cotonou, le ………………………                                                                                                                  Dr Jean AHOL

Number : B STRONG/DDM/S-05 Country of Delivery : Bangladesh   02. The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh  has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Bangladesh Sustainable Recovery, Emergency Preparedness and Response Project (B-STRONG) (DDM Part) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.   03. The consulting services (“the Services”) aims to secure the services of a Consultancy Firm/NGO (hereto referred to as the “Consultant”) to carry out a series of third-party assessments (spot-checks and evaluation) of the EGPP+ program under the B-STRONG (DDM Part) Project for a period up to June 2029. Such third parties will serve as an independent feedback mechanism of  program inputs, outputs and performance and is a key component of effective program  implementation. Incorporating such assessments on a regular and timely basis will play a major role  in ensuring the integrity of the public financial management and sustain a robust accountability  framework by enhancing the flow of information to the citizens and feedback from citizens to the  decision-makers. The service will be expected to start from February 2027 and the tentative duration of the consulting services to be provided by EGPP+ Third Party Spot Monitoring & Evaluation is up to 30 June 2029, as per approved DPP.   Notable, the EGPP+ will be implemented over 4 Financial Years (FY), i.e., FY: 2026-27, FY: 2027-28, FY: 2028-29, and FY: 2029-30 under this Assignment. As the completion date specified in the approved DPP is 30 June 2029, the contract period exist until that date. Subject to approval from the Competent Authority, the period may be extended to 30 June 2030 without any Variation or Modification to this contract. 04. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.ddm.gov.bd 05. The Bangladesh Sustainable Recovery, Emergency Preparedness and Response Project (B-STRONG) (DDM Part)  now invites eligible consulting firms/NGOs (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. 06. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 07. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Moreover, in case of such association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. The Project will seek to produce concrete and tangible results for the Palestinians by enhancing access to high-speed broadband services and increasing access to selected e-services for citizens and businesses. The Project will focus on key points to unleash digital transformation in the Palestinian territories, addressing some of the bilateral challenges that prevent digital transformation from achieving its full potential. It will strengthen the Palestinian territories' digital resilience and the PA's ability to respond to shocks such as COVID-19. The Project is implemented and overseen by the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE), formerly the Ministry of Telecom and Information Technology (MTIT), to support digital transformation and resilience in the West Bank and Gaza. The project has the following four components: Enabling legal and regulatory environment for Digital Economy, mainly institutional development including the development of section Palestinian Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and Trust Service Supervisory Body; legal and regulatory framework; a Quality-of-Service platform; and capacity building. Implementing Digital Infrastructure Solutions for Emergency Response, Recovery and Resilience which includes the development of an emergency response center. Fostering User Centered E-Service Delivery, which includes the establishment of a whole government digital transformation strategy, data infrastructure, support for a digital public platform and prioritization, simplification and digitization of services, the launch of e-services, and implementation of an e-Government Procurement (e-GP) System; and Project Management, which will support the establishment of a Project management unit in MTDE.   The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) was established as an independent regulatory body under Decree-Law No. (37) of 2021 Concerning Telecommunications and Information Technology. Its mandate includes overseeing and developing the Palestinian telecommunications market and implementing policies designed by MTDE. The Project supports the establishment and operationalization of TRA, including capacity building to strengthen its effectiveness, credibility and independence.   MTDE seeks a qualified consulting or specialized training firm to design and deliver a targeted capacity-building program for TRA staff. The program will strengthen core regulatory skills, institutional processes and evidence-based decision-making, drawing on ITU guidance, ITU Global Symposium for Regulators best practices, and regional and international regulatory experience.   The assignment covers the following five training topics, with course content and modalities as detailed in the TOR: Telecom Licensing, Regulatory Compliance and Enforcement (15 trainees): licensing procedures and conditions; compliance monitoring; risk-based inspections; evidence and case management; proportionate enforcement, sanctions and due process. Expert-led applied workshop with practical exercises. Telecom Market Analysis and Competition Regulation (7 trainees): market definition and analysis; significant market power; competition remedies; infrastructure sharing, network access and interconnection; and regulatory case studies. Blended training with practical market analysis exercises. Regulation and Measurement of Telecommunications Quality of Service (QoS) and Quality of Experience (QoE) (7 trainees): regulatory frameworks and standards; network performance indicators; drive testing; measurement, monitoring, data analysis and reporting; and compliance assessment. Specialized training with remote follow-up sessions. Protection of Telecommunications Consumers and Users' Rights (5 trainees): consumer protection frameworks; provider obligations; complaints and dispute resolution; contracts, pricing and billing transparency; investigations, remedies and consumer protection indicators. Practical workshops. National Emergency Telecommunications Planning and Telecom Sector Resilience (15 trainees): emergency governance; critical infrastructure risks; business continuity and disaster recovery; incident coordination and reporting; priority communications and service restoration; supply-chain resilience; and tabletop emergency and cyber scenarios. Multi-stakeholder workshop with practical scenarios.   Assignment deliverables include training delivery; printed/electronic training materials for each trainee, PMU and TRA; course completion certificates for successful participants; and an evaluation report for each course summarizing outcomes and comparing pre- and post-training test results. Detailed training plans and course outlines will be requested at the subsequent proposal stage and are not required with the expression of interest.   Training shall be conducted physically at MTDE labs or the firm's labs, with the course-specific follow-up modalities indicated in the TOR. Arabic is preferred but is not mandatory. Where relevant, professional certification examinations, vouchers, registration and related services may be proposed as optional components with a separate itemized financial offer; TRA may procure all, some or none of these components.   Download Full Tor from Here: TRA-Capacity Building ToR.pdf   The Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE) now invites eligible consulting firms and specialized training centers ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Experience providing training to telecom/ICT regulatory authorities, ministries or comparable public-sector institutions, preferably in the MENA region. Technical and managerial capacity to organize and deliver the program, and a clear understanding of the assignment and approach to its execution.   Expressions of interest should include a firm profile; details of relevant completed assignments, including dates, clients, scope and supporting evidence; and a initial list of proposed trainers and Key Experts, indicating their intended training topics or roles. Trainers and Key Experts will not be evaluated or assigned scores at this stage. No training plan or course outline is required at the expression-of-interest stage.   Interested firms must also answer the following questions in their expressions of interest: What training delivery modality does the firm offer for this assignment: face-to-face, online, or blended? In which language(s) can the firm deliver the training: Arabic, English, or both? Please specify the available language(s) for each training topic.   The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy.
